children.text: yatra tu naiṣā śaṅkā tā dharmārthakāmebhyo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But where this doubt does not arise, homage to <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.
Because they are the subject matter treated in the treatise.
And homage to the teachers who make known their established conventions.
Because of their connection with them.

children.text: prajāpatir hi prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā tāsāṃ sthitinibandhanaṃ trivargasya sādhanam adhyāyānāṃ śatasahasreṇāgre provāca ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created living beings, first expounded, in one hundred thousand chapters, the means of attaining the <s>trivarga</s> (three aims of life), the basis for their continuance.

children.text: tasyaikadeśikaṃ manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo dharmādhikārikaṃ pṛthak cakāra ||
children.translated_text: <s>Manu Svāyaṃbhuva</s> separately composed the portion of that which concerns <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> composed the portion concerning <s>artha</s>.

children.text: mahādevānucaraśca nandī sahasreṇādhyāyānāṃ pṛthak kāmasūtraṃ provāca ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Nandī</s>, attendant of <s>Mahādeva</s>, separately expounded the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> in one thousand chapters.

children.text: tad eva tu pañcabhir adhyāyaśatair auddālakiḥ śvetaketuḥ saṃcikṣepa ||
children.translated_text: That same work <s>Auddālaki Śvetaketu</s> condensed into five hundred chapters.

children.text: tad eva tu punar adhyardhenādhyāyaśatena sādhāraṇasāmprayogikakanyāsaṃprayuktakabhāryādhikārikapāradārikavaiśikaupaniṣadikaḥ saptabhir adhikaraṇair bābhravyaḥ pāñcālaḥ saṃcikṣepa ||
children.translated_text: That same work again <s>Bābhravya Pāñcāla</s> condensed into one hundred and fifty chapters, in seven divisions: the general, sexual union, acquisition of maidens, duties concerning wives, relations with others' wives, courtesans, and the secret teachings.

children.text: tasya ṣaṣṭhaṃ vaiśikam adhikaraṇaṃ pāṭaliputrikāṇāṃ gaṇikānāṃ niyogād dattakaḥ pṛthak cakāra ||
children.translated_text: Of that, at the request of the courtesans of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, <s>Dattaka</s> separately composed the sixth division, concerning courtesans.
In connection with that, <s>Cārāyaṇa</s> separately expounded the general division.
<s>Suvarṇanābha</s> expounded the division on sexual union.
<s>Ghoṭakamukha</s> expounded the division on acquisition of maidens.
<s>Gonardīya</s> expounded the division concerning wives.
<s>Goṇikāputra</s> expounded the division on relations with others' wives.
<s>Kucumāra</s> expounded the secret division.

children.text: evaṃ bahubhir ācāryaistacchāstraṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ praṇītam utsannakalpam abhūt
children.translated_text: Thus, when that treatise had been composed in sections by many teachers, it had nearly disappeared.

children.text: tatra dattakādibhiḥ praṇītānāṃ śāstrāvayavānām ekadeśatvāt mahad iti ca bābhravīyasya duradhyeyatvāt saṃkṣipya sarvam artham alpena granthena kāmasūtram idaṃ praṇītam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because the parts of the treatise composed by <s>Dattaka</s> and the others were only partial, and because the work of <s>Bābhravya</s> was large and difficult to study, this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been composed with the whole subject condensed into a small treatise.
This is the enumeration of its topics and divisions.
The compendium of the treatise.
The attainment of the <s>trivarga</s>.
The enumeration of the sciences.
The conduct of a city gentleman.
Consideration of the work of the lover's assistants and female messengers.
Thus ends the first division, the general division.
Five chapters.
Five topics.
The establishment of sexual union according to measure, time, and disposition.
Special forms of affection.
Considerations on embraces.
Varieties of kisses.
Types of nail and tooth marks.
Methods of biting.
Local forms of courtship.
Kinds of sexual positions.
Varied forms of intercourse.
Methods of striking.
The accompanying beginnings of cries and sighs.
The woman acting as the man.
Ways of approaching the man.
Oral intercourse.
The beginning and conclusion of sexual union.
Special forms of sexual union.
A lovers' quarrel.
Thus ends the second division, concerning sexual union.
Ten chapters.
Seventeen topics.
The procedure for choosing a bride.
The determination of connections.
Winning the confidence of a maiden.
Approaches to a young girl.
Indicating intentions by gestures and expressions.
A single man's courtship.
Turning back one who is to be won over.
The maiden's response to courtship.
The arrangement of marriage.
Thus ends the third division, concerning acquisition of maidens.
Five chapters.
Nine topics.
The conduct of an only wife.
Conduct during the husband's absence.
The conduct of the senior wife among co-wives.
The conduct of the junior wife.
The conduct of a remarried woman.
The conduct of an unfortunate wife.
Matters of the inner apartments.
A man's conduct toward many wives.
Thus ends the fourth division, concerning wives.
Two chapters.
Eight topics.
The establishment of the character and disposition of women and men.
Reasons for estrangement.
Men who are successful with women.
Women who are easily attained without effort.
Reasons for acquaintance.
Courtships.
Testing feelings.
The work of female messengers.
Love for powerful men.
Women of the inner apartments and protected wives.
Thus ends the fifth division, concerning others' wives.
Six chapters.
Ten topics.
Considering who is approachable.
Reasons for visiting.
The method of winning someone back.
Compliance with a lover.
Means of acquiring wealth.
Signs of loss of affection.
Conduct toward one who has lost affection.
Ways of dismissing someone.
Reconciliation after a break.
Special kinds of gain.
Consideration of wealth, loss, consequence, and uncertainty.
And special types of courtesans.
Thus ends the sixth division, concerning courtesans.
Six chapters.
Twelve topics.
Making oneself attractive.
Bringing under one's control.
And aphrodisiac preparations.
Restoring lost passion.
Methods of enlargement.
And various preparations.
Thus ends the seventh division, the secret teachings.
Two chapters.
Six topics.
Thus there are thirty-six chapters.
Sixty-four topics.
Seven divisions.
One thousand two hundred and fifty verses.
Thus ends the compendium of the treatise.
Having stated this summary of it, its detailed exposition will now be given.
For in the world the learned approve speech that is both concise and expansive.

children.text: śatāyur vai puruṣo vibhajya kālam anyonyānubaddhaṃ parasparasyānupaghātakaṃ trivargaṃ seveta ||
children.translated_text: A man whose life span is one hundred years should divide his time and pursue the <s>trivarga</s> in such a way that its members are mutually connected and do not injure one another.
In childhood, he should pursue matters such as the acquisition of knowledge.
And <s>kāma</s> in youth.
In old age, <s>dharma</s> and <s>mokṣa</s>.
Or, because life is impermanent, he should pursue them as occasion permits.
But celibacy should be observed until the acquisition of knowledge is complete.

children.text: alaukikatvād adṛṣṭārthatvād apravṛttānāṃ yajñādīnāṃ śāstrāt pravartanam laukikatvād dṛṣṭārthatvācca pravṛttebhyaśca māṃsabhakṣaṇādibhyaḥ śāstrād eva nivāraṇaṃ dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is the undertaking, on the authority of scripture, of acts such as sacrifices, which are not commonly practiced because they are otherworldly and have unseen results; and likewise the refraining, again on the authority of scripture, from acts such as eating meat, though they are commonly practiced because they are worldly and have visible results.
One should learn that <s>dharma</s> (normative duty) from revelation and from the assembly of those who know <s>dharma</s>.
<s>Artha</s> (material advantage) is the acquisition of learning, land, gold, cattle, grain, goods, equipment, friends, and the like, and the increase of what has been acquired.
One should learn that from the practice of superintendents, from those who know commercial conventions, and from merchants.

children.text: śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇānām ātmasaṃyuktena manasādhiṣṭhitānāṃ sveṣu sveṣu viṣayeṣv ānukūlyataḥ pravṛttiḥ kāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kama</s> is the activity, according to agreeable inclination, of hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell toward their respective objects, when they are presided over by the mind joined with the self.

children.text: sparśaviśeṣaviṣayāt tv asyābhimānikasukhānuviddhā phalavatyarthapratītiḥ prādhānyāt kāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But, because touch has primacy, <s>kama</s> is the fruitful apprehension of an object whose object is a particular touch and which is suffused with the pleasure of self-regard.
One should learn that from the <s>Kamasutra</s> and from the assembly of urbane people.
When these are combined, each preceding one is weightier than the one that follows.
And <s>artha</s> is weightier for a king,
because the course of the world has that as its root,
and also for a courtesan; thus there is the understanding of the threefold aim.
Since <s>dharma</s> is otherworldly, a <s>sastra</s> that expounds it is appropriate;
because success in <s>artha</s> is preceded by means,
knowledge of the means comes from <s>sastra</s>.

children.text: tiryagyoniṣvapi tu svayaṃ pravṛttatvāt kāmasya nityatvācca na śāstreṇa kṛtyam astītyācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But since <s>kama</s> operates by itself even among animals, and since it is constant, there is no need for a <s>sastra</s> in its case, say the teachers.
Since sexual union depends on woman and man together, it requires a means.
And knowledge of that means comes from the <s>Kamasutra</s>, says <s>Vatsyayana</s>.

children.text: tiryagyoniṣu punar anāvṛtatvāt strījāteśca ṛtau yāvadarthaṃ pravṛtter abuddhipūrvakatvācca pravṛttīnām anupāyaḥ pratyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among animals, however, because there is no concealment, because females act as much as needed in season, and because their activities are not preceded by understanding, the impulse has no deliberate means.
One should not practice <s>dharma</s>,
because its fruit is future and uncertain.
For what person, unless foolish, would make what is in his hand pass into another's possession?
A pigeon today is better than a peacock tomorrow.
An assured <s>karsapana</s> is better than a doubtful <s>niska</s>,
so say the <s>Laukayatika</s>s.

children.text: śāstrasyānabhiśaṅkyatvād abhicārānuvyāhārayośca kvacit phaladarśanān nakṣatracandrasūryatārāgrahacakrasya lokārthaṃ buddhipūrvakam iva pravṛtter darśanād varṇāśramācārasthitilakṣaṇatvāc ca lokayātrāyā hastagatasya ca bījasya bhaviṣyataḥ sasyārthe tyāgadarśanāccared dharmān iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>sastra</s> is not to be suspected, because results are sometimes seen from sorcery and imprecation, because the movement of the circle of lunar mansions, moon, sun, stars, and planets is seen as if deliberately undertaken for the sake of the world, because the course of the world is marked by the established conduct of class and life-stage, and because one sees seed held in the hand given up for the sake of a future crop, one should practice acts of <s>dharma</s>, says <s>Vatsyayana</s>.
One should not pursue <s>artha</s>,

children.text: prayatnato 'pi hyete anuṣṭhīyamānā naiva kadācit syuḥ
children.translated_text: for even when these things are undertaken with effort, they may sometimes not come about at all,
and even when they are not undertaken, they may come about by chance.
All that is brought about by time, they say.

children.text: kāla eva hi puruṣān arthānarthayor jayaparājayayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayośca sthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: For time alone places men in advantage and misfortune, victory and defeat, pleasure and pain.
By time <s>Bali</s> was made <s>Indra</s>;
by time he was cast down;

children.text: kāla eva punar apyenaṃ karteti kālakāraṇikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and time itself will make him so again, say the time-causation theorists.
Because all activities are preceded by human effort, a means is the cause.
Even for an object that will necessarily come to be, it is precisely because it is preceded by means;
there is no good for the inactive, says <s>Vatsyayana</s>.
One should not pursue <s>kama</s>,

children.text: dharmārthayoḥ pradhānayor evam anyeṣāṃ ca satāṃ pratyanīkatvāt
children.translated_text: because it is opposed to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, which are principal, and likewise to other good things.

children.text: anarthajanasaṃsargam asadvyavasāyam aśaucam anāyatiṃ caite puruṣasya janayanti ||
children.translated_text: These produce for a man association with harmful people, improper occupation, impurity, and lack of future benefit.

children.text: tathā pramādaṃ lāghavam apratyayam agrāhyatāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Likewise they produce negligence, frivolity, distrustworthiness, and social unacceptability.

children.text: bahavaśca kāmavaśagāḥ sagaṇā eva vinaṣṭāḥ śrūyante ||
children.translated_text: And many who were under the sway of <s>kama</s> are heard to have perished together with their followers.

children.text: yathā dāṇḍakyo nāma bhojaḥ kāmād brāhmaṇakanyām abhimanyamānaḥ sabandhurāṣṭro vinanāśa ||
children.translated_text: For example, the <s>Bhoja</s> named <s>Dandakya</s>, desiring a brahmin girl out of passion, perished together with his kinsmen and kingdom.

children.text: devarājaścāhalyām atibalaśca kīcako draupadīṃ rāvaṇaśca sītām apare cānye ca bahavo dṛśyante kāmavaśagā vinaṣṭā ityarthacintakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too the king of gods with <s>Ahalya</s>, the mighty <s>Kicaka</s> with <s>Draupadi</s>, <s>Ravana</s> with <s>Sita</s>, and many others are seen to have perished under the sway of <s>kama</s>, say those concerned with <s>artha</s>.
Since desires are a cause of bodily maintenance, being of the same nature as food,
and since they are the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>,
one should be aware of the faults, as in other cases.

children.text: na hi bhikṣukāḥ santīti sthālyo nādhiśrīyante
children.translated_text: Cooking pots are not left off the fire because beggars exist;

children.text: na hi mṛgāḥ santīti yavā nopyanta iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: barley is not left unsown because deer exist, says <s>Vatsyayana</s>.
And here there are verses:

children.text: evam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca dharmaṃ copācaran naraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus a man, attending to <s>artha</s>, <s>kama</s>, and <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: ihāmutra ca niḥśalyam atyantaṃ sukham aśnute ||
children.translated_text: enjoys complete happiness, free from trouble, both here and hereafter.

children.text: kiṃ syāt paratretyāśaṅkā kārye yasmin na jāyate
children.translated_text: The disciplined are settled on an act in regard to which no anxiety arises, 'What might happen in the next world?'

children.text: na cārthaghnaṃ sukhaṃ ceti śiṣṭāstatra vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and which is not destructive of <s>artha</s> and is pleasant.

children.text: trivargasādhakaṃ yat syād dvayor ekasya vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever may accomplish the threefold aim, or two aims, or again even one,

children.text: kāryaṃ tad api kurvīta na tv ekārthaṃ dvibādhakam ||
children.translated_text: that act too one should perform, but not one aimed at a single end that obstructs two.
Without obstructing <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, the ancillary sciences, and the proper times, a man should study the <s>Kamasutra</s> and its ancillary sciences.
A woman should study before youth,
and, when given in marriage, according to her husband's intention.

children.text: yoṣitāṃ śāstragrahaṇasyābhāvād anarthakam iha śāstre strīśāsanam ityācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because women do not undertake the study of <s>sastra</s>, instruction of women in this <s>sastra</s> is useless, say the teachers.
But their grasp is of practice,
and practice is preceded by <s>sastra</s>, says <s>Vatsyayana</s>.
That is not only so here.

children.text: sarvatra hi loke katicid eva śāstrajñāḥ
children.translated_text: For everywhere in the world only a few people know <s>sastra</s>,
while practice is the sphere of all people.

children.text: prayogasya ca dūrastham api śāstram eva hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And even when <s>sastra</s> is remote, it is the cause of practice.

children.text: asti vyākaraṇam ityavaiyākaraṇā api yājñikā ūhaṃ kratuṣu prayuñjate ||
children.translated_text: Because grammar exists, even ritualists who are not grammarians employ adaptation in sacrifices.

children.text: asti jyautiṣam iti puṇyāheṣu karma kurvate ||
children.translated_text: Because astrology exists, they perform rites on auspicious days.
Likewise, horse-riders and elephant-riders train horses and elephants even without having mastered the treatise.

children.text: tathāsti rājeti dūrasthā api janapadā na maryādām ativartante tadvad etat ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, because people know that there is a king, even distant provinces do not overstep the boundary; so it is with this matter.

children.text: santyapi khalu śāstraprahatabuddhayo gaṇikā rājaputryo mahāmātraduhitaraśca ||
children.translated_text: Indeed there are courtesans, princesses, and daughters of high officials whose understanding has been sharpened by the śāstra.

children.text: tasmād vaiśvāsikājjanād rahasi prayogāñchāstram ekadeśaṃ vā strī gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a woman should learn the practical applications, and the śāstra or some part of it, from a trusted person in private.
A maiden should practice alone and in secret the sixty-four techniques that depend upon exercise.
For maidens, the teachers are a nurse's daughter who has already had experience of intercourse with a man and who grew up together with her,
or a friend of that same sort, with whom conversation involves no risk,
or a maternal aunt of the same age,
or a trusted old female servant occupying that place,
or a female mendicant formerly associated with her,
and also her sister, because dealings with her are based on confidence.

children.text: gītaṃ vādyaṃ nṛtyaṃ ālekhyaṃ viśeṣakachedyaṃ taṇḍulakusumavalivikārāḥ puṣpāstaraṇaṃ daśanavasanāṅgarāgaḥ maṇibhūmikākarma śayanaracanam udakavādyam udakāghātaḥ citrāśca yogāḥ mālyagrathanavikalpāḥ śekharakāpīḍayojanaṃ nepathyaprayogāḥ karṇapattrabhaṅgāḥ gandhayuktiḥ bhūṣaṇayojanam aindrajālāḥ kaucumārāś ca yogāḥ hastalāghavaṃ vicitraśākayūṣabhakṣyavikārakriyā pānakarasarāgāsavayojanaṃ sūcīvānakarmāṇi sūtrakrīḍā vīṇāḍamarukavādyāni prahelikā pratimālā durvācakayogāḥ pustakavācanaṃ nāṭakākhyāyikādarśanaṃ kāvyasamasyāpūraṇaṃ paṭṭikāvetravānavikalpāḥ takṣakarmāṇi takṣaṇaṃ vāstuvidyā rūpyaratnaparīkṣā dhātuvādaḥ maṇirāgākarajñānaṃ vṛkṣāyurvedayogāḥ meṣakukkuṭalāvakayuddhavidhiḥ śukasārikāpralāpanam utsādane saṃvāhane keśamardane ca kauśalyaṃ akṣaramuṣṭikākathanaṃ mlecchitavikalpāḥ deśabhāṣāvijñānaṃ puṣpaśakaṭikā nimittajñānaṃ yantramātṛkā dhāraṇamātṛkā sampāṭhyaṃ mānasī kāvyakriyā abhidhānakośaḥ chandojñānaṃ kriyākalpaḥ chalitakayogāḥ vastragopanāni dyūtaviśeṣā ākarṣakrīḍā bālakrīḍanakāni vainayikīnāṃ vaijayikīnāṃ vyāyāmikīnāṃ ca vidyānāṃ jñānam iti catuḥṣaṣṭir aṅgavidyāḥ kāmasūtrasyāvayavinyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sixty-four ancillary arts that are component parts of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> are: singing; instrumental music; dancing; painting; cutting decorative marks; arrangements of rice, flowers, and offerings; flower-beds; coloring the teeth, garments, and body; inlaying jeweled floors; arranging beds; playing music with water; splashing water; various techniques; different ways of stringing garlands; arranging crests and head-ornaments; theatrical costuming; folding ear-ornaments; compounding perfumes; arranging ornaments; conjuring tricks; juvenile or playful arts; sleight of hand; preparing varied vegetables, soups, and foods; mixing drinks, juices, scented syrups, and wines; needlework and weaving; thread-games; playing the vīṇā and the ḍamaru; riddles; chain-recitation; techniques for difficult utterances; reading books; seeing plays and stories; completing poetic problems; varieties of plaiting with cloth strips and cane; carpentry; wood-turning; architecture; testing silver and jewels; alchemy; knowledge of jewels, dyes, and mines; applications of tree-science; rules for fights of rams, cocks, and quails; teaching parrots and mynahs to speak; skill in rubbing, massage, and hair-dressing; communicating by finger-signs; forms of secret writing; knowledge of regional languages; flower-carts; omen-knowledge; mechanical diagrams; mnemonic diagrams; recitation in concert; mental composition of poetry; lexicography; knowledge of meters; ritual or artistic procedure; deceptive techniques; concealing garments; special forms of gambling; the game of ākarṣa; children's toys; and knowledge of disciplines relating to training, victory, and physical exercise.
There is also another set of sixty-four called <s>Pāñcālikī</s>.
Having examined its applications, we shall describe them in the section on sexual union,
because <s>kāma</s> consists of that.
A courtesan elevated by these arts, endowed with character, beauty, and virtues,
obtains the title <s>gaṇikā</s> and a place in the public assembly.

children.text: pūjitā sā sadā rājñā guṇavadbhiśca saṃstutā
children.translated_text: Always honored by the king and praised by men of merit,
she becomes sought after, accessible, and an object of attention.
A princess skilled in these techniques, and likewise the daughter of a high official,
brings her husband under her own control, even if he has a thousand women in his inner apartments.

children.text: tathā pativiyoge ca vyasanaṃ dāruṇaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: Likewise, when separated from her husband and fallen into severe misfortune,

children.text: deśāntare api vidyābhiḥ sā sukhenaiva jīvati ||
children.translated_text: even in another country she lives comfortably by means of these arts.
A man skilled in the arts, eloquent and adept at flattery,

children.text: asaṃstuto 'pi nārīṇāṃ cittam āśv eva vindati ||
children.translated_text: quickly wins the minds of women, even though he was previously unknown to them.
Good fortune arises simply from acquiring the arts;
but depending on place and time, their application may or may not be possible.

children.text: gṛhītavidyaḥ pratigrahajayakrayanirveśādhigatair arthair anvayāgatair ubhayair vā gārhasthyam adhigamya nāgarakavṛttaṃ varteta ||
children.translated_text: An educated man, having entered the household state with wealth obtained by gifts, conquest, purchase, service, inheritance, or both means together, should live according to the conduct of a cultivated city-dweller.

children.text: nagare pattane kharvaṭe mahati vā sajjanāśraye sthānam
children.translated_text: His residence should be in a city, a town, a market-village, or a large settlement that is a refuge for good people,
or else wherever travel requires.

children.text: tatra bhavanam āsannodakaṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāvad vibhaktakarmakakṣaṃ dvivāsagṛhaṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: There he should have a house built near water, furnished with a grove of trees, divided into workrooms, and containing two living apartments.

children.text: bāhye ca vāsagṛhe suślakṣṇam ubhayopadhānaṃ madhye vinataṃ śuklottaracchadaṃ śayanīyaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: In the outer living room there should be a fine bed, with pillows at both ends, depressed in the middle, and covered with a white upper coverlet,
and also a second bed.
At its head there should be a place for the grooming brush and a small platform.

children.text: tatra rātriśeṣam anulepanaṃ mālyaṃ sikthakaraṇḍakaṃ saugandhikapuṭikā mātuluṅgatvacastāmbūlāni ca syuḥ
children.translated_text: There should be the ointment left for the end of the night, a garland, a small wax-box, a pouch of perfumes, citron peel, and betel leaves.
On the floor there should be a spittoon.
A vīṇā should hang from an ivory peg.
There should be a painting board,
a box for brushes or wicks,
some book or other,
and garlands of kuraṇṭaka flowers.
Not very far away on the floor there should be a round spread with a cushion,
together with a board for ākarṣa and a gambling board.
Outside it should be cages for pet sporting birds.

children.text: ekānte ca takṣatakṣaṇasthānam anyāsāṃ ca krīḍānām
children.translated_text: In a secluded place there should be a place for carpentry, wood-turning, and other games.
In the tree-garden there should be a well-spread swing or hanging seat, with shade,
and a raised earthen seat with flowers; this is the arrangement of the house.

children.text: sa prātar utthāya kṛtaniyatakṛtyaḥ gṛhītadantadhāvanaḥ mātrayānulepanaṃ dhūpaṃ srajam iti ca gṛhītvā dattvā sikthakam alaktakaṃ ca dṛṣṭvādarśe mukham gṛhītamukhavāsatāmbūlaḥ kāryāṇyanutiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Rising in the morning, having performed his fixed duties and cleaned his teeth, he should take ointment, incense, and a garland in due measure, apply wax and red lac, look at his face in a mirror, take mouth-perfume and betel, and then attend to his affairs.
Bathing is to be done every day.
Rubbing and cleansing is to be done every second day.
The foaming preparation is for every third day.
The āyuṣya treatment is for every fourth day.
The fifth or the tenth [day], according to one's vitality, should not be omitted.
And, regularly, sweat should be removed from the covered armpits.
Meals are to be taken in the forenoon and afternoon.
In the evening, there is the cārāyaṇa meal.
After eating come occupations such as teaching parrots and mynah birds to speak.
There are fights of quails, cocks, and rams,
and various amusements in the arts.
There are activities dependent on the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> (attendant companion), the <s>viṭa</s> (man-about-town), and the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester-companion),
and also lying down by day.
When he has put on his adornment, in the afternoon there are diversions in social gatherings.
At twilight there are musical performances.

children.text: tadante ca prasādhite vāsagṛhe saṃcāritasurabhidhūpe sasahāyasya śayyāyām abhisārikāṇāṃ pratīkṣaṇam dūtīnāṃ preṣaṇam svayaṃ vā gamanam
children.translated_text: After that, in the sleeping chamber, adorned and perfumed with fragrant incense, he waits on the bed with his companion for women coming to a tryst, sends female messengers, or goes himself.

children.text: āgatānāṃ ca manoharair ālāpair upacāraiśca sasahāyasyopakramāḥ
children.translated_text: When they have arrived, he begins with them, together with his companion, by charming conversation and courtesies.

children.text: varṣapramṛṣṭanepathyānāṃ durdinābhisārikāṇāṃ svayam eva punar maṇḍanam mitrajanena vā paricaraṇam ityāhorātrikam ||
children.translated_text: For women coming to a tryst on a rainy day, whose dress has been rubbed and spoiled by the rain, he himself should adorn them again, or have them attended by his friends: this is the day-and-night routine.

children.text: ghaṭānibandhanam goṣṭhīsamavāyaḥ samāpānakam udyānagamanam samasyāḥ krīḍāśca pravartayet
children.translated_text: He should set in motion the forming of festive groups, assemblies for conversation, drinking parties, garden excursions, riddling contests, and games.

children.text: pakṣasya māsasya vā prajñāte ahani sarasvatyā bhavane niyuktānāṃ nityaṃ samājaḥ
children.translated_text: On a known day of the fortnight or the month, there is always an assembly of the appointed persons in the temple of <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Visiting performers should give them a show.

children.text: dvitīye ahani tebhyaḥ pūjā niyataṃ labheran
children.translated_text: On the second day they should regularly receive honor from them.

children.text: tato yathāśraddham eṣāṃ darśanam utsargo vā
children.translated_text: After that, according to inclination, there is attendance at their performance or dismissal of them.
In misfortunes and festivals they should act with one another as having a single common business.
Guests who have joined the association should be honored and received.
This is the rule of the group.

children.text: etena taṃ taṃ devatāviśeṣam uddiśya saṃbhāvitasthitayo ghaṭā vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this are also explained the festive associations whose established customs are directed toward particular deities.

children.text: veśyābhavane sabhāyām anyatamasyodavasite vā samānavidyābuddhiśīlavittavayasāṃ saha veśyābhir anurūpair ālāpair āsanabandho goṣṭhī
children.translated_text: A <s>goṣṭhī</s> (social gathering) is the sitting together, in a courtesan's house, in an assembly hall, or at someone's lodging, of people equal in learning, intelligence, character, wealth, and age, together with courtesans and with suitable conversation.
There, too, they have riddling contests in poetry or in the arts.
In that gathering, brilliant people who are beloved by the world are to be honored.
And those whose affection is equal should be invited.
There are also drinking parties in one another's houses.

There the courtesans should make them drink honey-wine, maireya, surā, and āsava, with various relishes of salt, fruit, greens, vegetables, and bitter, pungent, and sour things, and should drink after them as well.
By this, garden excursions are explained.

children.text: pūrvāhṇa eva svalaṃkṛtāsturagādhirūḍhā veśyābhiḥ saha paricārakānugatā gaccheyuḥ
children.translated_text: In the very forenoon, well adorned and mounted on horses, they should go with courtesans and followed by attendants.

children.text: daivasikīṃ ca yātrāṃ tatrānubhūya kukkuṭayuddhadyūtaiḥ prekṣābhir anukūlaiśca ceṣṭitaiḥ kālaṃ gamayitvā aparāhṇe gṛhītatadudyānopabhogacihnāstathaiva pratyāvrajeyuḥ
children.translated_text: After enjoying the day's outing there, passing the time with cockfights, gambling, spectacles, and suitable amusements, in the afternoon they should return in the same way, bearing the signs of enjoyment in that garden.
By this is explained the summer outing for water sports, when the water-apparatus has been arranged.
There is the <s>Yakṣarātri</s> festival.
There is the moonlight vigil.
There is the auspicious spring festival.

children.text: sahakārabhañjikā abhyūṣakhādikā bisakhādikā navapattrikā udakakṣveḍikā pāñcālānuyānam ekaśālmalī kadambayuddhāni tāstāśca māhimānyo deśyāśca krīḍā janebhyo viśiṣṭam ācareyuḥ
children.translated_text: They should perform for people, as special events, the <s>Sahakārabhañjikā</s>, eating roasted grain, eating lotus stalks, the new-leaf festival, water-splashing, the <s>Pāñcālānuyāna</s>, the <s>Ekaśālmalī</s>, kadamba battles, and various celebrated local games.
Thus are the games performed in company.

children.text: ekacāriṇaśca vibhavasāmarthyād gaṇikāyā nāyikāyāśca sakhībhir nāgarakaiśca saha caritam etena vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: By this is also explained the conduct of a man living alone, according to the power of his resources, together with the friends of a courtesan or heroine and with city gentlemen.

children.text: avibhavastu śarīramātro mallikāphenakakaṣāyamātraparicchadaḥ pūjyād deśād āgataḥ kalāsu vicakṣaṇastadupadeśena goṣṭhyāṃ veśocite ca vṛtte sādhayed ātmānam iti pīṭhamardaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man without wealth, possessing only his body and equipped only with jasmine, soap, and a dyed garment, who has come from a respected region and is skilled in the arts, should establish himself in the salon and in conduct suited to the courtesan's world by instructing in those arts: this is the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>.

children.text: bhuktavibhavastu guṇavān sakalatro veśe goṣṭhyāṃ ca bahumatas tadupajīvī ca viṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>viṭa</s> is one whose fortune has been spent, but who is accomplished, has a wife, is highly regarded in the courtesan's circle and in the salon, and lives by that.
The <s>vidūṣaka</s> is one who knows some part of the arts, is a playmate, and is trustworthy.
Or he may be a humorist.

children.text: ete veśyānāṃ nāgarakāṇāṃ ca mantriṇaḥ saṃdhivigrahaniyuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are the counselors of courtesans and city gentlemen, appointed for alliance and estrangement.

children.text: tair bhikṣukyaḥ kalāvidagdhā muṇḍā vṛṣalyo vṛddhagaṇikāśca vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By them are also explained female mendicants, women clever in the arts, shaven-headed women, low-born women, and old courtesans.

children.text: grāmavāsī ca sajātān vicakṣaṇān kautūhalikān protsāhya nāgarakajanasya vṛttaṃ varṇayañ śraddhāṃ ca janayaṃstad evānukurvīta
children.translated_text: A village-dweller, after encouraging clever and curious men of his own community, should describe the conduct of city people, create interest in it, and imitate that very conduct.
He should also set social gatherings in motion.
Through association he should charm people.
In their affairs, and through assistance, he should favor them.
He should also do them services.
This is the conduct of the city gentleman.
Neither entirely in Sanskrit nor entirely in the regional language,
but telling a story in assemblies, one becomes highly regarded in the world.

children.text: yā goṣṭhī lokavidviṣṭā yā ca svairavisarpiṇī
children.translated_text: A gathering that is hated by the world, or one that roams about licentiously,

children.text: parahiṃsātmikā yā ca na tām avatared budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or one whose nature is injury to others: a wise man should not enter it.
By keeping company with a gathering that follows people's feelings and has play alone as its business,
a learned man obtains success in the world.

children.text: kāmaścaturṣu varṇeṣu savarṇataḥ śāstrataścānanyapūrvāyāṃ prayujyamānaḥ putrīyo yaśasyo laukikaśca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (erotic practice), when applied among the four varṇas to a woman of the same varṇa, according to the śāstra, and not previously possessed by another, is conducive to sons, fame, and worldly approval.
The opposite is the case with women of a higher varṇa and with women possessed by another.
It is forbidden with women of a lower varṇa who have not been cast out.

children.text: veśyāsu punarbhūṣu ca na śiṣṭo na pratiṣiddhaḥ
children.translated_text: With courtesans and remarried women it is neither approved by the respectable nor forbidden.
For it has pleasure as its purpose.

children.text: tatra nāyikāstisraḥ kanyā punarbhūr veśyā ca
children.translated_text: There the heroines are three: a maiden, a remarried woman, and a courtesan.
Thus it is stated.
For another reason, even a woman possessed by another may optionally be a fourth, according to <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
When he thinks, "This woman is promiscuous."

children.text: anyato 'pi bahuśo vyavasitacāritrā tasyāṃ veśyāyām iva gamanam uttamavarṇinyām api na dharmapīḍāṃ kariṣyati
children.translated_text: Since she has often deliberately behaved improperly elsewhere, going to that woman, as to a courtesan, even if she is of the highest class, will not injure <s>dharma</s>.
She is a remarried woman.
She has previously been possessed by another; there is no hesitation in this case.

children.text: patiṃ vā mahāntam īśvaram asmadamitrasaṃsṛṣṭam iyam avagṛhya prabhutvena carati
children.translated_text: Or: "She has gained control over her husband, a great lord allied with my enemy, and she behaves with authority.

children.text: sā mayā saṃsṛṣṭā snehād enaṃ vyāvartayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: If she is connected with me, she will, out of affection, turn him away from that alliance.

children.text: virasaṃ vā mayi śaktam apakartukāmaṃ ca prakṛtim āpādayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Or she will restore to his proper disposition a man who is hostile toward me, powerful, and wishing to harm me.

children.text: tayā vā mitrīkṛtena mitrakāryam amitrapratīghātam anyad vā duṣpratipādakaṃ kāryaṃ sādhayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Or, through her when she has been made friendly, I shall accomplish a friend's business, the repulse of an enemy, or some other task difficult to carry out.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭo vānayā hatvāsyāḥ patim asmadbhāvyaṃ tadaiśvaryam evam adhigamiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Or, having become connected with her, I shall kill her husband and in this way obtain that lordship which is to come to me.
Or access to her is free of danger and is connected with wealth.
And I, because I am without resources, have exhausted my means of livelihood.

children.text: so 'ham anenopāyena taddhanam atimahad akṛcchrād adhigamiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Therefore by this means I shall obtain that very great wealth without difficulty.

children.text: marmajñā vā mayi dṛḍham abhikāmā sā mām anicchantaṃ doṣavikhyāpanena dūṣayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Or she knows my vulnerable points and is firmly in love with me; if I do not consent, she will ruin me by publicizing my faults.

children.text: asadbhūtaṃ vā doṣaṃ śraddheyaṃ duṣparihāraṃ mayi kṣepsyati yena me vināśaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Or she will cast upon me some nonexistent fault, believable and hard to refute, by which my destruction may come about.

children.text: āyatimantaṃ vā vaśyaṃ patiṃ matto vibhidya dviṣataḥ saṃgrāhayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Or she will split from me a husband who has future prospects and is controllable, and will bring him into the hands of enemies.
Or she herself may enter into alliance with them.

children.text: madavarodhānāṃ vā dūṣayitā patir asyāstad asyāham api dārān eva dūṣayan pratikariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: Or her husband is a corrupter of the women of my inner apartments; therefore I too, by corrupting his wives, shall retaliate against him.
Or, on the king's order, I shall destroy his enemy who is within her household.
The woman whom I desire elsewhere is under her control.
Through this connection with her I shall obtain that woman.

children.text: kanyām alabhyāṃ vātmādhīnām artharūpavatīṃ mayi saṃkrāmayiṣyati
children.translated_text: Or she will transfer to me an unattainable maiden who is under her authority and endowed with wealth and beauty.

children.text: mamāmitro vāsyāḥ patyā sahaikībhāvam upagatastam anayā rasena yojayiṣyāmītyevamādibhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ parastriyam api prakurvīta ||
children.translated_text: Or my enemy has entered into union with her husband; I shall join him to this woman by means of passion." For such reasons and the like, one may also approach another man's wife.

children.text: iti sāhasikyaṃ na kevalaṃ rāgād eva
children.translated_text: Thus this is an undertaking of bold risk, not simply from passion alone.

children.text: etair eva kāraṇair mahāmātrasambaddhā rājasambaddhā vā tatraikadeśacāriṇī kācid anyā vā kāryasaṃpādinī vidhavā pañcamīti cārāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For these same reasons, a widow connected with a minister or connected with the king, moving in one part of that sphere, or some other widow able to accomplish a task, is a fifth type, according to <s>Cārāyaṇa</s>.
That same woman, if she is an ascetic, is the sixth type, according to <s>Suvarṇanābha</s>.

children.text: gaṇikāyā duhitā paricārikā vānanyapūrvā saptamīti ghoṭakamukhaḥ
children.translated_text: The daughter of a courtesan, or a maidservant, who has not previously belonged to another, is the seventh type, according to <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
A young woman of good family who has passed beyond childhood, because the modes of approach are different, is the eighth type, according to <s>Gonardīya</s>.

children.text: kāryāntarābhāvād etāsām api pūrvāsvevopalakṣaṇam tasmāccatasra eva nāyikā iti vātsyāyanaḥ
children.translated_text: Since these have no separate purpose, they too are included under the earlier types; therefore there are only four <s>nāyikās</s> (heroines), according to <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Because it is distinct, some say that the third nature is the fifth type.
But there is only one universally recognized <s>nāyaka</s> (male lover).
The concealed one is the second.
For no special distinction is obtained.
But one should know superiority, inferiority, and middling status from qualities and faults.
We shall state those qualities and faults of both in the section on courtesans.

children.text: agamyāstvevaitāḥ kuṣṭhinyunmattā patitā bhinnarahasyā prakāśaprārthinī gataprāyayauvanātiśvetātikṛṣṇā durgandhā saṃbandhinī sakhī pravrajitā saṃbandhisakhiśrotriyarājadārāśca ||
children.translated_text: The women who must not be approached are these: a leprous woman, a madwoman, a fallen woman, one who betrays secrets, one who seeks public exposure, one whose youth is almost gone, one excessively white, one excessively dark, one with a bad smell, a female relative, a friend, an ascetic woman, and the wives of a relative, a friend, a learned Brahmin, or the king.
According to the <s>Bābhravīyas</s>, no woman who has seen five men is unapproachable.
According to <s>Goṇikāputra</s>, except for the wives of a relative, a friend, a learned Brahmin, or the king.

children.text: saha pāṃsukrīḍitam upakārasambaddhaṃ samānaśīlavyasanaṃ sahādhyāyinaṃ yaścāsya marmāṇi rahasyāni ca vidyāt yasya cāyaṃ vidyād vā dhātrapatyaṃ sahasaṃvṛddhaṃ mitram ||
children.translated_text: A friend is one who played in the dust with him, is bound by favors, has the same character and vices, was a fellow student, knows his weak points and secrets, and whose weak points and secrets he himself knows, or the child of his nurse, one raised together with him.

children.text: pitṛpaitāmaham avisaṃvādakam adṛṣṭavaikṛtaṃ vaśyaṃ dhruvam alobhaśīlam aparihāryam amantravisrāvīti mitrasaṃpat ||
children.translated_text: The excellence of a friend is this: inherited from his father and grandfather, not deceptive, with no observed change for the worse, obedient, steady, free from greed by nature, impossible to discard, and not one who leaks counsel.
Washermen, barbers, garland-makers, perfumers, sellers of liquor, beggars, cowherds, betel sellers, goldsmiths, chair-companions, libertines, jesters, and the like are friends.
And urban men should be friends with their wives, according to <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: yad ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇam ubhayatrodāraṃ viśeṣato nāyikāyāḥ suvisrabdhaṃ tatra dūtakarma ||
children.translated_text: Where something is common to both parties, noble on both sides, and especially well trusted by the heroine, there is the work of a messenger.

children.text: paṭutā dhārṣṭyam iṅgitākārajñatā pratāraṇakālajñatā viṣahyabuddhitvaṃ laghvī pratipattiḥ sopāyā ceti dūtaguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Skill, boldness, knowledge of gestures and outward signs, knowledge of the time for deception, an intelligence that can endure, quick comprehension, and resourcefulness: these are the qualities of a messenger.
And on this point there is a verse:
A self-controlled man, possessed of friends, disciplined, knowing feelings, and aware of place and time,
may win even an unattainable woman without effort.
The male lovers are distinguished by the organ as hare, bull, and horse.
The heroine, in turn, is gazelle, mare, or elephant cow.
When there is union of similar partners, the three forms of intercourse are equal.
By contrast, the unequal forms are six.

children.text: viṣameṣvapi puruṣādhikyaṃ ced anantarasaṃprayoge dve uccarate
children.translated_text: Among the unequal forms, if the man is superior, two in immediately adjacent unions are called high.
The one separated by an interval is the very high form of intercourse.
In the opposite case, again, two are low forms of intercourse.
The one separated by an interval is the very low form of intercourse.
Among these, the equal forms are best.
The two marked by the comparative suffix are the lowest.
The remaining forms are middling.
Even in equality, the one with the higher mark is better than the one with the lower mark.
Thus, by measure, there are nine forms of intercourse.

children.text: yasya saṃprayogakāle prītir udāsīnā vīryam alpaṃ kṣatāni ca na sahate sa mandavegaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man whose pleasure during intercourse is indifferent, whose vigor is slight, and who cannot bear wounds is of slow intensity.
The middle and fierce intensities are the opposites of that; and so too in the case of the heroine.
In that matter too, just as with size, there are nine forms of intercourse.
Likewise, with respect to time too, the male lovers are quick, medium, and long-lasting.
On this point there is a dispute concerning the woman.

children.text: na strī puruṣavad eva bhāvam adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: A woman does not attain the state in exactly the same way as a man.
Rather, because of continuity, her itching is removed by the man.

children.text: sā punar ābhimānikena sukhena saṃsṛṣṭā rasāntaraṃ janayati
children.translated_text: That, again, when mixed with a self-imagined pleasure, produces another flavor.
In that she has the notion of pleasure.

children.text: puruṣapratīteś cānabhijñatvāt kathaṃ te sukham iti praṣṭum aśakyatvāt
children.translated_text: And because she is ignorant of the man's experience, and because it is impossible to ask, 'What is your pleasure like?'

children.text: katham etad upalabhyata iti cet puruṣo hi ratim adhigamya svecchayā viramati na striyam apekṣate na tvevaṃ strītyauddālakiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, 'How is this known?', for a man, after attaining <s>rati</s> (sexual pleasure), stops of his own will and does not attend to the woman; but a woman is not like this, according to <s>Auddālaki</s>.
In that matter one might say this:

children.text: ciravege nāyake striyo 'nurajyante śīghravegasya bhāvam anāsādyāvasāne 'bhyasūyinyo bhavanti
children.translated_text: Women become attached to a long-lasting male lover; failing to reach the state of a quick one, they become resentful at the end.
All that is a sign of the attainment or non-attainment of the state.
But that is not so.
For even the remedying of an itch is pleasant for a long time.
This is indeed reasonable.
Therefore, because it is doubtful, it is not a reliable sign.
In sexual union, a woman's itching is removed by the man.
And that, mixed with self-imagination, is called pleasure.

children.text: sātatyād yuvatir ārambhāt prabhṛti bhāvam adhigacchati
children.translated_text: Because of continuity, a young woman attains the state from the very beginning.
But a man does so only at the end.
This is more reasonable.

children.text: na hyasatyāṃ bhāvaprāptau garbhasaṃbhava iti bābhravīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For without attainment of the state there is no possibility of conception, according to the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.
Here too the same objection and answer occur again.
In that matter one might say this:
If flavor is attained continuously, then at the beginning there is neutrality of mind and not very great endurance.
Then, gradually, there is a stronger connection with passion and disregard for the body.
And at the end there is a desire to stop: this is reasonable.
But that is not so.

children.text: sāmānye api bhrāntisaṃskāre kulālacakrasya bhramarakasya vā bhrāntāv eva vartamānasya prārambhe mandavegatā tataśca krameṇa pūraṇam vegasyetyupapadyate
children.translated_text: For even in an ordinary impression of rotation, as with the turning of a potter's wheel or a spinning top while it is still rotating, there is slow speed at the start and then a gradual filling out of speed.
And the desire to stop arises from the depletion of the bodily element.
Therefore there is no objection.

children.text: suratānte sukhaṃ puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ tu satataṃ sukham
children.translated_text: For men there is pleasure at the end of intercourse, but for women there is continuous pleasure.
And the desire to stop arises because of depletion of the bodily element.

by <s>hallīsaka</s> games, songs, and <s>Lāṭa</s> dances,
by looking at the disk of the moon with eyes moist and restless with passion,

children.text: ādye saṃdarśane jāte pūrvaṃ ye syur manorathāḥ
children.translated_text: by recounting all the desires that arose before, when the first meeting took place,

children.text: punarviyoge duḥkhaṃ ca tasya sarvasya kīrtanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the sorrow of later separation,
and, at the end of that recounting, by passionate embraces with kisses,

children.text: taistaiśca bhāvaiḥ saṃyukto yūno rāgo vivardhate ||
children.translated_text: the passion of young people, joined with all these various states, increases.

children.text: rāgavad āhāryarāgaṃ kṛtrimarāgaṃ vyavahitarāgaṃ poṭārataṃ khalaratam ayantritaratam iti rataviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The special kinds of intercourse are <s>rāgavat</s> (passionate), <s>āhāryarāga</s> (induced passion), <s>kṛtrimarāga</s> (artificial passion), <s>vyavahitarāga</s> (displaced passion), <s>poṭārata</s>, <s>khalarata</s>, and <s>ayantritarata</s> (unrestrained intercourse).

children.text: saṃdarśanāt prabhṛtyubhayor api pravṛddharāgayoḥ prayatnakṛte samāgame pravāsapratyāgamane vā kalahaviyogayoge tadrāgavat ||
children.translated_text: When, from the time of seeing one another onward, the passion of both has grown, and union is achieved with effort, or when it occurs on returning from travel, or when there is union after separation caused by a quarrel, that is <s>rāgavat</s>.
In that case, activity proceeds according to one's own intention and as far as desired.

children.text: madhyastharāgayor ārabdhaṃ yad anurajyate tad āhāryarāgam ||
children.translated_text: What is begun when the passion of the two is moderate, and then becomes passionate, is <s>āhāryarāga</s>.

children.text: tatra cātuḥṣaṣṭikair yogaiḥ sātmyānuviddhaiḥ saṃdhukṣya saṃdhukṣya rāgaṃ pravarteta
children.translated_text: There, with the sixty-four techniques adapted to their temperament, one should proceed by kindling passion again and again.
For the purpose of bringing that about, or when the two are attached elsewhere, there is <s>kṛtrimarāga</s>.
There one should consider the techniques collectively, according to the treatise.

children.text: puruṣastu hṛdayapriyām anyāṃ manasi nidhāya vyavaharet
children.translated_text: But the man should keep in mind another woman dear to his heart and conduct himself accordingly,
from the beginning of union up to the point of pleasure.
Therefore that is <s>vyavahitarāga</s>.

children.text: nyūnāyāṃ kumbhadāsyāṃ paricārikāyāṃ vā yāvadarthaṃ saṃprayogastatpoṭāratam ||
children.translated_text: With an inferior woman, a pot-carrying slave girl, or a maidservant, union merely as far as required is <s>poṭārata</s>.
There one should not pay regard to the courtesies.

children.text: tathā veśyāyā grāmīṇena saha yāvadarthaṃ khalaratam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when a courtesan has intercourse with a villager merely as far as required, that is <s>khalarata</s>.
So too is the intercourse of a city man with women of villages, cattle-stations, or border regions.
When mutual confidence has arisen between two people, intercourse through mutual compliance is <s>ayantritarata</s>.
These are the kinds of intercourse.

children.text: vardhamānapraṇayā tu nāyikā sapatnīnām agrahaṇaṃ tadāśrayam ālāpaṃ vā gotraskhalitaṃ vā na marṣayet
children.translated_text: But a heroine whose love is increasing should not tolerate the mention of co-wives, talk connected with them, or a slip of the name.
Nor should she tolerate an offense committed by the lover.

children.text: tatra subhṛśaḥ kalaho ruditam āyāsaḥ śiroruhāṇām avakṣodanaṃ prahaṇanam āsanācchayanād vā mahyāṃ patanaṃ mālyabhūṣaṇāvamokṣo bhūmau śayyā ca ||
children.translated_text: In such a case there is a very violent quarrel: crying, distress, disheveling of the hair, striking, falling to the ground from a seat or bed, throwing off garlands and ornaments, and lying on the ground.

children.text: tatra yuktarūpeṇa sāmnā pādapatanena vā prasannamanāstām anunayann upakramya śayanam ārohayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, by suitable conciliation or by falling at her feet, he should begin to appease her, make her calm in mind, and raise her onto the bed.

children.text: tasya ca vacanam uttareṇa yojayantī vivṛddhakrodhā sakacagraham asyāsyam unnamayya pādena bāhau śirasi vakṣasi pṛṣṭhe vā sakṛd dvistrir avahanyāt
children.translated_text: And she, meeting his words with a retort and growing still angrier, should seize him by the hair, lift up his face, and strike him once, twice, or three times with her foot on the arm, head, chest, or back.
She should go to the doorway.
Sitting there, she should bring herself to tears.

children.text: atikruddhāpi tu na dvāradeśād bhūyo gacchet
children.translated_text: But even if she is very angry, she should not go beyond the doorway,
because that would be blameworthy.
So says <s>Dattaka</s>.
There, when she is being appeased by proper reasoning, she should look for reconciliation.

children.text: prasannāpi tu sakaṣāyair eva vākyair enaṃ tudatīva prasannaratikāṅkṣiṇī nāyakena parirabhyeta ||
children.translated_text: Even though appeased, however, still seeming to prick him with sharp words and desiring reconciled lovemaking, she should be embraced by the lover.

children.text: svabhavanasthā tu nimittāt kalahitā tathāvidhaceṣṭaiva nāyakam abhigacchet
children.translated_text: But if she is in her own house and has quarreled for some reason, she should approach the lover with gestures of that same kind.

children.text: tatra pīṭhamardaviṭavidūṣakair nāyakaprayuktair upaśamitaroṣā tair evānunītā taiḥ sahaiva tadbhavanam adhigacchet
children.translated_text: There, with her anger quieted by the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, <s>viṭa</s>, and <s>vidūṣaka</s> sent by the lover, and entreated by those same men, she should go with them to his house.
And there she should stay.
Thus is the lovers' quarrel.
And here there are verses:
Thus, practicing this <s>catuḥṣaṣṭi</s> (set of sixty-four arts), proclaimed by <s>Bābhravya</s>,
a lover attains success among excellent women.
Even if he speaks of other treatises, one who lacks the sixty-four arts
is not greatly honored in conversations in an assembly of learned people.
But one who is adorned with this, even if deprived of other knowledge,
plunges to the front in conversations in gatherings of men and women.

children.text: vidvadbhiḥ pūjitām enāṃ khalair api supūjitām
children.translated_text: Who would not honor this <s>Nandinī</s>, honored by the learned, well honored even by rogues,

children.text: pūjitāṃ gaṇikāsaṃghair nandinīṃ ko na pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: and honored by companies of courtesans?
In the treatises this is explained by teachers as <s>Nandinī</s>, fortunate, successful,
fortune-making, and dear to women.
A man skilled in the sixty-four arts is looked upon with esteem and affection
by maidens, by others' wives, and by courtesans.

children.text: savarṇāyām ananyapūrvāyāṃ śāstrato 'dhigatāyāṃ dharmo 'rthaḥ putrāḥ saṃbandhaḥ pakṣavṛddhir anupaskṛtā ratiśca ||
children.translated_text: With a woman of the same class, not previously possessed by another, and obtained according to the treatise, there are <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), <s>artha</s> (material prosperity), sons, kinship, increase of one's faction, and unadorned pleasure.

children.text: tasmāt kanyām abhijanopetāṃ mātāpitṛmatīṃ trivarṣāt prabhṛti nyūnavayasaṃ ślāghyācāre dhanavati pakṣavati kule saṃbandhipriye saṃbandhibhir ākule prasūtāṃ prabhūtamātṛpitṛpakṣāṃ rūpaśīlalakṣaṇasampannām anyūnādhikāvinaṣṭadantanakhakarṇakeśākṣistanīm arogiprakṛtiśarīrāṃ tathāvidha eva śrutavāñ śīlayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a learned man, being himself of that same kind, should court a maiden from a good family, having mother and father, younger than himself by at least three years, born in a family of praiseworthy conduct, wealthy, factionally strong, fond of kinship, filled with kinsmen, having abundant support on both the mother's and father's sides, endowed with beauty, character, and auspicious marks, not deficient, excessive, or defective in teeth, nails, ears, hair, eyes, and breasts, and healthy in natural constitution and body.

children.text: yāṃ gṛhītvā kṛtinam ātmānaṃ manyeta na ca samānair nindyeta tasyāṃ pravṛttir iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Activity toward her is proper when, having taken her, he would regard himself as successful and would not be blamed by his equals; so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
In choosing her, his mother and father and his relatives should exert themselves,
as also friends whose words are accepted and who are connected with both sides.
They should make known the faults of other suitors, both visible and known from report,
and the hero's qualities, familial and personal, that increase favorable intention.
Especially to the maiden's mother they should show qualities favorable both for the present and the future.

children.text: daivacintakarūpaśca śakunanimittagrahalagnabalalakṣaṇadarśanena nāyakasya bhaviṣyantam arthasaṃyogaṃ kalyāṇam anuvarṇayet ||
children.translated_text: And someone in the guise of an astrologer should describe the hero's future conjunction with wealth and good fortune by showing the strength of omens, portents, planets, ascendant, and marks.

children.text: apare punar asyānyato viśiṣṭena kanyālābhena kanyāmātaram unmādayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Others again should excite the maiden's mother with the prospect that he might obtain a maiden superior to this one elsewhere.
One should choose and give a maiden in conformity with divine signs, portents, omens, and overheard indications,
not by chance or by merely human judgment, so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
One should reject in choosing a girl who is sleeping, crying, or gone out,

children.text: apraśastanāmadheyāṃ ca guptāṃ dattāṃ ghonāṃ pṛṣatām ṛṣabhāṃ vinatāṃ vikaṭāṃ vimuṇḍāṃ śucidūṣitāṃ sāṃkarikīṃ rākāṃ phalīnīṃ mitrāṃ svanujām varṣakarīṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: and one should reject one with an inauspicious name, as also one named <s>Guptā</s>, <s>Dattā</s>, <s>Ghonā</s>, <s>Pṛṣatā</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhā</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, <s>Vikaṭā</s>, <s>Vimuṇḍā</s>, <s>Śucidūṣitā</s>, <s>Sāṃkarikī</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Phalīnī</s>, <s>Mitrā</s>, <s>Svanujā</s>, or <s>Varṣakarī</s>.
One should reject in choosing a girl named after a lunar mansion, named after a river,
named after a tree, censured, or having <s>la</s> or <s>ra</s> as the penultimate sound.
Prosperity is found in the girl on whom mind and eye are fastened;
one should not attend to another,
so some say.
Therefore at the time of giving her, they should present the maiden in splendid dress.

children.text: aparāhṇikaṃ ca nityaṃ prasādhitāyāḥ sakhībhiḥ saha krīḍā
children.translated_text: Every afternoon, when she is adorned, there should be play with her friends,
and there should be deliberate showing of her in crowds of people at sacrifices, weddings, and the like,
and likewise at festivals,
because she has the same status as merchandise.

children.text: varaṇārtham upagatāṃśca bhadradarśanān pradakṣiṇavācaśca tatsaṃbandhisaṃgatān puruṣān maṅgalaiḥ pratigṛhṇīyuḥ
children.translated_text: Men who have come for the purpose of choosing her, who are handsome in appearance, speak auspiciously, and are associated with her kin, should be received with auspicious offerings.
And they should show them the adorned maiden under some other pretext.
They should set a limit for examining fate and for making an inspection,
up to the determination of giving her.

children.text: snānādiṣu niyujyamānā varayitāraḥ sarvaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā na tadaharevābhyupagaccheyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the suitors are being appointed to bathing and the like, they should say, 'Everything will happen,' but should not consent on that very day.

children.text: deśapravṛttisātmyād vā brāhmaprājāpatyārṣadaivānām anyatamena vivāhena śāstrataḥ pariṇayet
children.translated_text: According to the custom suitable to the region, he should marry her according to the treatise by one of the marriages called <s>brāhma</s>, <s>prājāpatya</s>, <s>ārṣa</s>, or <s>daiva</s>.
Thus ends the rule for choosing.
And here there are verses:
Shared studies and the like, play together, marriages, and associations

children.text: samānair eva kāryāṇi nottamair nāpi vādhamaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be made only with equals, not with superiors and not with inferiors.

children.text: kanyāṃ gṛhītvā varteta preṣyavad yatra nāyakaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, after taking a maiden, the hero lives like a servant,
one should know that as a high alliance, rejected by the proud.

children.text: svāmivad vicared yatra bāndhavaiḥ svaiḥ puraskṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Where he moves about like a master, set forward by his own relatives,
that too is an unpraiseworthy low alliance, censured by good people.
Where play is practiced with mutual enjoyment of happiness,
and each distinguishes the other, that is prescribed as a proper alliance.
Even after making a high alliance, he should later bow to his kinsmen;

children.text: na tv eva hīnasaṃbandhaṃ kuryāt sadbhir vininditam ||
children.translated_text: but he should never make a low alliance, censured by good people.

children.text: saṃgatayostrirātram adhaḥśayyā brahmacaryaṃ kṣāralavaṇavarjam āhārastathā saptāhaṃ satūryamaṅgalasnānaṃ prasādhanaṃ sahabhojanaṃ ca prekṣā saṃbandhināṃ ca pūjanam
children.translated_text: When the two have come together, for three nights there should be sleeping on the floor, chastity, and food free from alkali and salt; likewise for a week there should be auspicious bathing with music, adornment, eating together, public entertainments, and honoring of relatives.
This applies to all classes.

children.text: tasminn etāṃ niśi vijane mṛdubhir upacārair upakrameta ||
children.translated_text: On that night, in private, he should begin with her by gentle attentions.

children.text: trirātram avacanaṃ hi stambham iva nāyakaṃ paśyantī kanyā nirvidyeta paribhavecca tṛtīyām iva prakṛtim
children.translated_text: For, seeing the hero silent for three nights like a post, the maiden would become disgusted and would despise him as if he were a third nature.
So say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.

children.text: upakrameta viśrambhayecca na tu brahmacaryam ativarteta
children.translated_text: He should begin and make her trust him, but he should not transgress chastity.
So says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
And while beginning, he should not do anything by force.
For women are like flowers, and approaches to them must be delicate.
When they are approached violently before confidence has been gained, they become averse to sexual union.
Therefore he should treat her only with gentle conciliation.

children.text: yuktyāpi tu yataḥ prasaram upalabhet tenaivānu praviśet ||
children.translated_text: But also by skill: from whatever point he obtains an opening, by that very point he should enter further.
He should proceed with an embrace pleasing to her, one that has already been practiced,
because it has not been long delayed.
And he should begin with the upper part of the body,
because it can be endured.
In lamplight, this applies to one whose youth is fully developed and who has been previously known;
in darkness, to a young girl and one who has not been known before.
When she has accepted an embrace, he should offer betel from his mouth.

children.text: tadapratipadyamānāṃ ca sāntvanair vākyaiḥ śapathaiḥ pratiyācitaiḥ pādapatanaiśca grāhayet
children.translated_text: If she does not accept it, he should make her take it with soothing words, oaths, entreaties, and falling at her feet.

children.text: vrīḍāyuktāpi yoṣidatyantakruddhāpi na pādapatanam ativartate iti sārvatrikam ||
children.translated_text: Even a woman possessed by shame, even one extremely angry, does not go beyond a falling at her feet: this is a general rule.
On the occasion of giving that, he should kiss her gently, clearly, and without disturbance.
When she has accepted that, he should engage her in conversation.

children.text: tacchravaṇārthaṃ yat kiṃcid alpākṣarābhidheyam ajānann iva pṛcchet
children.translated_text: For the sake of hearing her voice, he should ask about something that can be answered in a few syllables, as if he did not know it.

children.text: tatra niṣpratipattim anudvejayan sāntvanāyuktaṃ bahuśa eva pṛcchet
children.translated_text: If she has no reply there, he should ask again and again, with reassurance, without upsetting her.
And if she still does not speak, he should press her.

children.text: sarvā eva hi kanyāḥ puruṣeṇa prayujyamānaṃ vacanaṃ viṣahante
children.translated_text: For all maidens tolerate speech addressed to them by a man,

children.text: na tu laghumiśrām api vācaṃ vadanti
children.translated_text: but they do not themselves speak even a word mixed with familiarity.
So says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
When pressed, however, she should arrange her answers by shaking her head.
But in a quarrel she should not shake her head.

children.text: icchasi māṃ necchasi vā kiṃ te ahaṃ rucito na rucito veti pṛṣṭā ciraṃ sthitvā nirbadhyamānā tadānukūlyena śiraḥ kampayet
children.translated_text: When asked, 'Do you desire me or not? Do you like me or not?' she should remain for a long time and, when pressed, shake her head in accordance with his wish.
But when he elaborates on the matter, she should dispute it.

children.text: saṃstutā cet sakhīm anukūlām ubhayato 'pi visrabdhāṃ tām antarā kṛtvā kathāṃ yojayet
children.translated_text: If she is already acquainted with him, he should arrange conversation by placing between them a favorable female friend trusted by both sides.
At that, she should laugh with her face downcast.
And she should reproach that friend for talking too much and dispute with her.

children.text: sā tu parihāsārtham idam anayoktam iti cānuktam api brūyāt
children.translated_text: But the friend, for the sake of joking, should say, 'This was said by her,' even when it was not said.

children.text: tatra tām apanudya prativacanārtham abhyarthyamānā tūṣṇīm āsīta
children.translated_text: Then, after pushing that friend away, when she is asked for a reply, she should sit silently.

children.text: nirbadhyamānā tu nāham evaṃ bravīmītyavyaktākṣaram anavasitārthaṃ vacanaṃ brūyāt
children.translated_text: But when pressed, she should say, 'I am not saying that,' with indistinct syllables and words whose meaning is not fully settled.

children.text: nāyakaṃ ca vihasantī kadācit kaṭākṣaiḥ prekṣeta
children.translated_text: And while laughing, she should sometimes glance at the lover with sidelong looks.
Thus the arrangement of conversation.

children.text: evaṃ jātaparicayā cānirvadantī tatsamīpe yācitaṃ tāmbūlaṃ vilepanaṃ srajaṃ nidadhyāt
children.translated_text: In this way, once familiarity has arisen and she is not refusing, she should place near him the betel, ointment, or garland that has been requested.
Or she should tie it in his upper garment.

children.text: tathā yuktām ācchuritakena stanamukulayor upari spṛśet
children.translated_text: When she is thus engaged, he should touch the tops of her breasts with a feigned accidental contact.

children.text: vāryamāṇaśca tvam api māṃ pariṣvajasva tato naivam ācariṣyāmīti sthityā pariṣvañjayet
children.translated_text: And when he is restrained, he should make her embrace him on the pretext, 'You too embrace me, and then I will not behave like this.'

children.text: svaṃ ca hastam ā nābhideśāt prasārya nirvartayet
children.translated_text: He should extend his own hand as far as the region of her navel and then withdraw it.

children.text: krameṇa cainām utsaṅgam āropyādhikam adhikam upakramet
children.translated_text: And gradually, having lifted her onto his lap, he should proceed more and more.
If she does not consent, he should frighten her.

children.text: ahaṃ khalu tava dantapadānyadhare kariṣyāmi stanapṛṣṭhe ca nakhapadam
children.translated_text: 'I shall indeed make marks of my teeth on your lower lip and marks of my nails on the surface of your breasts.

children.text: ātmanaśca svayaṃ kṛtvā tvayā kṛtam iti te sakhījanasya purataḥ kathayiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: And after making them on myself, I shall tell your circle of female friends that they were made by you.

children.text: sā tvaṃ kim atra vakṣyasīti bālavibhīṣikair bālapratyāyanaiśca śanair enāṃ pratārayet
children.translated_text: What will you say about this?' With childish threats and childish assurances he should slowly deceive her.

children.text: dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ ca rātrau kiṃcid adhikaṃ viśrambhitāṃ hastena yojayet ||
children.translated_text: On the second and third nights, when her confidence has been increased somewhat, he should engage her with his hand.
He should begin kissing her whole body.

children.text: ūrvoścopari vinyastahastaḥ saṃvāhanakriyāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ krameṇorumūlam api saṃvāhayet
children.translated_text: When the act of massage has succeeded, with his hand placed on her thighs, he should gradually massage also the root of her thighs.

children.text: nivārite saṃvāhane ko doṣa ityākulayed enām
children.translated_text: If the massage is forbidden, he should unsettle her by saying, 'What fault is there in massage?'
And he should make that firm.

children.text: tatra siddhāyā guhyadeśābhimarśanaṃ raśanāviyojanaṃ nīvīvisraṃsanaṃ vasanaparivartanam ūrumūlasaṃvāhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: When she has accepted that, there are touching the private region, loosening the girdle, slipping down the lower garment, changing the clothing, and massaging the root of the thighs.
And these are his other pretexts.
When she is fitted to the device, he should delight her.
But he should instruct her not to break the vow at the wrong time.
He should show his own affection.
And he should recount former longings.
And for the future he should promise conduct in accordance with her wishes.
He should remove her fear of rival wives.

children.text: kālena ca krameṇa vimuktakanyābhāvām anudvejayann upakrameta
children.translated_text: And in due time, gradually, when she has abandoned the state of maidenhood, he should approach her without upsetting her.
Thus, gaining a maiden's confidence.
And here there are verses:
In this way, following her mind, he should conciliate the young girl by a suitable means.
Thus she becomes affectionate toward him and very trusting.
Success with maidens is not attained by excessive compliance, nor by excessive opposition;

children.text: siddhiṃ gacchati kanyāsu tasmān madhyena sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: therefore he should accomplish it by the middle way.
He who knows how to produce affection for himself, increase women's self-regard,

children.text: kanyāvisrambhaṇaṃ vetti yaḥ sa tāsāṃ priyo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and gain a maiden's confidence becomes dear to them.
But he who neglects a maiden, thinking, 'She is endowed with excessive modesty,'
is despised like a beast, as one who does not know her intention.
Or, when a maiden is approached suddenly by one who has not found her mind,

children.text: bhayaṃ vitrāsam udvegaṃ sadyo dveṣaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: she immediately comes to fear, terror, agitation, and hatred.
She, not having reached a union of affection and being spoiled by that agitation,

children.text: puruṣadveṣiṇī vā syād vidviṣṭā vā tato 'nyagā ||
children.translated_text: Or she may be hostile to men, or hostile to him and attached to another.

children.text: dhanahīnastu guṇayukto 'pi madhyasthaguṇo hīnāpadeśo vā sadhano vā prātiveśyaḥ mātṛpitṛbhrātṛṣu ca paratantraḥ bālavṛttir ucitapraveśo vā kanyām alabhyatvān na varayet
children.translated_text: But a man who is without wealth, even if endowed with virtues, or one of mediocre qualities, or one of low reputation, or a wealthy neighbor who is dependent on his mother, father, and brothers, or one who behaves like a child, or one who has a suitable opportunity of access, should not choose a girl if she is unattainable.
Rather, from childhood onward he should himself win her affection.

children.text: tathāyuktaśca mātulakulānuvartī dakṣiṇāpathe bāla eva mātrā ca pitrā ca viyuktaḥ paribhūtakalpo dhanotkarṣādalabhyāṃ mātuladuhitaram anyasmai vā pūrvadattāṃ sādhayet
children.translated_text: A man so situated, following his maternal uncle's family, in the <s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>, separated from both mother and father while still a boy and treated almost with contempt, may, through his abundance of wealth, obtain his maternal uncle's daughter who would otherwise be unattainable, or who had previously been given to someone else.
He may also desire another girl from outside the family.

children.text: bālāyām evaṃ sati dharmādhigame saṃvananaṃ ślāghyam iti ghoṭakamukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the girl is still young, winning her over in this way, once <s>dharma</s> (lawful propriety) has been secured, is praiseworthy, says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.

children.text: tayā saha puṣpāvacayaṃ grathanaṃ gṛhakaṃ duhitṛkākrīḍāyojanaṃ bhaktapānakaraṇam iti kurvīta
children.translated_text: Together with her he should gather flowers, weave garlands, play at house, arrange games with dolls, and prepare food and drink.
This should be done according to the suitability of acquaintance and age.

children.text: ākarṣakrīḍā paṭṭikākrīḍā muṣṭidyūtakṣullakādidyūtāni madhyamāṅguligrahaṇaṃ ṣaṭpāṣāṇakādīni ca deśyāni tatsātmyāt tadāptadāsaceṭikābhis tayā ca sahānukrīḍeta
children.translated_text: He should play together with her, and with trusted slave-girls and maidservants of hers, at local games suited to her habits, such as pulling games, board games, fist-dice, small dice games and the like, catching the middle finger, and six-stone games and so forth.

children.text: kṣveḍitakāni sunimīlitakām ārabdhikāṃ lavaṇavīthikām anilatāḍitakāṃ godhūmapuñjikām aṅgulitāḍitakāṃ sakhībhir anyāni ca deśyāni ||
children.translated_text: He should also play, with her friends, whistling games, the well-closed-eyes game, the beginning game, the salt-lane game, the wind-struck game, the heap-of-wheat game, the finger-struck game, and other local games.

children.text: yāṃ ca viśvāsyām asyāṃ manyeta tayā saha nirantarāṃ prītiṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: And with whatever girl he thinks trustworthy toward her, he should form an uninterrupted affection.
He should also learn her acquaintances.
He should especially win over her nurse's daughter with kindness and benefit.

children.text: sā hi prīyamāṇā viditākārāpy apratyādiśantī taṃ tāṃ ca yojayituṃ śaknuyāt
children.translated_text: For if she is pleased, even if she knows his intentions, she may not refuse and may be able to bring him and the girl together.
Even when not explicitly asked, she may act as a go-between.
For even if she does not know his intentions, out of affection she will disclose only his good qualities.
He should act so that the girl to be won becomes attached.

children.text: yatra yatra ca kautukaṃ prayojyāyāstad anu praviśya sādhayet
children.translated_text: Wherever the girl to be won has curiosity, he should enter into that and accomplish his purpose.

children.text: krīḍanakadravyāṇi yānyapūrvāṇi yānyanyāsāṃ viralaśo vidyeraṃstānyasyā ayatnena sampādayet
children.translated_text: Playthings that are novel, and that are rarely found among other girls, he should procure for her without apparent effort.

children.text: tatra kandukam anekabhakticitram alpakālāntaritam anyad anyacca saṃdarśayet
children.translated_text: Among these he should show her a ball painted in many colors, and then, after a short interval, one thing after another.
Likewise dolls made of thread, wood, horn, and ivory, and also those made of beeswax, flour, and clay.
For the sake of her cooking games, he should also provide a display of kitchen equipment.

children.text: kāṣṭhamedhrakayośca saṃyuktayośca strīpuṃsayor ajaiḍakānāṃ devakulagṛhakānāṃ mṛdvidalakāṣṭhavinirmitānāṃ śukaparabhṛtamadanasārikālāvakakukkuṭatittiripañjarakāṇāṃ ca vicitrākṛtisaṃyuktānāṃ jalabhājanānāṃ ca yantrikāṇāṃ vīṇikānāṃ paṭolikānām alaktakamanaḥśilāharitālahiṅgulakaśyāmavarṇakādīnāṃ tathā candanakuṅkumayoḥ pūgaphalānāṃ pattrāṇāṃ kālayuktānāṃ ca śaktiviṣaye pracchannaṃ dānaṃ prakāśadravyāṇāṃ ca prakāśam
children.translated_text: According to his means, he should secretly give secret things, and openly give things meant for public display: wooden pairs in sexual union, figures of women and men joined together, goats and sheep, little temple houses made of clay, split bamboo, and wood, cages of parrots, cuckoos, mynahs, quails, cocks, partridges, and the like, joined with varied designs, mechanical water vessels, small vīṇās, dolls, lac, realgar, orpiment, cinnabar, dark pigments and the like, sandalwood and saffron, betel nuts, leaves, and other timely things.

children.text: yathā ca sarvābhiprāyasaṃvardhakam enaṃ manyeta tathā prayatitavyam
children.translated_text: And he should endeavor in such a way that she thinks him one who fosters all her wishes.
When she looks at him, he should ask for his object secretly.
Likewise he should arrange conversation.

children.text: pracchannadānasya tu kāraṇam ātmano gurujanād bhayaṃ khyāpayet
children.translated_text: As the reason for secret giving, he should announce that he fears his elders.
And he should say that the thing to be given is desired by someone else.

children.text: vardhamānānurāgaṃ cākhyānake manaḥ kurvatīm anvarthābhiḥ kathābhiścittahāriṇībhiśca rañjayet
children.translated_text: As her affection grows and she fixes her mind on tales, he should charm her with meaningful and captivating stories.
When she is overcome by wonder, he should amaze her with conjuring tricks and displays.

children.text: kalāsu kautukinīṃ tatkauśalena gītapriyāṃ śrutiharair gītaiḥ
children.translated_text: If she is curious about the arts, he should charm her by his skill in them; if she loves song, with songs pleasing to the ear.

children.text: āśvayujyām aṣṭamīcandrake kaumudyām utsaveṣu yātrāyāṃ grahaṇe gṛhācāre vā vicitrair āpīḍaiḥ karṇapattrabhaṅgaiḥ sikthakapradhānair vastrāṅgulīyakabhūṣaṇadānaiśca
children.translated_text: On the <s>Āśvayujī</s>, on the eighth-moon night, at the moonlight festival, at festivals, on processions, during an eclipse, or in household observances, he should charm her with variegated garlands, folded ear-ornaments, waxen objects especially, and gifts of garments, rings, and ornaments.
That is, if he does not consider them liable to cause fault.

children.text: anyapuruṣaviśeṣābhijñatayā dhātreyikāsyāḥ puruṣapravṛttau cātuḥṣaṣṭikān yogān grāhayet
children.translated_text: Through the nurse's daughter, who has special knowledge of other men, he should make her learn the sixty-four practices connected with a man's sexual activity.

children.text: tadgrahaṇopadeśena ca prayojyāyāṃ ratikauśalam ātmanaḥ prakāśayet
children.translated_text: And under the pretext of instruction in learning them, he should reveal to the girl to be won his own skill in lovemaking.
He himself should be elegantly dressed and not displeasing to look at.
And when she shows feeling, he should indicate it by gestures and outward signs.

children.text: yuvatayo hi saṃsṛṣṭam abhīkṣṇadarśanaṃ ca puruṣaṃ prathamaṃ kāmayante
children.translated_text: For young women first desire a man who is familiar with them and frequently seen.

children.text: kāmayamānā api tu nābhiyuñjata iti prāyovādaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet even when they desire him, they generally do not make the approach themselves.
Thus the approaches toward a young girl.
We shall describe those gestures and outward signs.
She does not look at him face to face.
When looked at, she shows embarrassment.
Under some pretext, she displays a part of her own body that is attractive.

children.text: pramattaṃ pracchannaṃ nāyakam atikrāntaṃ ca vīkṣate
