children.translated_text: She looks at the hero when he is distracted, hidden, or has passed by.

children.text: pṛṣṭā ca kiṃcit sasmitam avyaktākṣaram anavasitārthaṃ ca mandaṃ mandam adhomukhī kathayati
children.translated_text: And when questioned, smiling slightly, indistinct in syllables and with meaning unfinished, she speaks very softly with her face lowered.
She enjoys remaining for a long time near him.

children.text: dūre sthitā paśyatu mām iti manyamānā parijanaṃ savadanavikāram ābhāṣate
children.translated_text: Standing at a distance, thinking, 'Let him see me,' she speaks to an attendant with changes of expression on her face.
She does not leave that place.
Seeing anything at all, she laughs.
There she continues the conversation in order to stay.
She embraces and kisses a child sitting on her lap.
and she makes a tilaka mark for the maidservant.
Relying on the attendants, she shows those various playful gestures.
She places trust in his friends.

children.text: vacanaṃ caiṣāṃ bahu manyate karoti ca
children.translated_text: She values their words highly and acts on them.

children.text: tatparicārakaiḥ saha prītiṃ saṃkathāṃ dyūtam iti ca karoti
children.translated_text: With his attendants she makes affection, conversation, gambling, and so forth.
And in her own tasks she appoints them as if she had authority over them.

children.text: teṣu ca nāyakasaṃkathām anyasya kathayatsvavahitā tāṃ śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: And when they are telling stories of the hero to another, she listens to that attentively.
Urged by the foster-nurse, she enters the hero's dwelling.

children.text: tām antarā kṛtvā tena saha dyūtaṃ krīḍām ālāpaṃ cāyojayitum icchati
children.translated_text: Putting her between them, she wishes to arrange gambling, play, and conversation with him.
Unadorned, she avoids the path of his sight.

children.text: karṇapattram aṅgulīyakaṃ srajaṃ vā tena yācitā sadhīram eva gātrād avatārya sakhyā haste dadāti
children.translated_text: When asked by him for an ear-ornament, a ring, or a garland, she takes it from her body only with composure and gives it into her friend's hand.
And what is given by him she always wears.
At conversations about another suitor she becomes dejected.
And she does not associate with those who side with him.
Here there are two verses:
Seeing these appearances and gestures joined with emotion,
one should consider those several stratagems for union with the maiden.
A girl should be won when she is a child by children's toys, when she is established in youth by the arts,
and, if affectionate, by winning the confidence of trusted people.
A maiden who has shown gestures and outward signs should be approached by method.

children.text: dyūte krīḍanakeṣu ca vivadamānaḥ sākāram asyāḥ pāṇim avalambeta ||
children.translated_text: While quarreling in gambling and in games, he should take hold of her hand with an expressive gesture.
And he should perform the method of embracing, beginning with the touching embrace, as previously stated.

children.text: patracchedyakriyāyāṃ ca svābhiprāyāsūcakaṃ mithunam asyā darśayet ||
children.translated_text: And in the practice of cutting leaves, he should show her a pair that indicates his own intention.
In this way he should occasionally show something else too.

children.text: jalakrīḍāyāṃ taddūrato 'psu nimagnaḥ samīpam asyā gatvā spṛṣṭvā caināṃ tatraivonmajjet ||
children.translated_text: In water play, having plunged into the water at some distance from her, he should go near her, touch her, and then rise up there itself.
And in fresh leaves and the like there should be a communication of feeling with special emphasis.
He should tell of his own suffering without weariness.
And he should tell of a dream charged with feeling under the pretext of someone else.
At a spectacle or in an assembly of his own people, he should sit near her.
There he should touch her under some other pretext.
And, on the pretext of needing support, he should press her foot with his foot.
Then, gradually, he should touch each one of her toes.
And with his big toe he should rub the tips of her nails.

children.text: tatra siddhaḥ padāt padam adhikam ākāṅkṣet ||
children.translated_text: When he has succeeded there, he should desire a greater step beyond each step.
And for the sake of her endurance, he should practice that same act repeatedly.
At the washing of feet, he should press her toes by clasping them with his toes.

children.text: dravyasya samarpaṇe pratigrahe vā tadgato vikāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the offering or receiving of an object, there should be an emotion directed toward her.
At the end of sipping water, there should be a sprinkling with water.

children.text: vijane tamasi ca dvandvam āsīnaḥ kṣāntiṃ kurvīta
children.translated_text: Sitting as a pair in a lonely place and in darkness, he should create forbearance,
and also on a couch in the same place.
There, without agitating her, he should declare his feeling according to the occasion.

children.text: vivikte ca kiṃcid asti kathayitavyam ityuktvā nirvacanaṃ bhāvaṃ ca tatropalakṣayet
children.translated_text: And in private, saying, 'There is something that must be told,' he should observe there her silence and feeling,
as we shall explain in the section on other men's wives.

children.text: viditabhāvastu vyādhim apadiśyaināṃ vārtāgrahaṇārthaṃ svam udavasitam ānayet ||
children.translated_text: But when her feeling is known, he should pretend illness and bring her to his dwelling for the purpose of receiving news of him.
And when she has come, there should be an assignment for pressing his head.

children.text: pāṇim avalambya cāsyāḥ sākāraṃ nayanayor lalāṭe ca nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Taking hold of her hand, with an expressive gesture he should place it on his eyes and forehead.
And under the pretext of medicine he should prescribe a task for her.
'This must be done by you.

children.text: na hyetad ṛte kanyayā anyena kāryam iti gacchantīṃ punar āgamanānubandham enāṃ visṛjet ||
children.translated_text: For without this, it cannot be done by any maiden other than you'; with a bond for returning again, he should let her go as she is departing.

children.text: asya ca yogasya trirātraṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ ca prayuktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the employment of this stratagem is for three nights and at the three twilights.
And when she has come for the sake of frequent seeing, he should extend the conversation.

children.text: anyābhir api saha viśvāsanārtham adhikam adhikaṃ cābhiyuñjīta
children.translated_text: Even with other women, for the sake of winning confidence, he should court her more and more,
but he should not make a verbal declaration.

children.text: dūragatabhāvo 'pi hi kanyāsu na nirvedena sidhyatīti ghoṭakamukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For even a feeling that has gone far in maidens is not accomplished by blunt declaration, so says <s>Ghoṭakamukha</s>.
But when he thinks her to be quite ready, then he should begin.

children.text: pradoṣe niśi tamasi ca yoṣito mandasādhvasāḥ suratavyavasāyinyo rāgavatyaśca bhavanti
children.translated_text: At twilight, at night, and in darkness women have little fear, are resolved on sexual pleasure, and are passionate,
and they do not reject a man.
Therefore that time should be employed: this is the common opinion.

children.text: ekapuruṣābhiyogānāṃ tvasaṃbhave gṛhītārthayā dhātreyikayā sakhyā vā tasyām antarbhūtayā tam artham anirvadantyā sahainām aṅkam ānāyayet
children.translated_text: But when courtship by one man is impossible, he should have her brought onto his lap together with a foster-nurse who has grasped the matter, or with a female friend included in her circle, without openly declaring that matter.
Then he should court her in the way stated.

children.text: svāṃ vā paricārikām ādāv eva sakhītvenāsyāḥ praṇidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or at the very beginning he should place his own maidservant near her as a friend.

children.text: yajñe vivāhe yātrāyām utsave vyasane prekṣaṇakavyāpṛte jane tatra tatra ca dṛṣṭeṅgitākārāṃ parīkṣitabhāvām ekākinīm upakrameta
children.translated_text: At a sacrifice, a wedding, a journey, a festival, a calamity, when people are occupied with a spectacle, and wherever he sees her alone after her gestures and outward signs have been seen and her feeling tested, he should begin.

children.text: na hi dṛṣṭabhāvā yoṣito deśe kāle ca prayujyamānā vyāvartanta iti vātsyāyanaḥ
children.translated_text: For women whose feeling has been seen do not turn away when approached in the right place and time, so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Thus end the approaches by one man.

children.text: mandāpadeśā guṇavatyapi kanyā dhanahīnā kulīnāpi samānair ayācyāmānā mātāpitṛviyuktā vā jñātikulavartinī vā prāptayauvanā pāṇigrahaṇaṃ svayam abhīpseta ||
children.translated_text: A maiden with a weak pretext, even if virtuous, poor though of good family, not being asked for by equals, or deprived of mother and father, or living in the family of her kinsmen, having reached youth, may herself desire taking of the hand in marriage.

children.text: sā tu guṇavantaṃ śaktaṃ sudarśanaṃ bālaprītyābhiyojayet ||
children.translated_text: But she should, through childhood affection, court a man who is virtuous, capable, and handsome.

children.text: yaṃ vā manyeta mātāpitror asamīkṣayā svayam apyayam indriyadaurbalyān mayi pravartiṣyata iti priyahitopacārair abhīkṣṇasaṃdarśanena ca tam āvarjayet ||
children.translated_text: Or, if she thinks, 'Even without the examination of his mother and father, this man himself, through weakness of the senses, will turn toward me,' she should win him over by affectionate and beneficial attentions and by frequent meetings.

children.text: mātā caināṃ sakhībhir dhātreyikābhiśca saha tadabhimukhīṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: And her mother, together with her friends and foster-companions, should make her face toward him.
There should be attendance upon him in a secluded place and at an irregular time, when she has flowers, perfumes, and betel in her hand.

children.text: kalākauśalaprakāśane vā saṃvāhane śirasaḥ pīḍane caucityadarśanam
children.translated_text: Or, in displaying skill in the arts, in massage, and in pressing his head, she should show what is proper.

children.text: prayojyasya sātmyayuktāḥ kathāyogāḥ bālāyām upakrameṣu yathoktam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: For the man to be worked upon, there should be conversational approaches suited to his taste; in approaches to a young girl one should act as stated before.
But even in private she should not herself solicit the man.

children.text: svayam abhiyoginī hi yuvatiḥ saubhāgyaṃ jahātītyācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the teachers say that a young woman who solicits on her own abandons her good fortune.
But she may receive favorably solicitations set in motion by him.
And when embraced, she should not show alteration.
She should receive his smooth approach as though she did not understand it.
When he takes hold of her face, the act is to be by force.
When she is being entreated for the experience of pleasure, touching the private parts should occur only with difficulty.
Even when entreated, she herself should not be too open.
Except at a time of uncertainty.

children.text: yadā tu manyetānurakto mayi na vyāvartiṣyata iti tadaivainam abhiyuñjānaṃ bālabhāvamokṣāya tvarayet
children.translated_text: But when she thinks, 'He is attached to me and will not turn away,' then, as he solicits her, she should hasten him toward the release from girlhood.
And, once freed from maidenhood, she should disclose it among trusted people.
Thus ends the winning over of the man to be worked upon.
But a maiden who is being courted should accept the man whom she considers a happy support,

children.text: anukūlaṃ ca vaśyaṃ ca tasya kuryāt parigraham ||
children.translated_text: favorable and controllable.

children.text: anapekṣya guṇān yatra rūpamaucityam eva ca
children.translated_text: Where, disregarding qualities, there is only beauty and social fitness,
she would, out of greed for wealth, make a man her husband even among co-wives.
In that matter, when a suitor endowed with suitable qualities, controllable, capable, strong, and deeply desirous
courts her by means, a maiden should not reject him.
Better a controllable poor man, even without virtues, who can support himself,

children.text: guṇair yukto 'pi na tv evaṃ bahusādhāraṇaḥ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: than a husband common to many, even if endowed with virtues.
For the most part the wives of wealthy men are many and unrestrained;
even when there is external enjoyment, they lack confidence and have happiness outside.
But a low man who courts her, or one who is gray-haired,
or one whose habit is going abroad, is not worthy of union.
One who courts by chance, or one much given to deceit and gambling,

children.text: sapatnīkaśca sāpatyo na sa saṃyogam arhati ||
children.translated_text: or one who already has a wife and children, is not worthy of union.
When the suitors are equal in qualities, the one who asks for her is the better choice;
in that case superiority belongs to the suitor, for he is characterized by attachment.

children.text: prācuryeṇa kanyāyā viviktadarśanasyālābhe dhātreyikāṃ priyahitābhyām upagṛhyopasarpet ||
children.translated_text: Since generally there is no chance for a private meeting with the maiden, he should approach by winning over the nurse's daughter with affection and benefit.

children.text: sā cainām aviditā nāma nāyakasya bhūtvā tadguṇair anurañjayet
children.translated_text: And she, becoming as if not known as the hero's agent, should charm the maiden with his qualities.
According to the maiden's liking, she should describe the hero's qualities at greatest length.
She should point out faults, contrary to the maiden's intentions, in other suitors and in their fathers.

children.text: mātāpitrośca guṇān abhijñatāṃ lubdhatāṃ ca capalatāṃ ca bāndhavānām
children.translated_text: She should mention the qualities and discernment of the maiden's mother and father, and also the greed and fickleness of her relatives.

children.text: yāścānyā api samānajātīyāḥ kanyāḥ śakuntalādyāḥ svabuddhyā bhartāraṃ prāpya samprayuktā modante sma tāścāsyā nidarśayet
children.translated_text: She should show her examples of other maidens of the same kind, such as <s>Śakuntalā</s>, who obtained husbands by their own intelligence and, being united with them, rejoiced.

children.text: mahākuleṣu sāpatnakair bādhyamānā vidviṣṭā duḥkhitāḥ parityaktāśca dṛśyante
children.translated_text: Women in great families are seen oppressed by co-wives, hated, miserable, and abandoned.
And she should describe his future prospects.

children.text: sukham anupahatam ekacāritāyāṃ nāyikānurāgaṃ ca varṇayet
children.translated_text: She should describe the unhindered happiness of being the only wife and the hero's attachment to the heroine.

children.text: samanorathāyāś cāsyā apāyaṃ sādhvasaṃ vrīḍāṃ ca hetubhir avacchindyāt
children.translated_text: And for her, who has the same desire, she should cut off danger, fear, and shame by means of reasons.
And she should carry out the entire procedure of a female messenger.

children.text: tvām ajānatīm iva nāyako balād grahīṣyatīti tathā suparigṛhītaṃ syād iti yojayet ||
children.translated_text: She should arrange it thus: 'The hero will seize you by force as if you did not know; in that way it will be well accomplished.'

children.text: pratipannām abhipretāvakāśavartinīṃ nāyakaḥ śrotriyāgārād agnim ānāyya kuśān āstīrya yathāsmṛti hutvā ca triḥ parikramet
children.translated_text: When she has consented and is in the desired opportunity, the hero should bring fire from the house of a <s>śrotriya</s>, spread <s>kuśa</s> grass, offer oblations according to memory, and circumambulate three times.
Then he should make it known to her mother and father.

children.text: agnisākṣikā hi vivāhā na nivartanta ityācāryasamayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For marriages witnessed by fire are not annulled; this is the convention of the teachers.
And after compromising her, he should gradually make it known among his own people.

children.text: tadbāndhavāśca yathā kulasyādhaṃ pariharanto daṇḍabhayācca tasmā evaināṃ dadyustathā yojayet
children.translated_text: And he should arrange matters so that her relatives, avoiding the lowering of the family and fearing punishment, would give her to him alone.

children.text: anantaraṃ ca prītyupagraheṇa rāgeṇa tadbāndhavān prīṇayed iti
children.translated_text: Immediately afterward, with affectionate favor and passion, he should please her relatives; thus.
Or he should proceed by a <s>gāndharva</s> marriage.

children.text: apratipadyamānāyām antaścāriṇīm anyāṃ kulapramadāṃ pūrvasaṃsṛṣṭāṃ prīyamāṇāṃ copagṛhya tayā saha viṣahyam avakāśam enām anyakāryāpadeśenānāyayet
children.translated_text: If she does not consent, he should win over another woman moving inside the household, a woman of good family formerly associated with her and fond of him, and with her, at a feasible opportunity, bring the maiden there under the pretext of another matter.

children.text: tataḥ śrotriyāgārād agnim iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: Then the instruction beginning 'fire from the house of a <s>śrotriya</s>' is the same as before.

children.text: āsanne ca vivāhe mātaram asyāstad abhimatadoṣair anuśayaṃ grāhayet
children.translated_text: And when her marriage is near, he should make her mother feel regret by pointing out faults in the man intended by her.

children.text: tatastadanumatena prātiveśyābhavane niśi nāyakam ānāyya śrotriyāgārād agnim iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: Then, with her consent, having brought the hero by night to a neighbor's house, the instruction beginning 'fire from the house of a <s>śrotriya</s>' is the same as before.

children.text: bhrātaram asyā vā samānavayasaṃ veśyāsu parastrīṣu vā prasaktam asukareṇa sāhāyadānena priyopagrahaiśca sudīrghakālam anurañjayet
children.translated_text: Or he should win over for a very long time her brother of the same age, if he is attached to courtesans or to other men's wives, by giving help in a difficult matter and by affectionate favors.
At the end he should make him understand his own intention.

children.text: prāyeṇa hi yuvānaḥ samānaśīlavyasanavayasāṃ vayasyānām arthe jīvitam api tyajanti
children.translated_text: For generally young men will give up even their lives for the sake of friends equal in character, vice, and age.
Then, through that very same woman, he should have her brought on some other pretext.
The statement that she is vulnerable and that there is an opportunity is the same as before.

children.text: aṣṭamīcandrikādiṣu ca dhātreyikā madanīyam enāṃ pāyayitvā kiṃcid ātmanaḥ kāryam uddiśya nāyakasya viṣahyaṃ deśam ānayet
children.translated_text: And on occasions such as the eighth-night moonlight festival, the <s>dhātreyikā</s> (nurse's daughter or attendant) should make her drink something intoxicating and, on the pretext of some business of her own, bring her to a place where the hero can overpower her.

children.text: tatraināṃ madāt saṃjñām apratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitveti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: There, while she is not aware of herself because of intoxication, he should violate her; this is the same as before.

children.text: suptāṃ caikacāriṇīṃ dhātreyikāṃ vārayitvā saṃjñām apratipadyamānāṃ dūṣayitveti samānaṃ pūrveṇa ||
children.translated_text: Or, having sent away the <s>dhātreyikā</s>, he should violate her when she is asleep, alone, and not aware of herself; this is the same as before.

children.text: grāmāntaram udyānaṃ vā gacchantīṃ viditvā susaṃbhṛtasahāyo nāyakastadā rakṣiṇo vitrāsya hatvā vā kanyām apaharet
children.translated_text: Knowing that she is going to another village or to a garden, the hero, with helpers well prepared, should frighten or kill her guards and carry off the maiden.
These are the means for marriage.

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ pradhānaṃ syād vivāho dharmataḥ sthiteḥ
children.translated_text: Of marriages established according to <s>dharma</s> (religious norm), each earlier one is more authoritative than the one after it;

children.text: pūrvābhāve tataḥ kāryo yo ya uttara uttaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when an earlier one is absent, then each later one should be performed in order.

children.text: vyūḍhānāṃ hi vivāhānām anurāgaḥ phalaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: For affection is the fruit of marriages when they have been duly arranged;
therefore even the middle and suitable form, the <s>gāndharva</s> marriage, is honored.
Because it is pleasant, involves little trouble, and here has no obstruction,
and because it consists in affection, the <s>gāndharva</s> marriage is considered the best.

children.text: bhāryaikacāriṇī gūḍhaviśrambhā devavat patim ānukūlyena varteta ||
children.translated_text: A wife devoted to one husband, with intimate trust kept private, should behave favorably toward her husband as toward a god.
In accordance with his opinion she should place the care of the household upon herself.

children.text: veśma ca śuci susaṃmṛṣṭasthānaṃ viracitavividhakusumaṃ ślakṣṇabhūmitalaṃ hṛdyadarśanaṃ triṣavaṇācaritabalikarma pūjitadevāyatanaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: She should make the house clean, with its places well swept, adorned with many kinds of flowers, its floor smooth, pleasing to look at, with offerings performed at the three daily times, and with the shrine of the deities honored.

children.text: na hyato 'nyad gṛhasthānāṃ cittagrāhakam astīti gonardīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For householders have nothing else so captivating to the mind as this, says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

children.text: guruṣu bhṛtyavargeṣu nāyakabhaginīṣu tatpatiṣu ca yathārhaṃ pratipattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Toward elders, the servant class, the hero's sisters, and their husbands, her conduct should be appropriate to each.
In purified places she should have beds of green vegetables made, along with sugarcane clumps and shrubs of cumin, mustard, ajamodā, śatapuṣpā, and tamāla.

children.text: kubjakāmalakamallikājātīkuraṇṭakanavamālikātagaranandyāvartajapāgulmān anyāṃśca bahupuṣpān bālakośīrakapātālikāṃśca vṛkṣavāṭikāyāṃ ca sthaṇḍilāni manojñāni kārayet ||
children.translated_text: In the tree garden she should have made attractive raised plots for kubjaka, āmalaka, mallikā, jātī, kuraṇṭaka, navamālikā, tagara, nandyāvarta, and japā shrubs, as well as other plants with many flowers, and for bālaka, uśīra, and pāṭalikā.

children.text: madhye kūpaṃ vāpīṃ dīrghikāṃ vā khānayet ||
children.translated_text: In the middle she should have a well, a reservoir, or a long pond dug.
She should not associate with female mendicants, wandering ascetics, Jain nuns, prostitutes, tricksters, fortune-tellers, or women who work with roots and charms.

children.text: bhojane ca rucitam idam asmai dveṣyam idaṃ pathyam idam apathyam idam iti ca vindyāt ||
children.translated_text: And in regard to food she should know, 'This is pleasing to him; this is hateful; this is wholesome; this is unwholesome.'

children.text: svaraṃ bahir upaśrutya bhavanam āgacchataḥ kiṃ kṛtyam iti bruvatī sajjā bhavanamadhye tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Hearing his voice outside as he comes home, she should stand ready inside the house, saying, 'What is to be done?'
Having sent away the maidservant, she should wash his feet herself.

children.text: nāyakasya ca na vimuktabhūṣaṇaṃ vijane saṃdarśane tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: And in a private meeting with the hero she should not appear with her ornaments removed.

children.text: ativyayam asadvyayaṃ vā kurvāṇaṃ rahasi bodhayet ||
children.translated_text: If he is spending excessively or spending improperly, she should admonish him in private.

children.text: āvāhe vivāhe yajñe gamanaṃ sakhībhiḥ saha goṣṭhīṃ devatābhigamanam ityanujñātā kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When permitted, she may go to bride-taking ceremonies, weddings, sacrifices, outings with female friends, assemblies, and visits to deities.
In all amusements her activity should be in conformity with him.

children.text: paścāt saṃveśanaṃ pūrvam utthānam anavabodhanaṃ ca suptasya ||
children.translated_text: She should go to bed after him, rise before him, and not wake him when he is asleep.

children.text: mahānasaṃ ca suguptaṃ syād darśanīyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The kitchen should be well guarded and also presentable.
When the hero commits offenses, she may be somewhat displeased, but should not reproach him too much.

children.text: sādhikṣepavacanaṃ tv enaṃ mitrajanamadhyastham ekākinaṃ vāpyupālabheta
children.translated_text: With reproachful speech, however, she may admonish him whether he is among friends or alone.
And she should not be a woman who works with roots and charms.
For there is no other cause of mistrust so great as this, says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

children.text: durvyāhṛtaṃ durnirīkṣitam anyato mantraṇaṃ dvāradeśāvasthānaṃ nirīkṣaṇaṃ vā niṣkuṭeṣu mantraṇaṃ vivikteṣu ciram avasthānam iti varjayet ||
children.translated_text: She should avoid ill-spoken words, improper glances, private consultation elsewhere, standing or looking at the doorway, consultation in enclosed yards, and staying long in secluded places.
She should be attentive to sweat, dirt on the teeth, and bad odors, for these are causes of loss of affection.

children.text: bahubhūṣaṇaṃ vividhakusumānulepanaṃ vividhāṅgarāgasamujjvalaṃ vāsa ityābhigāmiko veṣaḥ
children.translated_text: The dress for approaching him consists of many ornaments, various flowers and unguents, garments radiant with different body colors;

children.text: pratanuślakṣṇālpadukūlatā parimitam ābharaṇaṃ sugandhitā nātyulbaṇam anulepanam
children.translated_text: thin, smooth, light silk, limited ornaments, fragrance, and an unguent that is not too strong,
and likewise white and other flowers are the dress for recreation.

children.text: nāyakasya vratam upavāsaṃ ca svayam api karaṇenānuvarteta
children.translated_text: She should herself follow the hero's vow and fast by performing them too.

children.text: vāritāyāṃ ca nāham atra nirbandhanīyeti tadvacaso nivartanam ||
children.translated_text: And when she is restrained, she should turn back his words by saying, 'I should not be constrained in this matter.'
At the proper time she should buy earthen, wooden, leather, and metal vessels at a good price.

children.text: tathā lavaṇasnehayośca gandhadravyakaṭukabhāṇḍauṣadhānāṃ ca durlabhānāṃ bhavaneṣu pracchannaṃ nidhānam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise she should keep hidden stores in the house of salt and oils, fragrant substances, pungent goods, vessels, medicines, and things that are hard to obtain.

She should collect seeds, and sow at the proper time, of radish, āluka, pālaṅkī, damanaka, āmrātaka, ervāruka, trapusa, vārtāka, kūṣmāṇḍa, alābu, sūraṇa, śukanāsā, svayaṃguptā, tilaparṇikā, agnimantha, garlic, onion, and the like, and of all medicinal plants.

children.text: svasya ca sārasya parebhyo nākhyānaṃ bhartṛmantritasya ca ||
children.translated_text: She should not tell others about her own wealth or about what her husband has discussed in confidence.

children.text: samānāśca striyaḥ kauśalenojjvalatayā pākena mānena tathopacārair atiśayīta ||
children.translated_text: She should surpass women of equal standing by skill, brilliance, cooking, dignity, and forms of service.
Having calculated the yearly income, she should make expenditures in proportion to it.
From milk products left over from meals she should make ghee, and likewise manage oil and jaggery.
She should spin cotton into thread, and weave the thread.
the gathering of slings, ropes, nooses, and bark-fiber;
supervision of pounding and grinding;
the use of rinse-water, gruel-water, husks, broken grain, refuse, and charcoal;
knowledge of the wages and maintenance of servants;
the practical arrangements for agriculture, animal-keeping, planning, and transport;
supervision of sheep, cocks, quails, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, peacocks, monkeys, and deer;
and the reckoning of daily income and expenditure: this too she should know.

children.text: tajjaghanyānāṃ ca jīrṇavāsasāṃ saṃcayastair vividharāgaiḥ śuddhair vā kṛtakarmaṇāṃ paricārakāṇām anugraho mānārtheṣu ca dānam anyatra vopayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And for the lowest among them there should be an accumulation of old garments; by means of these, servants who have performed their work may be favored with garments variously dyed or clean, and gifts may be made to persons worthy of honor, or the garments may be used elsewhere.

children.text: surākumbhīnām āsavakumbhīnāṃ ca sthāpanaṃ tadupayogaḥ krayavikrayāv āyavyayāvekṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: There should be the storing of jars of liquor and jars of fermented drink, their use, their purchase and sale, and inspection of income and expenditure.
She should duly honor the hero's friends with garlands, unguents, and betel.

children.text: śvaśrūśvaśuraparicaryā tatpāratantryam anuttaravāditā parimitāpracaṇḍālāpakaraṇam anuccair hāsaḥ
children.translated_text: She should serve her mother-in-law and father-in-law, remain dependent on them, not answer back, keep her speech measured and not harsh, and not laugh loudly.
In enjoyments she should not be arrogant.
Toward the household staff she should be courteous.
Without informing the hero she should give nothing to anyone.

children.text: svakarmasu bhṛtyajananiyamanam utsaveṣu cāsya pūjanam ityekacāriṇīvṛttam ||
children.translated_text: She should regulate the servants in their own tasks and honor him at festivals: such is the conduct of a sole wife.

children.text: pravāse maṅgalamātrābharaṇā devatopavāsaparā vārtāyāṃ sthitā gṛhān avekṣeta ||
children.translated_text: When he is away, wearing only auspicious ornaments, devoted to the deities and to fasting vows, and waiting for news, she should watch over the house.
Her bed should be near the elders.
She should accomplish the tasks approved by him.

children.text: nāyakābhimatānāṃ cārthānām arjane pratisaṃskāre ca yatnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She should make effort in acquiring and repairing the things desired by the hero.
Expenditure should be recorded for regular and occasional rites.
Her mind should be set on completing works begun by him.
She should not go to her relatives' family except in distress or at a festival.

children.text: tatrāpi nāyakaparijanādhiṣṭhitāyā nātikālam avasthānam aparivartitapravāsaveṣatā ca ||
children.translated_text: Even there, she should stay only for a short time, attended by the hero's household staff, and should not change the dress proper to his absence.
She should perform fasts only when permitted by the elders.

children.text: paricārakaiḥ śucibhir ājñādhiṣṭhitair anumatena krayavikrayakarmaṇā sārasyāpūraṇaṃ tanūkaraṇaṃ ca śaktyā vyayānām ||
children.translated_text: Through clean servants acting under command, and by lawful buying and selling, she should replenish what is essential and reduce expenses as far as she can.

children.text: āgate ca prakṛtisthāyā eva prathamato darśanaṃ daivatapūjanam upahārāṇāṃ cāharaṇam iti pravāsacaryā ||
children.translated_text: And when he has returned, she should first appear just as she normally is, worship the deities, and bring offerings: such is the conduct during absence.
A woman who seeks the hero's welfare should follow good conduct,
whether she is a woman of good family, a remarried woman, a courtesan, or even a sole wife.

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ labhante sthānam eva ca
children.translated_text: Women who rely on good conduct obtain <s>dharma</s> (lawful propriety), wealth, and likewise pleasure,

children.text: niḥsapatnaṃ ca bhartāraṃ nāryaḥ sadvṛttam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as status and a husband without rivals.

children.text: jāḍyadauḥśīlyadaurbhāgyebhyaḥ prajānutpatter ābhīkṣṇyena dārikotpatter nāyakacāpalād vā sapatnyadhivedanam ||
children.translated_text: The taking of a co-wife occurs because of stupidity, bad character, ill fortune, failure to produce children, the frequent birth of daughters, or the hero's fickleness.
From the very beginning she should seek to avert that by displaying devotion, good character, and skill.

children.text: prajānutpattau ca svayam eva sāpatnake codayet ||
children.translated_text: And when there is no production of children, she herself should urge him toward taking a co-wife.

children.text: adhividyamānā ca yāvacchaktiyogād ātmano 'dhikatvena sthitiṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: When a co-wife is being installed, she should, by applying all her ability, cause her own position to be one of superiority.
She should regard the woman who has arrived as a sister.

children.text: nāyakaviditaṃ ca prādoṣikaṃ vidhim atīva yatnād asyāḥ kārayet saubhāgyajaṃ vaikṛtam utsekaṃ vāsyā nādriyeta ||
children.translated_text: With the hero's knowledge, she should very carefully have the evening routine performed for her; she should not heed any distortion or arrogance in her born of good fortune.
If the woman is negligent toward the husband, she should overlook it.

children.text: yatra manyetārtham iyaṃ svayam api pratipatsyata iti tatrainām ādarata evānuśiṣyāt ||
children.translated_text: Where she thinks, 'This one will understand the matter even by herself,' there she should instruct her respectfully.

children.text: nāyakasaṃśrave ca rahasi viśeṣān adhikān darśayet ||
children.translated_text: And in private intimacy with the hero she should show especially greater qualities.
Toward that woman's children there should be no distinction.
Toward the class of attendants there should be greater compassion.
Toward the circle of friends there should be affection.
Toward her own relatives there should not be excessive regard.
And toward that woman's relatives there should be very great respect.
But if she has been superseded by many women, she should associate with the one immediately next to her.

children.text: yāṃ tu nāyako 'dhikāṃ cikīrṣet tāṃ bhūtapūrvasubhagayā protsāhya kalahayet ||
children.translated_text: The one whom the hero wishes to make superior, she should incite a formerly favored woman against, and make them quarrel.
Then she should show sympathy.

children.text: tābhir ekatvenādhikāṃ cikīrṣitāṃ svayam avivadamānā durjanīkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Uniting with those women, while not herself quarreling, she should make the woman whom he wishes to make superior into an object of dislike.

children.text: nāyakena tu kalahitām enāṃ pakṣapātāvalambanopabṛṃhitām āśvāsayet ||
children.translated_text: But when that woman has quarreled with the hero, she should comfort her, strengthened by the support of taking her side.
And she should increase the quarrel.

children.text: mandaṃ vā kalaham upalabhya svayam eva saṃdhukṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Or, when she observes a slight quarrel, she should herself fan it.

children.text: yadi nāyako 'syām adyāpi sānunaya iti manyeta tadā svayam eva saṃdhau prayateteti jyeṣṭhāvṛttam ||
children.translated_text: If she thinks, 'The hero is still conciliatory toward her,' then she herself should work for reconciliation: such is the conduct of the senior wife.
The junior wife, however, should regard the co-wife as a mother.
She should not use even her own inheritance from relatives without that woman's knowledge.
She should make those who live from her own means subject to that woman's authority.
Having been permitted, she should sleep with her husband.

children.text: na vā tasyā vacanam anyasyāḥ kathayet ||
children.translated_text: Nor should she repeat that woman's words to anyone else.
She should regard that woman's children as superior to her own.
In secret she should attend to her husband especially well.
And she should not report her own distress arising from changes in the co-wife's behavior.
She should seek a secret, special favor from her husband.
She should say, 'Indeed, I live by this wholesome provision.'

children.text: tat tu ślāghayā rāgeṇa vā bahir nācakṣīta ||
children.translated_text: But she should not tell of it outside, whether out of praise or passion.
For a woman whose secret has been broken receives contempt from her husband.
And from fear of the senior wife she should desire hidden honor, says <s>Gonardīya</s>.

children.text: durbhagām anapatyāṃ ca jyeṣṭhām anukampeta nāyakena cānukampayet ||
children.translated_text: She should pity the senior wife who is unfortunate and childless, and cause the hero to pity her.

children.text: prasahya tv enām ekacāriṇīvṛttam anutiṣṭhed iti kaniṣṭhāvṛttam ||
children.translated_text: But even under constraint she should practice toward her the conduct of a sole wife: such is the conduct of the junior wife.

children.text: vidhavā tvindriyadaurbalyād āturā bhoginaṃ guṇasampannaṃ ca yā punar vindet sā punarbhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: But a widow who, distressed by weakness of the senses, again obtains a man who is enjoyable and possessed of good qualities is a <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman).

children.text: yatastu svecchayā punar api niṣkramaṇaṃ nirguṇo 'yam iti tadā anyaṃ kāṅkṣed iti bābhravīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since, however, if she again departs of her own will, thinking, "This man is without qualities," she may then desire another, so say the <s>Bābhravīyas</s>.
For the sake of happiness, she indeed may again obtain another man.

children.text: guṇeṣu sopabhogeṣu sukhasākalyaṃ tasmāt tato viśeṣa iti gonardīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the fullness of pleasure lies in qualities together with enjoyments, there is superiority on that account, says <s>Gonardīya</s>.
It is because of conformity to her own mind, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: sā bāndhavair nāyakād āpānakodyānaśraddhādānamitrapūjanādi vyayasahiṣṇu karma lipseta ||
children.translated_text: She should seek from the lover, through her kinsmen, actions involving expense, such as drinking parties, gardens, gifts to the pious, and honoring of friends.

children.text: ātmanaḥ sāreṇa vālaṃkāraṃ tadīyam ātmīyaṃ vā bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, according to her own means, she should wear ornaments belonging to him or belonging to herself.
There is no fixed rule in gifts of affection.

children.text: svecchayā ca gṛhān nirgacchantī prītidāyād anyan nāyakadattaṃ jīyeta
children.translated_text: And when leaving the house of her own will, she should forfeit what was given by the lover other than gifts of affection.
But if she is being expelled, she should give nothing at all.

children.text: sā prabhaviṣṇur iva tasya bhavanam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: She should enter his house as though she had authority.
But among women of good family she should behave with affection.

children.text: dākṣiṇyena parijane sarvatra saparihāsā mitreṣu pratipattiḥ
children.translated_text: Toward the attendants there should be kindness, and toward friends everywhere a manner joined with joking.
She should have skill in the arts and knowledge greater than others.
And in occasions for quarrel she should herself reproach the lover.
In private she should comply by means of the art of the sixty-four practices.
She herself should assist the co-wives.
She should give ornaments to their children.
Toward them she should show attention as toward her own master.
She should carefully make adornments and costumes.
She should give more liberally to the attendants and the circle of friends.
And she should have the habit of going to gatherings, drinking parties, gardens, journeys, and recreations. Thus is the conduct of the <s>punarbhū</s>.

children.text: durbhagā tu sāpatnakapīḍitā yā tāsām adhikam iva patyāvupacaret tām āśrayet
children.translated_text: But the unlucky woman, oppressed by co-wives, should attach herself to the one among them who seems to have greater influence over the husband.
She should display arts and kinds of knowledge that are to be shown openly.
Because of her misfortune there is no place for secrets.
She should act as a foster-nurse for the lover's children.

children.text: tanmitrāṇi copagṛhya tair bhaktim ātmanaḥ prakāśayet ||
children.translated_text: And having won over his friends, she should through them make her devotion evident.
She should be foremost in religious duties, and also in vows and fasts.
Toward the attendants she should show kindness.
And she should not regard herself as superior.
In bed, by accommodating herself to his habits, she should bring back his affection for her.

children.text: na copālabheta vāmatāṃ ca na darśayet ||
children.translated_text: And she should not reproach him, nor should she show perverseness.

children.text: yayā ca kalahitaḥ syāt kāmaṃ tām āvartayet ||
children.translated_text: If he has quarreled with some woman, she may, if she wishes, bring that woman back.

children.text: yāṃ ca pracchannāṃ kāmayet tām anena saha saṃgamayed gopayecca ||
children.translated_text: And if he secretly desires a woman, she should arrange a meeting between that woman and him and should keep it concealed.

children.text: yathā ca pativratātvam aśāṭhyaṃ nāyako manyeta tathā pratividadhyād iti durbhagāvṛttam ||
children.translated_text: She should act so that the lover thinks she is devoted to her husband and free from deceit. Thus is the conduct of the unlucky wife.

children.text: antaḥpurāṇāṃ ca vṛttam eteṣv eva prakaraṇeṣu lakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: And the conduct of the women of the inner palace should be recognized in these very topics.

children.text: mālyānulepanavāsāṃsi cāsāṃ kañcukīyā mahattarikā vā rājño nivedayeyur devībhiḥ prahitam iti
children.translated_text: The chamberlain or the senior woman should report to the king their garlands, unguents, and garments, saying, "These have been sent by the queens."

children.text: tadādāya rājā nirmālyam āsāṃ pratiprābhṛtakaṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: Having received them, the king should give them his used garlands as return gifts.
Then, adorned himself, he should in the afternoon see all the women of the inner palace, likewise adorned, gathered in one place.

children.text: tāsāṃ yathākālaṃ yathārhaṃ ca sthānamānānuvṛttiḥ saparihāsāśca kathāḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should treat each of them according to the proper time and according to her rank and honor, and should converse with them in a joking manner.
After that he should see the remarried women in the same way.
Then he should see the courtesans, the women of the inner apartments, and the actresses.
Their places should be in the ranks already described.

children.text: vāsakapālyastu yasyā vāsako yasyāścātīto yasyāśca ṛtustatparicārikānugatā divā śayyotthitasya rājñastābhyāṃ prahitam aṅgulīyakāṅkam anulepanam ṛtuṃ vāsakaṃ ca nivedayeyuḥ
children.translated_text: The attendants in charge of the sleeping turns should, during the day when the king has risen from bed, accompanied by the personal attendants of the woman whose turn it is, of the one whose turn has passed, and of the one who is in season, report the unguent marked with a ring sent by those two, and announce her season and her turn.

children.text: tatra rājā yad gṛhṇīyāt tasyā vāsakam ājñāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In that matter, whichever one the king accepts, he should order that woman's turn for cohabitation.

children.text: utsaveṣu ca sarvāsām anurūpeṇa pūjāpānakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: At festivals there should be appropriate honoring and drinking for all of them.
And likewise at musical performances.
Women who move within the inner palace should not go outside, and outside women should not enter.
Except for women whose purity is known.
And the execution of duties should be without harassment. Thus is the matter concerning the inner palace.
And here there are verses:

children.text: puruṣastu bahūn dārān samāhṛtya samo bhavet
children.translated_text: A man, having gathered many wives, should be impartial.

children.text: na cāvajñāṃ cared āsu vyalīkān na saheta ca ||
children.translated_text: He should not show contempt toward them, and he should not tolerate their deceits.

children.text: ekasyāṃ yā ratikrīḍā vaikṛtaṃ vā śarīrajam
children.translated_text: The erotic play with one woman, or some bodily peculiarity,
or even a reproach uttered in confidence, he should not recount among the others.

children.text: na dadyāt prasaraṃ strīṇāṃ sapatnyāḥ kāraṇe kvacit
children.translated_text: He should never give women free scope over the matter of a co-wife.
And when one is reproaching a co-wife, he should charge her herself with faults.
One woman he should delight in private by intimacies, another by public honors,
and another likewise by acts of high regard; in this way he should please the women.
By trips to gardens, enjoyments, gifts, and honoring their relatives,
and by secret acts of affection, he should delight each one separately.
And a young woman who has conquered anger and acts according to the treatise
brings her husband under her control and prevails over her co-wives.

children.text: strīpuruṣaśīlavasthāpanaṃ vyāvartanakāraṇāṇi strīṣu siddhāḥ puruṣā ayatnasādhyā yoṣitaḥ vyākhyātakāraṇāḥ paraparigrahopagamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The establishment of the dispositions of women and men, the causes for turning away, men who are successful with women, women who are attainable without effort, and the causes already explained for approaching another man's wife have been set forth.

children.text: teṣu sādhyatvam anatyayaṃ gamyatvam āyatiṃ vṛttiṃ cādita eva parīkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: With regard to these, at the very beginning one should examine attainability, absence of danger, approachability, future consequence, and livelihood.

children.text: yadā tu sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ kāmaṃ pratipadyamānaṃ paśyet tadātmaśarīropaghātatrāṇārthaṃ paraparigrahān abhyupagacchet ||
children.translated_text: But when he sees desire moving from one place to another, then, for the sake of protecting his own body from harm, he should consent to affairs with the wives of others.
Now there are ten places of desire.

children.text: cakṣuḥprītir manaḥsaṅgaḥ saṃkalpotpattir nidrācchedastanutā viṣayebhyo vyāvṛttir lajjāpraṇāśa unmādo mūrchā maraṇam iti teṣāṃ liṅgāni ||
children.translated_text: Delight in seeing, attachment of the mind, the arising of imagining, loss of sleep, emaciation, turning away from sense-objects, loss of shame, madness, fainting, and death: these are their signs.

children.text: tatrākṛtito lakṣaṇataśca yuvatyāḥ śīlaṃ satyaṃ śaucaṃ sādhyatāṃ caṇḍavegatāṃ ca lakṣayed ityācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this matter, from a young woman's form and from her marks one should observe her character, truthfulness, purity, attainability, and fierceness of passion, say the teachers.

children.text: vyabhicārād ākṛtilakṣaṇayogānām iṅgitākārābhyām eva pravṛttir boddhavyā yoṣita iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But because the conjunctions of form and marks are variable, a woman's disposition is to be understood only from gestures and outward behavior, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: yaṃ kaṃcid ujjvalaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā strī kāmayate
children.translated_text: On seeing any brilliant man, a woman desires him,
and likewise a man desires a woman;

children.text: apekṣayā tu na pravartata iti goṇikāputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: but because of considerations he does not proceed, says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.
In this matter there is a distinction with respect to a woman.

children.text: na strī dharmam adharmaṃ cāpekṣate kāmayata eva
children.translated_text: A woman does not consider <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>; she simply desires.
But with regard to the action to be done, she does not undertake it.
And by nature, when she is approached by a man, even though she wants to act, she turns away.
When approached again and again, she is won.

children.text: puruṣastu dharmasthitim āryasamayaṃ cāpekṣya kāmayamāno 'pi vyāvartate
children.translated_text: But a man, though desiring, turns away out of regard for the standing of <s>dharma</s> and the convention of respectable people.
And having such a state of mind, even when approached, he is not won.
He approaches without cause.
Even after approaching, he does not approach again.
And when she has been won, he becomes indifferent.
He despises one who is easily obtained.
He longs for one who is hard to obtain: this is the general rule.
In this matter the causes of turning away are:
attachment to the husband;
regard for children;
being past youth;
being overwhelmed by sorrow;
reproach connected with separation;
anger, thinking, 'He invites me with contempt';
abandonment of the intention, thinking, 'He is unpredictable';
lack of future prospect, thinking, 'He will go away,' and, 'His mind is attached elsewhere';
agitation, thinking, 'His behavior is unconcealed';
regard for friends, thinking, 'His feelings are entrusted to his friends';
suspicion, thinking, 'He is a dry suitor';
nervous fear, thinking, 'He is forceful';
fear in a deer-like woman, thinking, 'He is fierce in passion, or too capable';
shame, thinking, 'He is a man-about-town, skilled in the arts';
and because he has been treated as a friend;
resentment, thinking, 'He does not know the proper place and time';
lack of respect, thinking, 'He is a source of humiliation';
contempt, thinking, 'Even when signaled, he does not understand';
in an elephant-like woman, thinking, 'He is a hare and slow in passion';
compassion, thinking, 'Let no misfortune come to him from me';
disgust through seeing faults in herself;
fear, thinking, 'If I am discovered, I shall be cast out by my own people';
disregard, thinking, 'He is gray-haired';
reflection, thinking, 'He has been sent by my husband and is testing me';
and regard for <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: teṣu yadātmani lakṣayet tadādita eva paricchindyāt ||
children.translated_text: Among these, whichever cause he observes as applying to himself, he should cut it off from the very beginning.
Those connected with respectability are removed by increasing passion;
those born from incapacity, by showing expedients;
those caused by respect, by excessive familiarity;
those caused by humiliation, by excessive gallantry and cleverness;
those born from contempt for him, by submission;
those connected with fear, by reassurance.
But the following men are generally successful:
one who knows the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>;

children.text: kathākhyānakuśalo bālyāt prabhṛti saṃsṛṣṭaḥ pravṛddhayauvanaḥ krīḍanakarmādināgataviśvāsaḥ preṣaṇasya kartocitasaṃbhāṣaṇaḥ priyasya kartānyasya bhūtapūrvo dūto marmajña uttamayā prārthitaḥ sakhyā pracchannaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaḥ subhagābhikhyātaḥ saha saṃvṛddhaḥ prātiveśyaḥ kāmaśīlastathābhūtaś ca paricāriko dhātreyikāparigraho navavarakaḥ prekṣodyānatyāgaśīlo vṛṣa iti siddhapratāpaḥ sāhasikaḥ śūro vidyārūpaguṇopabhogaiḥ patyur atiśayitā mahārhaveṣopacāraśceti ||
children.translated_text: one skilled in telling stories; one associated with her from childhood onward; one whose youth is fully grown; one in whom confidence has come through play and other activities; one who performs errands; one who converses suitably; one who does what is pleasing; one who has previously been another's messenger; one who knows her vulnerable points; one sought by a high-ranking woman; one secretly associated with her friend; one reputed to be fortunate; one who grew up together with her; a neighbor; one whose nature is erotic; a servant of such a kind; one connected with the nurse's daughter; a newly chosen bridegroom; one whose habit is shows, gardens, and generosity; one renowned for proven potency as a bull; one who is daring; one who is brave; one who surpasses the husband in learning, beauty, virtues, and enjoyments; and one who has costly dress and attentions.
Just as he should see his own likelihood of success, so also that of the woman.
The women who can be won without effort are these:
those to be won by mere approach;
one who stays at the doorway;
one who looks from a palace onto the royal road;
one who arranges gatherings in the house of a young neighbor;
one who constantly gazes;
one who, when gazed at, looks sideways;
one who for no reason has been superseded by a co-wife;
one who hates her husband and is hated by him;
one without protection or means of avoidance;
one without children;
one who is always at her relatives' house;
one whose child has died;
one who arranges gatherings;
one who arranges affection;
the wife of an actor;
a young woman whose husband is dead;
one who is poor and has had many enjoyments;
an eldest wife with many brothers-in-law;
one who thinks highly of herself and has an inferior husband;
one proud of her skill and distressed by her husband's stupidity;
one who, through greed, makes no distinction;

children.text: kanyākāle yatnena varitā kathaṃcid alabdhābhiyuktā ca sā tadānīṃ samānabuddhiśīlamedhāpratipattisātmyā
children.translated_text: one who in maidenhood was carefully sought but somehow not obtained, and who, when approached, now has the same mind, character, intelligence, judgment, and habitual disposition;
one naturally partial;
one insulted without offense;
one put down by women equal to her in beauty;
one whose husband is abroad;
and the wives of men who are jealous, foul, over-fastidious, impotent, procrastinating, unmanly, hunchbacked, dwarf, deformed, jewel-makers, rustic, foul-smelling, diseased, or old.
Here are verses on this:
Desire born by nature and increased by action,
with its agitation purified by understanding, becomes firm and unfailing.
Knowing his own likelihood of success and inferring the signs of women,
a man who cuts off the causes of withdrawal succeeds with women.

children.text: yathā kanyā svayam abhiyogasādhyā na tathā dūtyā
children.translated_text: A maiden can be won by personal approach, not in the same way by a female messenger;
but other men's wives, subtle in feeling, can be won by female messengers, not so much by oneself, say the teachers.

children.text: sarvatra śaktiviṣaye svayaṃ sādhanam upapannatarakaṃ durupapādatvāt tasya dūtīprayoga iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In every case, when the matter lies within his own capacity, accomplishing it himself is more fitting, because the use of a female messenger is difficult to carry out; so says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Women who are bold at the outset and unrestrained in conversation should be won over by oneself.
Those who are the opposite should be won through a female messenger; this is the general rule.

children.text: svayam abhiyokṣyamāṇastv ādāv eva paricayaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: But one who intends to court her himself should make an acquaintance at the very beginning.
The seeing of her is of two kinds: natural and contrived.

It is natural when she is near his own house; it is contrived when she is near the houses of friends, relatives, ministers, or physicians, or at weddings, sacrifices, festivals, misfortunes, trips to gardens, and the like.

children.text: darśane cāsyāḥ satataṃ sākāraṃ prekṣaṇaṃ keśasaṃyamanaṃ nakhāchuraṇam ābharaṇaprahlādanam adharaoṣṭhavimardanaṃ tāstāśca līlā vayasyaiḥ saha prekṣamāṇāyās tatsambaddhāḥ parāpadeśinyaśca kathāstyāgopabhogaprakāśanaṃ sakhyur utsaṅganiṣaṇṇasya sāṅgabhaṅgaṃ jṛmbhaṇam ekabhrūkṣepaṇaṃ mandavākyatā tadvākyaśravaṇaṃ tām uddiśya bālenānyajanena vā sahānyopadiṣṭā dvyarthā kathā tasyāṃ svayaṃ manorathāvedanam anyāpadeśena tām evoddiśya bālacumbanam āliṅganaṃ ca jihvayā cāsya tāmbūladānaṃ pradeśinyā hanudeśaghaṭṭanaṃ tat tad yathāyogaṃ yathāvakāśaṃ ca prayoktavyam
children.translated_text: When seeing her, he should constantly look at her with meaningful signs: arranging his hair, scratching with his nails, making his ornaments sound, rubbing his lower lip, and performing various playful gestures. While she is looking on, he should tell stories with his friends that are connected with her or refer to her under another name, display his generosity and enjoyment, yawn with a stretching of the limbs while a friend sits in his lap, raise one eyebrow, speak softly, listen to her words, and, with a child or another person, utter equivocal speech taught as if directed elsewhere but really aimed at her. Indirectly he should make known his own desire for her; as if referring to her, he should kiss and embrace a child, give him betel with his tongue, and touch his chin with his forefinger. Each of these should be used according to what is suitable and according to the occasion.

children.text: tasyāścāṅkagatasya bālasya lālanaṃ bālakrīḍanakānāṃ cāsya dānaṃ grahaṇaṃ tena saṃnikṛṣṭatvāt kathāyojanaṃ tatsaṃbhāṣaṇakṣameṇa janena ca prītim āsādya kāryaṃ tadanubandhaṃ ca gamanāgamanasya yojanaṃ saṃśraye cāsyāstām apaśyato nāma kāmasūtrasaṃkathā ||
children.translated_text: He should also caress a child sitting in her lap, give and receive the child's toys, and, because of the closeness produced through him, arrange conversation. After gaining affection through someone able to converse with her, he should arrange the matter to be done and its continuation, and should arrange coming and going. When he is near her but does not see her, there should be conversation called discussion of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>.

children.text: prasṛte tu paricaye tasyā haste nyāsaṃ nikṣepaṃ ca nidadhyāt
children.translated_text: When the acquaintance has grown, he should place a pledge and deposit in her hand.
He should take it back every day and at every moment, a little at a time.
Also perfumes and areca nuts.

children.text: tām ātmano dāraiḥ saha visrambhagoṣṭhyāṃ viviktāsane ca yojayet nityadarśanārthaṃ viśvāsanārthaṃ ca
children.translated_text: He should bring her together with his wives in confidential conversation and on a secluded seat, for the sake of seeing her constantly and gaining her trust.

children.text: suvarṇakāramaṇikāravaikaṭikanīlīkusumbharañjakādiṣu ca kāmārthinyāṃ sahātmano vaśyaiścaiṣāṃ tatsaṃpādane svayaṃ prayateta
children.translated_text: If she has some desire involving goldsmiths, jewelers, lapidaries, dyers in indigo or safflower, and the like, he himself, along with those of them who are under his control, should try to procure it.
For one occupied with carrying this out, there is a publicly known occasion for seeing her over a long time.
And in that situation other tasks too may be connected with it.

children.text: yena karmaṇā dravyeṇa kauśalena cārthinī syāt tasya prayogam utpattim āgamam upāyaṃ vijñānaṃ cātmāyattaṃ darśayet
children.translated_text: Whatever work, object, or skill she desires, he should show that its use, production, acquisition, means, and knowledge depend upon himself.

children.text: pūrvapravṛtteṣu lokacariteṣu dravyaguṇaparīkṣāsu ca tayā tatparijanena ca saha vivādaḥ
children.translated_text: In matters already begun, in common social practices, and in the testing of the qualities of goods, there should be discussion with her and with her attendants.

children.text: tatra nirdiṣṭāni paṇitāni teṣv enāṃ prāśnikatvena yojayet
children.translated_text: There, after he has specified and staked the items, he should appoint her as judge among them.

children.text: tayā tu vivadamāno 'tyantādbhutam iti brūyād iti paricayakāraṇāni ||
children.translated_text: But while disputing with her, he should say, "This is utterly astonishing." Such are the means of making acquaintance.
A woman with whom acquaintance has been made and to whom his gestures and signs have been shown should be courted by stratagem, like a maiden.
In that case the approaches are generally subtle.
Because maidens have not had sexual experience.
With other women, he should apply those same approaches plainly.
Because they have had sexual experience.
When she has shown signs and her true feeling has been opened up, then at the occasion of mutual enjoyment he should make use of things belonging to her.

children.text: tatra mahārhagandham uttarīyaṃ kusumaṃ ca ātmīyaṃ syād aṅgulīyakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Among these should be his own costly perfume, upper garment, flower, and ring.
When he is ready to go to a gathering, after taking betel from her hand, he should ask for a flower from her hair or hand.

children.text: tatra mahārhagandhaṃ spṛhaṇīyaṃ svanakhadaśanapadacihnitaṃ sākāraṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: There he should give her a costly and desirable perfume, visibly marked with the traces of his own nails and teeth.
By stronger and stronger approaches he should break off her timidity.

children.text: krameṇa ca viviktadeśe gamanam āliṅganaṃ cumbanaṃ tāmbūlasya grāhaṇaṃ dānānte dravyāṇāṃ parivartanaṃ guhyadeśābhimarśanaṃ cetyabhiyogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And, gradually, the approaches are going to a secluded place, embracing, kissing, making her take betel, exchanging objects after a gift has been given, and touching the secret parts.
Where one woman has been approached, he should not approach another there.

children.text: tatra yā vṛddhānubhūtaviṣayā priyopagrahaiśca tām upagṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: There he should favor the woman who is experienced in such matters and responsive to loving attentions.
Here there are verses:
Where her husband has observed his movements elsewhere and is a leading man,

children.text: na tatra yoṣitaṃ kāṃcit suprāpām api laṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: there he should not transgress with any woman, even one who is very easy to obtain.

children.text: śaṅkitāṃ rakṣitāṃ bhītāṃ saśvaśrūkāṃ ca yoṣitam ||
children.translated_text: A woman who is suspected, guarded, frightened, or accompanied by her mother-in-law,

children.text: na tarkayeta medhāvī jānan pratyayam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a wise man should not try to judge, even if he knows his own grounds for confidence.
When courting women, he should examine their inclination.
Through that, her feeling has been examined.
And he should receive the responses to his advances.
A woman who does not open herself to confidential speech he should win through a female messenger.

children.text: apratigṛhyābhiyogaṃ punar api saṃsṛjyamānāṃ dvidhā bhūtamānasāṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: If, after not accepting an advance, she again associates with him, he should know that her mind is divided.
He should win her gradually.

children.text: apratigṛhyābhiyogaṃ saviśeṣam alaṃkṛtā ca punar dṛśyeta tathaiva tam abhigacchecca vivikte balād grahaṇīyāṃ vidyāt ||
children.translated_text: If, after not accepting an advance, she appears again especially adorned and approaches him in the same way, he should know that in a secluded place she is to be seized by force.

children.text: bahūn api viṣahate abhiyogān na ca cireṇāpi prayacchatyātmānaṃ sā śuṣkapratigrāhiṇī paricayavighaṭanasādhyā ||
children.translated_text: If she endures many advances but does not give herself even after a long time, she is a dry receiver; she can be won by breaking off the acquaintance.
Because the mind of human nature is inconstant.
Though approached, she avoids him,
and she does not associate with him.
And she does not reject him.
This is because of her proud sense of regard for him and for herself.
Because of excessive familiarity, she is difficult to win.
One should win her through a go-between who knows her vulnerable points.
If, when she is approached, she rejects him with harshness, she should be disregarded.
But even after she has spoken harshly, he should win her if she can be joined to him by affection.

children.text: kāraṇāt saṃsparśanaṃ sahate nāvabudhyate nāma dvidhābhūtamānasā sātatyena kṣāntyā vā sādhyā
children.translated_text: If for some reason she endures touching and, as it were, does not notice it, since her mind is divided, she can be won by persistence or by patience.

children.text: samīpe śayānāyāḥ supto nāma karam upari vinyaset
children.translated_text: When she is lying nearby, he should, as if asleep, place his hand upon her.
She too, as if asleep, overlooks it.
But if, while awake, she pushes it away, she is desiring a further approach.
By this, placing one's foot upon her foot is also explained.
When that has been allowed to proceed, he should again begin an embrace as if in sleep.

children.text: tadasahamānām utthitāṃ dvitīye ahani prakṛtivartinīm abhiyogārthinīṃ vidyāt
children.translated_text: If she cannot endure it and gets up, but on the second day behaves naturally, he should know that she wants to be approached.
But if she does not show herself, she is to be won through a go-between.

children.text: ciram adṛṣṭāpi prakṛtisthaiva saṃsṛjyate kṛtalakṣaṇāṃ tāṃ darśitākārām upakramet ||
children.translated_text: Even if she has not been seen for a long time, if she associates with him just as before, he should approach her once she has made signs and shown indications.
Even when she has not been approached, she gives indications.
And in a secluded place she shows herself.
She speaks with trembling and a choked voice.
Her fingers and toes are moist with sweat, and her face is moist too.

children.text: śiraḥpīḍane saṃvāhane corvor ātmānaṃ nāyake niyojayati
children.translated_text: In head-pressing and in massaging the thighs, she places herself at the hero's disposal.

children.text: āturā saṃvāhikā caikena hastena saṃvāhayantī dvitīyena bāhunā sparśam āvedayati śleṣayati ca
children.translated_text: When she is ill, or when she is acting as masseuse, while massaging with one hand she makes contact known with the other arm and embraces him.
She has an expression of surprise.

children.text: nidrāndhā vā parispṛśyorubhyāṃ bāhubhyām api tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Or, as if blind with sleep, after touching him she remains there with her thighs and even with her arms.
She lets part of her forehead fall upon his thighs.
When assigned to massage the roots of the thighs, she does not resist.
Right there she places one hand motionless.
And when pressed by the clasp of the limbs, she removes it only after a long time.

children.text: pratigṛhyaivaṃ nāyakābhiyogān punar dvitīye ahani saṃvāhanāyopagacchati
children.translated_text: Having accepted the hero's approaches in this way, she comes again on the second day for massage.
She does not associate with him too much.
Nor does she avoid him.

children.text: vivikte bhāvaṃ darśayati niṣkāraṇaṃ cāgūḍham anyatra pracchannapradeśāt
children.translated_text: In seclusion she shows her feeling, and without cause she shows it openly, except in a hidden place.

children.text: saṃnikṛṣṭaparicārakopabhogyā sā ced ākāritāpi tathaiva syāt sā marmajñayā dūtyā sādhyā
children.translated_text: If, being accessible to nearby attendants, she remains just so even when signaled, she should be won through a go-between who knows her vulnerable points.
But if she turns away, she is to be regarded with suspicion. Thus ends the testing of feeling.
And here there are verses:
At first he should make acquaintance, and then conversation;
mixed with conversation there should be mutual revealing of signs.
If, through her reply, he sees that the sign has been accepted,
then the man, free from fear, should approach the woman.

children.text: ākāreṇātmano bhāvaṃ yā nārī prāk prayojayet
children.translated_text: The woman who first sets forth her own feeling by a sign

children.text: kṣipram evābhiyojyā sā prathame tv eva darśane ||
children.translated_text: should be approached quickly, even at the very first sight.

children.text: ślakṣṇam ākāritā yā tu darśayet sphuṭam uttaram
children.translated_text: But she who, when gently signaled, shows a clear response
should also be known as attainable at that very moment, being eager for love.
For a steadfast woman, one who is not bold, and one who tests him,

children.text: eṣa sūkṣmo vidhiḥ proktaḥ siddhā eva sphuṭaṃ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this subtle method has been taught; women who are explicit are already won.

children.text: darśiteṅgitākārāṃ tu praviraladarśanām apūrvāṃ ca dūtyopasarpayet
children.translated_text: But a woman who has shown gestures and signs, who is rarely seen, or who is unfamiliar, he should approach through a go-between.

children.text: saināṃ śīlato 'nupraviśyākhyānakapaṭaiḥ subhagaṃkaraṇayogair lokavṛttāntaiḥ kavikathābhiḥ pāradārikakathābhiśca tasyāśca rūpavijñānadākṣiṇyaśīlānupraśaṃsābhiśca tāṃ rañjayet
children.translated_text: Entering into her character, the go-between should please her with fabricated stories, methods for making one fortunate in love, reports of the world, tales of poets, stories of adulterous love, and praises of her beauty, intelligence, cleverness, and character.

children.text: katham evaṃvidhāyāstavāyam itthaṃbhūtaḥ patiriti cānuśayaṃ grāhayet
children.translated_text: She should make her feel regret, saying, 'How can someone like you have such a husband as this?'

children.text: na tava subhage dāsyam api kartuṃ yukta iti brūyāt
children.translated_text: She should say, 'Fortunate lady, it is not fitting for you even to serve him as a slave.'

children.text: mandavegatām īrṣyālutāṃ śaṭhatām akṛtajñatāṃ cāsaṃbhogaśīlatāṃ kadaryatāṃ capalatām anyāni ca yāni tasmin guptānyasyā abhyāśe sati sadbhāve atiśayena bhāṣeta
children.translated_text: In her presence, when goodwill has arisen, she should speak at length of the faults hidden in him: dull passion, jealousy, deceitfulness, ingratitude, lack of inclination for intercourse, stinginess, fickleness, and whatever else there is.
And by whichever fault she observes that the woman is distressed, by that very fault she should make her entrance.
When she is a <s>mṛgī</s> (doe-type woman), then his being a <s>śaśa</s> (hare-type man) is certainly no fault.
By this same rule, the cases of the <s>vaḍavā</s> (mare-type woman) and the <s>hastinī</s> (elephant-type woman) have also been stated.

children.text: nāyikāyā eva tu viśvāsyatām upalabhya dūtītvenopasarpayet prathamasāhasāyāṃ sūkṣmabhāvāyāṃ ceti goṇikāputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But only after discovering that the heroine herself is trustworthy should one approach her through the office of a go-between, in the case of a first bold attempt and of a woman whose feelings are subtle, says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.

children.text: sā nāyakasya caritam anulomatāṃ kāmitāni ca kathayet
children.translated_text: She should tell of the hero's conduct, his favorable disposition, and his desires.

children.text: prasṛtasadbhāvāyāṃ ca yuktyā kāryaśarīram itthaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: And when goodwill has spread, she should state the substance of the matter by a stratagem, saying this:

children.text: śṛṇu vicitram idaṃ subhage tvāṃ kila dṛṣṭvāmutrāsāv itthaṃ gotraputro nāyakaścittonmādam anubhavati
children.translated_text: 'Listen, dear lady, to this strange thing: after seeing you, that hero, a noble man of such-and-such family, is experiencing madness of mind there.'
She should describe him: 'By nature he is delicate; the poor man has perhaps never before been distressed over another woman.'

children.text: tato 'dhunā śakyam anena maraṇam apyanubhavitum iti varṇayet
children.translated_text: 'Therefore now it is possible that he might even undergo death.'

children.text: tatra siddhā dvitīye ahani vāci vaktre dṛṣṭyāṃ ca prasādam upalakṣya punar api kathāṃ pravartayet
children.translated_text: When the matter has succeeded, on the second day, perceiving favor in her speech, face, and glance, she should again begin the story.

children.text: śṛṇvatyāṃ cāhalyāvimārakaśākuntalādīny anyānyapi laukikāni ca kathayet tadyuktāni
children.translated_text: While the woman listens, she should tell stories such as those of <s>Ahalyā</s>, <s>Vimāraka</s>, and <s>Śākuntala</s>, and also other worldly stories suited to that purpose.
She should describe the hero's virility, his knowledge of the sixty-four arts, and his good fortune,

children.text: ślāghanīyatāṃ cāsya pracchannaṃ saṃprayogaṃ bhūtam abhūtapūrvaṃ vā varṇayet
children.translated_text: and his praiseworthiness; she should also describe a secret union of his, whether real or never actually occurring.
And she should observe the woman's indication.
When she sees her, she converses with a smile.
And she invites her to a seat.

children.text: kvāsitaṃ kva śayitaṃ kva bhuktaṃ kva ceṣṭitaṃ kiṃ vā kṛtam iti pṛcchati
children.translated_text: She asks, 'Where have you sat? Where have you slept? Where have you eaten? Where have you gone about? Or what have you done?'
In seclusion she shows herself.
She sets stories in motion.
Thinking of him, she sighs and yawns.
And she gives a gift of affection.
And at desired festivals she remembers him.
She sends out an attachment aimed at seeing him again.

children.text: sādhuvādinī satī kim idam aśobhanam abhidhatsa iti kathām anubadhnāti
children.translated_text: Though speaking as if virtuous, she keeps the conversation going, saying, "Why are you saying this improper thing?"
She imputes to the <s>nāyaka</s> faults connected with deceit and fickleness.

children.text: pūrvapravṛttaṃ ca tatsaṃdarśanaṃ kathābhiyogaṃ ca svayam akathayantī tayocyamānam ākāṅkṣati
children.translated_text: Without herself mentioning that earlier meeting and the attempt at conversation, she longs for it to be mentioned by the other woman.

children.text: nāyakamanoratheṣu ca kathyamāneṣu saparibhavaṃ nāma hasati
children.translated_text: And when the <s>nāyaka</s>'s desires are being described, she laughs as if with disdain.
Yet she does not denounce him.
The go-between should strengthen a woman who has shown signs of inclination by means of tokens from the <s>nāyaka</s>.
But one who is not acquainted should be won over by accounts of his virtues and by stories of his affection.
"There is no mission of a go-between between two people who are unacquainted and whose signs have not been seen," says <s>Auddālaki</s>.
"There can be one even between two unacquainted people if their signs have come into contact," say the <s>Bābhravīyas</s>.
"There can be one even between two acquainted people whose signs have not come into contact," says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.

children.text: asaṃstutayor adṛṣṭākārayor api dūtīpratyayād iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Even between two unacquainted people whose signs have not been seen, because of confidence in the <s>dūtī</s> (female go-between)," says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: tāsāṃ manoharāṇyupāyanāni tāmbūlam anulepanaṃ srajam aṅgulīyakaṃ vāso vā tena prahitaṃ darśayet
children.translated_text: She should show them the charming presents sent by him: betel, unguent, a garland, a ring, or a garment.

children.text: teṣu nāyakasya yathārthaṃ nakhadaśanapadāni tāni tāni ca cihnāni syuḥ
children.translated_text: On these there should be, as appropriate for the <s>nāyaka</s>, nail and tooth marks and various other signs.
And on a garment he should place the imprint of joined hands marked with saffron.
She should show cut-out leaf designs of various shapes expressing different intentions.
She should show ear-ornaments and head-garlands that contain written leaves, and in these an announcement of his own desire.
And she should arrange for the woman to give return gifts.
Thus, when the two have mutually accepted one another, their meeting takes place through confidence in the <s>dūtī</s>.

children.text: sa tu devatābhigamane yātrāyām udyānakrīḍāyāṃ jalāvataraṇe vivāhe yajñavyasanotsaveṣv agnyutpāte cauravibhrame janapadasya cakrārohaṇe prekṣāvyāpāreṣu teṣu teṣu ca kāryeṣv iti bābhravīyāḥ
children.translated_text: According to the <s>Bābhravīyas</s>, that meeting may occur when going to a deity, on a journey, in garden play, at entering the water, at a wedding, at sacrifices, calamities, and festivals, at an outbreak of fire, in confusion caused by thieves, when the district is overrun by an army, at theatrical entertainments, and on various other occasions.
In the houses of a female friend, a mendicant woman, a female ascetic, or a female hermit, it is an easy means, says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.

children.text: tasyā eva tu gehe viditaniṣkramapraveśe cintitātyayapratīkāre praveśanam upapannaṃ niṣkramaṇam avijñātakālaṃ ca tan nityaṃ sukhopāyaṃ ceti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in her own house, where exits and entrances are known, with remedies for anticipated dangers thought out, entry is proper, departure can be at an unnoticed time, and that is always an easy means, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: nisṛṣṭārthā parimitārthā patrahārī svayaṃdūtī mūḍhadūtī bhāryādūtī mūkadūtī vātadūtī ceti dūtīviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The special kinds of <s>dūtī</s> are these: one entrusted with the whole affair, one entrusted with a limited affair, a letter-carrier, a self-messenger, a foolish messenger, a wife-messenger, a silent messenger, and a wind-messenger.

children.text: nāyakasya nāyikāyāśca yathāmanīṣitam artham upalabhya svabuddhyā kāryasaṃpādinī nisṛṣṭārthā ||
children.translated_text: The one entrusted with the whole affair is a woman who, having learned the desired aim of the <s>nāyaka</s> and the <s>nāyikā</s>, accomplishes the business by her own intelligence.
She is used mostly when the two are acquainted and converse with each other.
When appointed by the <s>nāyikā</s>, she may be used even when the two are unacquainted but converse.
And, from curiosity, even when the two are unacquainted, thinking, "These two are suited and fit for each other."

children.text: kāryaikadeśam abhiyogaikadeśaṃ copalabhya śeṣaṃ sampādayatīti parimitārthā ||
children.translated_text: The one entrusted with a limited affair is so called because, having learned one part of the business and one part of the approach, she completes the rest.
She is used for two people who have seen each other's signs but meet only rarely.
The letter-carrier is so called because she conveys only a message.
She is used for two people whose sincere feeling is intense and who have already come together, in order to inform them of place and time.

children.text: dautyena prahitānyayā svayam eva nāyakam abhigacched ajānatī nāma tena sahopabhogaṃ svapne vā kathayet
children.translated_text: Sent by another as a messenger, she herself may approach the <s>nāyaka</s>; pretending not to understand, she may speak of enjoyment with him, or say that it happened in a dream.
She should criticize a slip in a family-name, and also his wife.
Using that as a pretext, she should show jealousy herself.
Or she should give him something marked with nail and tooth marks.

children.text: bhavate aham adau dātuṃ saṃkalpiteti cābhidadhīta
children.translated_text: And she should say, "I had first intended to give this to you, sir."

children.text: mama bhāryāyā kā ramanīyeti vivikte paryanuyuñjīta sā svayaṃdūtī
children.translated_text: In private she should ask, "What is charming about my wife?" She is a self-messenger.
For her, seeing him in private and receiving gifts are appropriate.

children.text: pratigrahacchalenānyām abhisaṃdhāyāsyāḥ saṃdeśaśrāvaṇadvāreṇa nāyakaṃ sādhayet tāṃ copahanyāt sāpi svayaṃdūtī
children.translated_text: Under the pretext of receiving a gift, while aiming at another woman, she should win over the <s>nāyaka</s> by making him hear that woman's message, and she should undermine that woman; she too is a self-messenger.
By this, the <s>nāyaka</s> too, and another messenger, have been explained.

children.text: nāyakabhāryāṃ mugdhāṃ viśvāsyāyantraṇayānupraviśya nāyakasya ceṣṭitāni pṛcchet
children.translated_text: Having won the trust of the <s>nāyaka</s>'s naive wife and entered without restraint, she should ask about the <s>nāyaka</s>'s actions.
She should teach her devices.
She should adorn her so as to show signs.
She should make her angry.
She should have her hear, "Act in this way."
And she herself should produce nail and tooth marks on her.
