children.text: tena dvāreṇa nāyakam ākārayet sā mūḍhadūtī ||
children.translated_text: Through that opening she should summon the <s>nāyaka</s>. She is a foolish messenger.
She should arrange replies from her through that very woman.

children.text: svabhāryāṃ vā mūḍhāṃ prayojya tayā saha viśvāsena yojayitvā tayaivākārayet
children.translated_text: Or, employing his own naive wife, after joining her in trust with that woman, he should summon her through that same wife.
And he should display his own cleverness.
She is a wife-messenger.
The grasping of her signs is through that very wife.

children.text: bālāṃ vā paricārikām adoṣajñām aduṣṭenopāyena prahiṇuyāt
children.translated_text: Or he should send a young maidservant, unaware of fault, by an innocent device.

children.text: tatra sraji karṇapattre vā gūḍhalekhanidhānaṃ nakhadaśanapadaṃ vā sā mūkadūtī
children.translated_text: If there is a secret letter placed in a garland or ear-ornament there, or a mark of nails and teeth, she is a silent messenger.
Replies should be requested through that very girl.

children.text: pūrvaprastutārthaliṅgasambaddham anyajanāgrahaṇīyaṃ laukikārthaṃ dvyarthaṃ vā vacanam udāsīnā yā śrāvayet sā vātadūtī
children.translated_text: One who, while apparently neutral, causes him to hear an ordinary statement connected with a sign of the matter previously introduced, incomprehensible to other people, or a statement with double meaning, is a wind-messenger.

children.text: tasyā api tayaiva pratyuttaraprārthanam iti tāsāṃ viśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For her too, replies should be requested through that very woman. Thus are their distinctions.
And here there are verses:
A widow, a female observer, a maidservant, a mendicant woman, a craftswoman
Entering into trust quickly, she also obtains the work of a go-between.
She should make the woman take on hatred toward her husband and should describe delightful things;
she should also show the varied pleasures of sexual enjoyment belonging to other women.
And she should describe the lover's attachment, and again his skill in lovemaking,
his entreaty by means of superior women, and his firmness.
Even an aim not originally intended, abandoned because it had become a cause of fault,
a go-between brings back again through skill in speech.

children.text: na rājñāṃ mahāmātrāṇāṃ vā parabhavanapraveśo vidyate
children.translated_text: Kings and high officials have no entering into another's house.

children.text: mahājanena hi caritam eṣāṃ dṛśyate anuvidhīyate ca ||
children.translated_text: For their conduct is seen by the populace and is imitated.

children.text: savitāram udyantaṃ trayo lokāḥ paśyanti anūdyante ca
children.translated_text: The three worlds see the sun as it rises, and they follow after it in speech;
they see it even as it goes, and they follow after it.

children.text: tasmād aśakyatvād garhaṇīyatvācceti na te vṛthā kiṃcid ācareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, because it is impossible and blameworthy, they should not do anything at random.
But when action is unavoidable, they should employ stratagems.

children.text: grāmādhipater ayuktakasya halotthavṛttiputrasya yūno grāmīṇayoṣito vacanamātrasādhyāḥ
children.translated_text: For a village headman, an appointed official, or the young son of a man whose livelihood comes from the plough, village women are attainable by mere words.
Libertines call those women <s>carṣaṇyaḥ</s>.

children.text: tābhiḥ saha viṣṭikarmasu koṣṭhāgārapraveśe dravyāṇāṃ niṣkramaṇapraveśanayor bhavanapratisaṃskāre kṣetrakarmaṇi karpāsorṇātasīśaṇavalkalādāne sūtrapratigrahe dravyāṇāṃ krayavikrayavinimayeṣu teṣu teṣu ca karmasu saṃprayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With them there may be union during forced labor, entry into granaries, the taking out and bringing in of goods, repairs to houses, fieldwork, the taking of cotton, wool, flax, hemp, and bark, the receiving of thread, the buying, selling, and exchange of goods, and those various tasks.
In the same way, the superintendent of cattle may have union with cowherd women.
The superintendent of thread may have union with widows, unprotected women, and women who have not gone forth.
A city man may have union with women who wander about at night, because he knows their vulnerable points and because he roams at night.
The superintendent of merchandise may have union in connection with buying and selling.

children.text: aṣṭamīcandrakaumudīsuvasantakādiṣu pattananagarakharvaṭayoṣitām īśvarabhavane saha antaḥpurikābhiḥ prāyeṇa krīḍā ||
children.translated_text: On eighth-day moonlight festivals, <s>Suvasantaka</s>, and the like, women of port towns, cities, and market towns generally sport with the women of the inner palace in the lord's residence.

children.text: tatra cāpānakānte nagarastriyo yathāparicayam antaḥpurikāṇāṃ pṛthak pṛthag bhogāvāsakān praviśya kathābhir āsitvā pūjitāḥ prapītāścopapradoṣaṃ niṣkrāmayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, at the end of drinking, the city women, according to their acquaintance, should enter separately the pleasure apartments of the women of the inner palace, sit in conversation, be honored and given drink, and be sent out toward early night.

children.text: tatra praṇihitā rājadāsī prayojyāyāḥ pūrvasaṃsṛṣṭā tāṃ tatra sambhāṣeta
children.translated_text: There a planted royal maid, previously acquainted with the woman to be used, should speak with her there;
she should connect her with the sight of charming things.
Even beforehand, when she is in her own house, she should say,

children.text: amuṣyāṃ krīḍāyāṃ tava rājabhavanasthānāni rāmaṇīyakāni darśayiṣyāmīti kāle ca yojayet
children.translated_text: "At that festival I shall show you the charming places in the royal residence," and at the proper time she should arrange it.
"I shall show you the outer coral pavement,

children.text: maṇibhūmikāṃ vṛkṣavāṭikāṃ mṛdvīkāmaṇḍapaṃ samudragṛhaprāsādān gūḍhabhittisaṃcārāṃścitrakarmāṇi krīḍāmṛgān yantrāṇi śakunān vyāghrasiṃhapañjarādīni ca yāni purastād varṇitāni syuḥ
children.translated_text: the jeweled floor, the grove, the grape arbor, the sea-house mansions, hidden passages in the walls, paintings, tame animals, mechanical devices, birds, cages of tigers and lions, and the like, which have been described before."
And in private she should let her hear of the lord's attachment directed toward her.
She should also praise his cleverness in union.
When the woman has consented, she should arrange the meeting so that no counsel is overheard.

children.text: apratipadyamānāṃ svayam eveśvara āgatyopacāraiḥ sānvitāṃ rañjayitvā sambhūya ca sānurāgaṃ visṛjet
children.translated_text: If she does not consent, the lord himself should come, win her over with attentive courtesies, unite with her, and then release her affectionately.

children.text: prayojyāyāśca patyur anugrahocitasya dārān nityam antaḥpuram aucityāt praveśayet
children.translated_text: And, as propriety allows, he should regularly cause the wives of the husband of the woman to be used, if he is fit for favor, to enter the inner palace.
There, the planted royal maid is to be understood as before.

children.text: antaḥpurikā vā prayojyayā saha svaceṭikā saṃpreṣaṇena prītiṃ kuryāt
children.translated_text: Or a woman of the inner palace, through the sending of her own maidservant with the woman to be used, should establish affection with her.
When affection has developed, she should arrange an audience under a pretext.

children.text: praviṣṭāṃ pūjitāṃ pītavartīm praṇihitā rājadāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa
children.translated_text: When she has entered, been honored, and had drink, the planted royal maid is to be understood as before.

children.text: yasmin vā vijñāne prayojyā vikhyātā syāt taddarśanārtham antaḥpurikā sopacāraṃ tām āhvayet
children.translated_text: Or, in whatever branch of knowledge the woman to be used is famous, a woman of the inner palace should courteously summon her for a display of it.
When she has entered, the planted royal maid is to be understood as before.

children.text: udbhūtānarthasya bhītasya vā bhāryāṃ bhikṣukī brūyāt asāvantaḥpurikā rājani siddhā gṛhītavākyā mama vacanaṃ śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: A female mendicant should say to the wife of a man whose calamity has arisen, or who is afraid: "That woman of the inner palace is successful with the king, her words are accepted, and she listens to what I say.
By nature she is compassionate. I shall approach her by this means.
I myself shall obtain entry for you.

children.text: sā ca te bhartur mahāntam anarthaṃ nivartayiṣyatīti pratipannāṃ dvistrir iti praveśayet
children.translated_text: And she will avert a great calamity from your husband." When the woman has accepted, the mendicant should have her enter two or three times with such words.
The woman of the inner palace should give her assurance of safety.

children.text: abhayaśravaṇācca samprahṛṣṭāṃ praṇihitā rājadāsīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa
children.translated_text: And when she is delighted by hearing that assurance, the planted royal maid is to be understood as before.

children.text: etayā vṛttyarthināṃ mahāmātrābhitaptānāṃ balād vigṛhītānāṃ vyavahāre durbalānāṃ svabhogenāsaṃtuṣṭānāṃ rājani prītikāmānāṃ rājyajaneṣu paṅktim icchatāṃ sajātair bādhyamānānāṃ sajātān bādhitukāmānāṃ sūcakānām anyeṣāṃ kāryavaśināṃ jāyā vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure the wives have been explained for men seeking livelihood, men afflicted by high officials, men seized by force, men weak in litigation, men dissatisfied with their own enjoyment, men desiring favor with the king, men wishing for standing among royal people, men oppressed by their own kin, men wishing to oppress their own kin, informers, and others constrained by some business.

children.text: anyena vā prayojyāṃ saha saṃsṛṣṭāṃ saṃgrāhya dāsyam upanītāṃ krameṇāntaḥpuraṃ praveśayet
children.translated_text: Or, having caused the woman to be used to associate with another person and having brought her into service as a maid, one should gradually introduce her into the inner palace.

children.text: praṇidhinā cāyatim asyāḥ saṃdūṣya rājani vidviṣṭa iti kalatrāvagrahopāyenainām antaḥpuraṃ praveśayed iti pracchannayogāḥ
children.translated_text: Or, through an agent, having damaged her future prospects, one should introduce her into the inner palace by the expedient of seizing the wife on the grounds that she is hostile to the king. These are covert stratagems.
These are mostly used among princes.

children.text: na tv evaṃ parabhavanam īśvaraḥ praviśet ||
children.translated_text: But the lord himself should certainly not enter another's house in this way.

children.text: ābhīraṃ hi koṭṭarājaṃ parabhavanagataṃ bhrātṛprayukto rajako jaghāna
children.translated_text: For a washerman, instigated by his brother, killed the <s>Ābhīra</s> <s>Koṭṭarāja</s> when he had gone to another's house,
and the superintendent of horses killed <s>Jayasena</s>, the king of <s>Kāśī</s>.
But practices in which desire is made public occur according to local custom.

children.text: prattā janapadakanyā daśame ahani kiṃcid aupāyanikam upagṛhya praviśantyantaḥpuram upabhuktā eva visṛjyanta ityāndhrāṇām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Āndhras</s>, country girls who have been given are said to enter the inner palace on the tenth day, taking some gift, and, after being enjoyed, are released.

children.text: mahāmātreṣvarāṇām antaḥpurāṇi niśi sevārthaṃ rājānam upagacchanti vātsagulmakānām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Vātsagulmakas</s>, the women of the inner palaces of high officials and lords approach the king at night for service.

children.text: rūpavatīr janapadayoṣitaḥ prītyapadeśena māsaṃ māsārdhaṃ vātivāsayanty antaḥpurikā vaidarbhāṇām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Vaidarbhas</s>, the women of the inner palace keep beautiful country women staying there for a month or half a month under the pretext of affection.

children.text: darśanīyāḥ svabhāryāḥ prītidāyām eva mahāmātrarājabhyo dadaty aparāntakānām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Aparāntakas</s>, they give their own attractive wives to high officials and kings simply as a gift of favor.

children.text: rājakrīḍārthaṃ nagarastriyo janapadastriyaśca saṃghaśa ekaśaśca rājakulaṃ praviśanti saurāṣṭrakāṇām iti ||
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Saurāṣṭrakas</s>, city women and country women enter the royal household, in groups and singly, for the king's sport.
Here there are verses:

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ prayogāḥ pāradārikāḥ
children.translated_text: These and many other adulterous practices
prevail from region to region, set in motion by kings.

children.text: na tv evaitān prayuñjīta rājā lokahite rataḥ
children.translated_text: But a king intent on the welfare of the people should not employ these at all;
having restrained the group of six enemies, he thereby conquers the earth.

children.text: nāntaḥpurāṇāṃ rakṣaṇayogāt puruṣasaṃdarśanaṃ vidyate patyuścaikatvād anekasādhāraṇatvāccātṛptiḥ
children.translated_text: Because the inner palaces are guarded, there is no seeing of men; and because the husband is one, yet common to many, there is dissatisfaction.

children.text: tasmāt tāni prayogata eva parasparaṃ rañjayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those women should delight one another by practical devices themselves.

children.text: dhātreyikāṃ sakhīṃ dāsīṃ vā puruṣavad alaṃkṛtyākṛtisaṃyuktaiḥ kandamūlaphalāvayavair apadravyair vātmābhiprāyāṃ nirvartayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: They should dress a foster-sister, a female friend, or a slave woman like a man, and satisfy their own desire with tubers, roots, or fruit-parts shaped to fit, or with artificial implements.
They should also lie upon male images and upon figures with indistinct sexual marks.

children.text: rājānaśca kṛpāśīlā vināpi bhāvayogād āyojitāpadravyā yāvadartham ekayā rātryā bahvībhir api gacchanti
children.translated_text: And compassionate kings, even without emotional union, equipped with artificial implements, go as far as necessary with many women in a single night.

children.text: yasyāṃ tu prītir vāsaka ṛtuv vā tatrābhiprāyataḥ pravartanta iti prācyopacārāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But where there is affection for a woman, or where it is her turn for the night's residence or her season, there they act according to their desire. Such are the eastern usages.

children.text: strīyogeṇaiva puruṣāṇām apyalabdhavṛttīnāṃ viyoniṣu vijātiṣu strīpratimāsu kevalopamardanāccābhiprāyanivṛttir vyākhyātā ||
children.translated_text: By the very case of women's union, the satisfaction of desire has also been explained for men whose livelihood has not been obtained: with non-vaginal places, with beings of another species, with female images, and by mere rubbing.

children.text: yoṣaveṣāṃśca nāgarakān prāyeṇa antaḥpurikāḥ paricārikābhiḥ saha praveśayanti
children.translated_text: The women of the inner palace generally have city men in women's dress brought in together with female attendants.

children.text: teṣām upāvartane dhātreyikāśca abhyantarasaṃsṛṣṭā āyatiṃ darśayantyaḥ prayateran
children.translated_text: For bringing those men in, foster-sisters who have contact inside should exert themselves while pointing out future prospects.

children.text: sukhapraveśitām apasārabhūmiṃ viśālatāṃ veśmanaḥ pramādaṃ rakṣiṇām anityatāṃ parijanasya varṇayeyuḥ
children.translated_text: They should describe the ease of entry, the ground for escape, the spaciousness of the residence, the carelessness of the guards, and the inconstancy of the attendants.

children.text: na cāsadbhūtenārthena praveśayituṃ janam āvartayeyur doṣāt ||
children.translated_text: But they should not induce a man to enter by means of a false matter, because of the danger.

children.text: nāgarakastu suprāpam apyantaḥpuram apāyabhūyiṣṭhatvān na praviśed iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet a city man should not enter even an easily accessible inner palace, because it is full of danger, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: sāpasāraṃ tu pramadavanāvagāḍhaṃ vibhaktadīrghakakṣyam alpapramattarakṣakaṃ proṣitārājakaṃ kāraṇāni samīkṣya bahuśa āhūyamāno 'rthabuddhyā kakṣyāpraveśaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tābhir eva vihitopāyaḥ praviśet
children.translated_text: But if it has an escape route, is sunk deep in a pleasure grove, has separate long corridors, has few or careless guards, and has a king who is away, then, after considering the reasons, when he has been repeatedly summoned, has judged the matter advantageous, has seen the entrance to the corridor, and has been given a means arranged by those very women, he may enter.
And, when it is within his power, he should go out every day.

children.text: bahiśca rakṣibhir anyad eva kāraṇam apadiśya saṃsṛjyeta
children.translated_text: Outside, he should associate with the guards while alleging some other reason.

children.text: antaścāriṇyāṃ ca paricārikāyāṃ viditārthāyāṃ saktam ātmānaṃ rūpayet
children.translated_text: Inside, he should present himself as attached to a female attendant who moves within and knows the matter.

children.text: tadalābhācca śokam antaḥpraveśinībhiśca dūtīkalpaṃ sakalam ācaret
children.translated_text: If that is not possible, he should show grief and carry out the entire procedure resembling that of a go-between through women who enter inside.
He should also become aware of the king's spies.
When the go-between cannot move about, he should stay in a place where there is an opportunity to see the woman to be approached, once he has learned her appearance.
Even there, among the guards, the pretext should be a female attendant.
When she fixes her eyes on him, he should communicate his signs and intentions.

children.text: yatra saṃpāto 'syāstatra citrakarmaṇastad yuktasya vyarthānāṃ gītavastukānāṃ krīḍanakānāṃ kṛtacihnānām āpīnakānām aṅgulīyakasya ca nidhānam
children.translated_text: Where she comes into contact with him, he should deposit a picture connected with her, purposeless song-texts, toys, marked objects, small vessels, and a ring.
He should watch for the reply given by her.
After that he should strive for entry.

children.text: yatra cāsyā niyataṃ gamanam iti vidyāt tatra pracchannasya prāg evāvasthānam
children.translated_text: Where he knows that her going is fixed, he should be there beforehand in concealment.
Or, in the form of a guard, he should enter at the time permitted by her.
Or there may be entry and exit while wrapped in bedding and coverings.
Or, by devices of packets within packets, he may pass with his shadow and form concealed.

children.text: tatrāyaṃ prayogaḥ nakulahṛdayaṃ corakatumbīphalāni sarpākṣīṇi cāntardhūmena pacet
children.translated_text: Here the procedure is this: one should cook the heart of a mongoose, fruits of <s>coraka</s> and gourd, and <s>sarpākṣī</s> with smoke enclosed inside.
Then one should grind them with an equal amount of collyrium.
With his eyes anointed by this, he moves about with shadow and form invisible.
And he may enter on bright moonlit nights, in a crowd of lamps, or by means of a tunnel.
On this there is the following verse:
At the carrying out of goods and the bringing in of drinks,
and in the bustle of maidservants for the sake of a drinking festival,

children.text: vyatyāse veśmanāṃ caiva rakṣiṇāṃ ca viparyaye
children.translated_text: in the exchange of residences and likewise in the changing of guards,
at departure for a garden outing and at entry after the outing,
on a journey that has arisen for a long time, and also when the king is abroad,

children.text: praveśanaṃ bhavet prāyo yūnāṃ niṣkramaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: there is generally entry for young men, and likewise exit.
When the residents of the inner palace know one another's affairs,
then, having one common purpose, they should also cause the division of the others.
Having first corrupted one another, and then remaining firm in commitment to the common purpose,

children.text: abhedyatāṃ gataḥ sadyo yatheṣṭaṃ phalam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: one who has at once become impossible to divide obtains the desired fruit.

children.text: tatra rājakulacāriṇya eva lakṣaṇyān puruṣān antaḥpuraṃ praveśayanti nātisurakṣatvād āparāntikānām
children.translated_text: There, among the <s>Āparāntikas</s>, the women who move in the royal household themselves bring suitable men into the inner palace, because it is not very well guarded.
Among the <s>Ābhīrakas</s>, women accomplish their aim through men called kṣatriyas who are guards of the inner palace.

children.text: preṣyābhiḥ saha tadveṣān nāgarakaputrān praveśayanti vātsagulmakānām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Vātsagulmakas</s>, together with maidservants, they introduce city youths in that same disguise.

children.text: svair eva putrair antaḥpurāṇi kāmacārair jananīvarjam upayujyante vaidarbhakāṇām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Vaidarbhas</s>, the inner palaces are enjoyed by their own sons as they please, with the mother excepted.

children.text: tathā praveśibhir eva jñātisaṃbandhibhir nānyair upayujyante strairājakānām
children.translated_text: Likewise, among the <s>Strairājakas</s>, they are enjoyed only by kinsmen and relatives who have gained entry, and by no others.
Among the <s>Gauḍas</s>, they are enjoyed by brahmins, friends, servants, slaves, and attendants.

children.text: parispandāḥ karmakarāścāntaḥpureṣvaniṣiddhā anye api tadrūpāśca saindhavānām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Saindhavas</s>, messengers and workmen are not forbidden in the inner palaces, nor are others of that sort.

children.text: arthena rakṣiṇam upagṛhya sāhasikāḥ saṃhatāḥ praviśanti haimavatānām
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Haimavatas</s>, bold men enter in bands after winning over the guard with money.
Among the <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Aṅgas</s>, and <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, city brahmins go into the inner palaces on the assignment of presenting flowers, with the king's knowledge.
Their conversation takes place through a curtain.
Through that occasion, sexual contact occurs.

children.text: saṃhatya navadaśetyekaikaṃ yuvānaṃ pracchādayanti prācyānām iti
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Prācyas</s>, having gathered in groups of nine or ten, they conceal one young man each, so it is said.
Thus one may act with regard to the wives of others.
Thus ends the conduct of women of the inner palace.

children.text: ebhya eva ca kāraṇebhyaḥ svadārān rakṣet ||
children.translated_text: And for these very reasons one should guard one's own wives.
The teachers say that one should station in the inner palace guards who have been tested as pure by the trial of sexual desire.

children.text: te hi bhayena cārthena cānyaṃ prayojayeyustasmāt kāmabhayārthopadhāśuddhān iti goṇikāputraḥ
children.translated_text: For they might employ another man through fear or through money; therefore they should be tested as pure by the trials of desire, fear, and money, says <s>Goṇikāputra</s>.

children.text: adroho dharmastam api bhayājjahyād ato dharmabhayopadhāśuddhān iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Non-betrayal is <s>dharma</s> (proper conduct), but even that one might abandon from fear; therefore they should be tested as pure by the trials of <s>dharma</s> and fear, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: paravākyābhidhāyinībhiśca gūḍhākārābhiḥ pramadābhir ātmadārān upadadhyācchaucāśaucaparijñānārtham iti bābhravīyāḥ
children.translated_text: And one should test one's own wives, in order to know their purity or impurity, by means of women who repeat another's words and whose form is disguised, say the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s>.

children.text: duṣṭānāṃ yuvatiṣu siddhatvān nākasmād aduṣṭadūṣaṇam ācared iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since corrupt women are adept among young women, one should not, without cause, undertake the corruption of an uncorrupt woman, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

children.text: atigoṣṭhī niraṅkuśatvaṃ bhartuḥ svairatā puruṣaiḥ sahāniyantraṇatā
children.translated_text: Excessive social visiting, lack of restraint, the husband's permissiveness, freedom with men, and absence of supervision,

children.text: pravāse avasthānaṃ videśe nivāsaḥ svavṛttyupaghātaḥ svairiṇīsaṃsargaḥ patyur īrṣyālutā ceti strīṇāṃ vināśakāraṇāni ||
children.translated_text: remaining away from home while he is abroad, residence in a foreign place, damage to one's livelihood, association with wanton women, and the husband's jealousy: these are the causes of ruin for women.
Having perceived from the treatise the stratagems marked out for adultery,

children.text: na yāti chalanāṃ kaścit svadārān prati śāstravit ||
children.translated_text: no one who knows the treatise is deceived regarding his own wives.
Because the practices are uncertain in outcome, because the dangers are seen,
and because it is contrary to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> (profit), one should not practice adultery.

children.text: tad etad dāraguptyartham ārabdhaṃ śreyase nṛṇām
children.translated_text: This topic has been undertaken for the sake of guarding wives and for the welfare of men;
its procedure should not be understood as meant merely for the corruption of people.
For courtesans, pleasure and livelihood in obtaining men are innate.
Activity arising from passion is natural; artificial activity is for the sake of money.
Even that artificial activity she should make appear as if it were natural.
For men devoted to desire are susceptible to trust.
And she should make her lack of greed known, as a demonstration for him.
Nor should she obtain money by improper means, for the sake of preserving her future prospects.

children.text: nityam alaṃkārayoginī rājamārgāvalokinī dṛśyamānā na cātivivṛtā tiṣṭhet
children.translated_text: Always adorned, looking out on the royal road, visible but not too exposed, she should stand there.
For she shares the nature of merchandise.

children.text: yair nāyakam āvarjayed anyābhyaś cāvacchindyād ātmanaścānarthaṃ pratikuryād arthaṃ ca sādhayen na ca gamyaiḥ paribhūyeta tān sahāyān kuryāt
children.translated_text: She should make those men her helpers by whom she may win over a lover, cut him off from other women, avert harm from herself, obtain money, and not be despised by men fit to be approached.

children.text: te tv ārakṣakapuruṣā dharmādhikaraṇasthā daivajñā vikrāntāḥ śūrāḥ samānavidyāḥ kalāgrāhiṇaḥ pīṭhamardaviṭavidūṣakamālākāragandhikaśauṇḍikarajakanāpitabhikṣukās te ca te ca kāryayogāt ||
children.translated_text: They are guards, men attached to the court of justice, astrologers, powerful men, heroes, men of the same learning, connoisseurs of the arts, pīṭhamardas, viṭas, jesters, garland-makers, perfumers, distillers, washermen, barbers, mendicants, and whatever others are suited to the business.

children.text: kevalārthāstvamī gamyāḥ svatantraḥ pūrve vayasi vartamāno vittavān aparokṣavṛttir adhikaraṇavān akṛcchrādhigatavittaḥ
children.translated_text: But these men are to be approached for money alone: one who is independent, still in early youth, wealthy, whose occupation is visible, who has authority, whose wealth has been obtained without hardship,

children.text: saṃgharṣavān saṃtatāyaḥ subhagamānī ślāghanakaḥ ṣaṇḍakaśca puṃśabdārthī
children.translated_text: who is contentious, has continual income, thinks himself handsome, is boastful, or is a eunuch desiring the name of man,
who competes with his equals, or who is by nature generous,

children.text: rājani mahāmātre vā siddho daivapramāṇo vittāvamānī gurūṇāṃ śāsanātigaḥ sajātānāṃ lakṣyabhūtaḥ savitta ekaputro liṅgī pracchannakāmaḥ śūro vaidyaśceti ||
children.translated_text: one who has influence with the king or a high minister, who trusts to fate, despises wealth, transgresses the commands of elders, is a marked man among his peers, is wealthy, is an only son, bears religious marks, has hidden desire, is brave, or is a physician.
But those to be approached for affection, fame, and money are known by their qualities.

children.text: mahākulīno viddhān sarvasamayajñaḥ kavir ākhyānakuśalo vāgmī pragalbho vividhaśilpajño vṛddhadarśī sthūlalakṣo mahotsāho dṛḍhabhaktir anasūyakastyāgī mitravatsalo ghaṭāgoṣṭhīprekṣaṇakasamājasamasyākrīḍanaśīlo nīrujo 'vyaṅgaśarīraḥ prāṇavānamadyapo vṛṣo maitraḥ strīṇāṃ praṇetā lālayitā ca
children.translated_text: A man of great family, learned, knowing all conventions, a poet, skilled in stories, eloquent, bold, versed in various arts, experienced with elders, having large aims, very energetic, firm in devotion, free from envy, generous, affectionate to friends, habitually fond of clubs, conversation, spectacles, assemblies, problems, and games, free from illness, with an unblemished body, vigorous, not addicted to drink, virile, friendly, a guide for women, and one who pampers them,

children.text: na cāsāṃ vaśagaḥ svatantravṛttir aniṣṭhuro 'nīrṣyālur anavaśaṅkī ceti nāyakaguṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet is not under their control, acts independently, is not harsh, not jealous, and not suspicious: these are the qualities of a lover.

children.text: nāyikāyāḥ punā rūpayauvanalakṣaṇamādhuryayoginī guṇeṣvanuraktā na tathārtheṣu prītisaṃyogaśīlā sthiram atirekajātīyā viśeṣārthinī nityam akadaryavṛttir goṣṭhīkalāpriyā ceti ||
children.translated_text: The heroine, again, should be endowed with beauty, youth, auspicious marks, and sweetness, attached to virtues and not so much to money, inclined to loving union, steadfast, of an exceptional kind, desirous of distinction, always not miserly in conduct, and fond of conversation and the arts.

children.text: nāyikā punarbuddhiśīlācāra ārjavaṃ kṛtajñatā dīrghadūradarśitvaṃ avisaṃvāditā deśakālajñatā nāgarakatā dainyātihāsapaiśunyaparivādakrodhalobhastambhacāpalavarjanaṃ pūrvābhibhāṣitā kāmasūtrakauśalaṃ tadaṅgavidyāsu ceti sādhāraṇaguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: For the <s>nāyikā</s>, intelligence, character, good conduct, straightforwardness, gratitude, long and far-reaching foresight, truthfulness, knowledge of place and time, urbanity, and avoidance of wretchedness, excessive laughter, tale-bearing, slander, anger, greed, obstinacy, and fickleness; speaking first, skill in the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, and in the auxiliary arts: these are common virtues.
When the qualities are reversed, they are faults.

children.text: kṣayī rogī kṛmiśakṛdvāyasāsyaḥ priyakalatraḥ paruṣavāk kadaryo nirghṛṇo gurujanaparityaktaḥ steno dambhaśīlo mūlakarmaṇi prasakto mānāpamānayor anapekṣī dveṣyair apyarthahāryo vilajja ityagamyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man who is consumptive, diseased, whose mouth is foul like worms, excrement, or a crow, who is devoted to his wife, harsh-spoken, miserly, merciless, abandoned by elders, a thief, hypocritical, addicted to root-magic, indifferent to honor and dishonor, whose wealth may be taken even by enemies, or shameless: such men are not to be approached.

children.text: rāgo bhayam arthaḥ saṃgharṣo vairaniryātanaṃ jijñāsā pakṣaḥ khedo gharmo yaśo 'nukampā suhṛdvākyaṃ hrīḥ priyasādṛśyaṃ dhanyatā rāgāpanayaḥ sājātyaṃ sāhaveśyaṃ sātatyam āyatiśca gamanakāraṇāni bhavantītyācāryāḥ
children.translated_text: Passion, fear, wealth, rivalry, retaliation for enmity, curiosity, taking a side, weariness, heat, fame, compassion, a friend's word, shame, resemblance to the beloved, good fortune, removal of passion, sameness of kind, living together as neighbors, continuity, and future advantage are causes for going to a man, according to the teachers.
<s>Vātsyāyana</s> says: wealth, averting misfortune, and affection.
But wealth is not obstructed by affection,
because it has primacy.

children.text: bhayādiṣu tu gurulāghavaṃ parīkṣyam iti sahāyagamyāgamyakāraṇacintā ||
children.translated_text: In cases such as fear, however, the relative weight should be examined. Thus ends the consideration of assistants, men fit and unfit to be approached, and the causes.
Even when invited by an approachable man, she should not consent at once.
For men disparage what is easily obtained.

children.text: bhāvajijñāsārthaṃ paricārakamukhān saṃvāhakagāyanavaihāsikān gamye tadbhaktān vā praṇidadhyāt
children.translated_text: In order to find out his feeling, she should appoint attendants as spies: masseurs, singers, jesters, or men devoted to the approachable man.
In their absence, she should appoint a <s>pīṭhamarda</s> and others.

children.text: tebhyo nāyakasya śaucāśaucaṃ rāgāparāgau saktāsaktāṃ dānādāne ca vidyāt
children.translated_text: From them she should learn the lover's purity or impurity, his passion or lack of passion, his attachment or lack of attachment, and his giving or not giving.

children.text: saṃbhāvitena ca saha viṭapurogāṃ prītiṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: And with a promising man she should arrange affection through a <s>viṭa</s> as intermediary.
Under the pretext of quail, cock, and ram fights, of teaching parrots and mynahs to speak, of spectacles, and of the arts, the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> should bring the lover to her residence.
Or he should bring her to his residence.

children.text: āgatasya prītikautukajananaṃ kiṃcid dravyajātaṃ svayam idam asādhāraṇopabhogyam iti prītidāyaṃ dadyāt
children.translated_text: To him when he has arrived, she should affectionately give some sort of object that creates pleasure and curiosity, saying, 'This is for your exceptional private enjoyment.'

children.text: yatra ca ramate tayā goṣṭhyainam upacāraiśca rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he takes delight, through that gathering and through courtesies she should charm him.

children.text: gate ca saparihāsapralāpāṃ sopāyanāṃ paricārikām abhīkṣṇaṃ preṣayet
children.translated_text: When he has gone, she should often send a maidservant with joking conversation and with a gift.

children.text: sapīṭhamardāyāśca kāraṇāpadeśena svayaṃ gamanam iti gamyopāvartanam ||
children.translated_text: And she herself may go with the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> under the pretext of some reason. Thus ends the bringing around of an approachable man.
And here there are verses:
Betel, garlands, and prepared unguent
she should bring with affection for him when he has arrived, and she should arrange gatherings devoted to the arts.
She should give objects in affection, and should also make exchanges.
And she should herself indicate the intention of sexual union.
With gifts of affection, with suggestive remarks, and with courtesies alone,

children.text: gamyena saha saṃsṛṣṭā rañjayet taṃ tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: once she is connected with the approachable man, she should charm him thereafter.
When joined with the lover, in order to charm him she should follow the conduct of a woman devoted to one man.

children.text: rañjayenna tu sajjeta saktavacca viceṣṭeteti saṃkṣepoktiḥ
children.translated_text: The concise statement is this: she should charm him, but not become attached; she should act as though attached.

children.text: mātari ca krūraśīlāyām arthaparāyāṃ cāyattā syāt
children.translated_text: If her mother is cruel by nature and intent on money, she should be under her control.
In her absence, she should be under a foster-mother or madam.
But that woman should not become too fond of the approachable man,
and she should bring her daughter by force.

children.text: tatra tu nāyikāyāḥ saṃtatam aratir nirvedo vrīḍābhayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: In that situation the <s>nāyikā</s> should have constant dissatisfaction, disgust, shame, and fear,
but never transgression of the instruction.

children.text: vyādhiṃ caikam animittam ajugupsitam acakṣurgrāhyam anityaṃ ca khyāpayet
children.translated_text: She should announce a single illness that has no cause, is not disgusting, is not visible to the eye, and is temporary.

children.text: sati kāraṇe tadapadeśaṃ ca nāyakān abhigamanam
children.translated_text: When there is a reason, she should approach lovers under that pretext.

children.text: nirmālyasya tu nāyikā ceṭikāṃ preṣayet tāmbūlasya ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nāyikā</s> should send a maidservant with a worn garland and with betel.

children.text: vyavāye tadupacāreṣu vismayaś catuḥṣaṣṭyāṃ śiṣyatvaṃ tadupadiṣṭānāṃ ca yogānām ābhīkṣṇyenānuyogas tatsātmyād rahasi vṛttir manorathānām ākhyānaṃ guhyānāṃ vaikṛtapracchādanaṃ śayane parāvṛttasyānupekṣaṇam ānulomyaṃ guhyasparśane suptasya cumbanam āliṅganaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In intercourse and in his courtesies, she should show amazement; in the sixty-four arts, discipleship; and repeated practice of the techniques he has taught. Because of familiarity with him, she should behave privately, tell her desires, conceal deformities of the private parts, not neglect him when he has turned away in bed, be compliant when the private parts are touched, and kiss and embrace him while he sleeps.
She should look at him when his mind is elsewhere.
When she is standing in a mansion on the royal road and is recognized there by him, bashfulness and coy deception should disappear.
She should hate the one whom he hates,
and be fond of the one whom he loves.
She should follow him in joy and sorrow.
She should show curiosity about women.
Her anger should not last long.
Even with nail and tooth marks made by herself, she should suspect another woman.
She should not speak of her attachment in words, but should show it through outward signs.
In intoxication, sleep, and illness, however, she may speak it plainly,
and she may speak plainly of the lover's praiseworthy actions.
When he is speaking, she should grasp the meaning of his words.
Having understood it, she should speak on a subject fit for praise.
And she should connect his statement with a reply.
If he is affectionate,
she should follow along in stories, except when the subject is a rival woman.

children.text: niḥśvāse jṛmbhite skhalite patite vā tasya cārtim āśaṃsīta
children.translated_text: When he sighs, yawns, stumbles, or falls, she should express concern for his distress.
When he sneezes, speaks out, or is startled, she should say, 'Live!'
When she is downcast, she should use illness or a craving as the pretext.
She should not praise another man's qualities.
She should not censure one who has the same fault.
She should wear what he has given.
When he has been falsely offended or is in trouble, she should refuse ornaments and food.
And there should be lamentations suited to that situation.

children.text: tena saha deśamokṣaṃ rocayed rājani niṣkrayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: She should desire release from the country together with him, and ransom when he is in the king's power.
She should say that the possibility of her life depends on obtaining that.

children.text: tasyārthādhigame abhipretasiddhau śarīropacaye vā pūrvasaṃbhāṣita iṣṭadevatopahāraḥ
children.translated_text: When he has gained wealth, accomplished what he desired, or recovered his body, she should make an offering to the chosen deity as previously promised.
She should always wear ornaments.
She should eat in measured quantity.
and taking up his name and lineage in song;

children.text: glānyām urasi lalāṭe ca karaṃ kurvīta
children.translated_text: in weariness, she should place her hand on his chest and forehead;
having experienced that pleasure, there is the attainment of sleep;
and sitting and sleeping on his lap;
going away when there is separation;
therefore she should be desirous of a son;
she should not wish for any excess of lifespan beyond his.
She should not speak in private of a matter of his that is not known.

children.text: vratam upavāsaṃ cāsya nirvartayet mayi doṣa iti
children.translated_text: She should complete his vow and fast, saying, "The fault is mine."
When this is impossible, she herself should take on that same form.
In a dispute, the statement of the matter is that even by him it is impossible.

children.text: tadīyam ātmīyaṃ vā svayam aviśeṣeṇa paśyet
children.translated_text: She should view what is his or her own without making any distinction.
She should not go to gatherings and the like without him.
She should praise the wearing of his cast-off garlands and the eating of his leavings.
She should honor his family, character, arts, birth, learning, complexion, wealth, country, friends, virtues, age, and sweetness.
She should urge him, when he is skilled, in singing and the other arts.
She should go to him without regard for fear, cold, heat, or rain.

children.text: sa eva ca me syād ityaurdhvadehikeṣu vacanam
children.translated_text: In matters concerning the next world she should say, "May he alone be mine."
She should conform to his preferred tastes, feelings, and character.
There is suspicion of root-magic.

children.text: tadabhigamane ca jananyā saha nityo vivādaḥ
children.translated_text: And in going to him there is constant quarrel with her mother.

children.text: balāt kāreṇa ca yadyanyatra tayā nīyeta tadā viṣamanaśanaṃ śastraṃ rajjum iti kāmayeta
children.translated_text: And if she is led elsewhere by her mother by force, then she should long for poison, fasting to death, a weapon, or a rope.
She should make the lover trust her through spies.
Or she herself should undertake her own livelihood.
But there should never be a dispute over money.
Without her mother she should not undertake anything at all.
When he is abroad, she should lay a curse for his quick return.
When he has gone abroad, there should be a rule about cleansing and a prohibition of adornment.
But auspicious observances should be attended to.
Or she should wear a single conch bracelet.
She should remember past things.
She should yearn toward the constellations, moon, sun, and stars.
On seeing an agreeable dream she should say, "May union with him be mine."
There should be agitation at an inauspicious dream and a rite of pacification.
When he has returned, there should be <s>kāmapūjā</s>, worship connected with love.
She should make offerings to the deities.
Her friends should bring a full vessel.
And there should be <s>vāyasapūjā</s>, worship of the crow.
After the first union, this same procedure is followed, except for the worship of the crow.
And she should say that, if he is attached, she will die with him.

children.text: nisṛṣṭabhāvaḥ samānavṛttiḥ prayojanakārī nirāśaṅko nirapekṣo 'rtheṣv iti saktalakṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: Full surrender of feeling, equal conduct, action for his benefit, freedom from suspicion, and indifference in monetary matters: these are the marks of one attached.
This has been stated from <s>Dattaka</s>'s teaching for the sake of illustration.
What has not been stated she should learn from common practice and from the nature of the man.
And on this point there are two verses:
Because of subtlety, excessive greed, and also ignorance of their nature,

children.text: kāmalakṣma tu durjñānaṃ strīṇāṃ tadbhāvitair api ||
children.translated_text: the mark of passion in women is hard to know even by those who live with them.
They desire, become indifferent, charm, and abandon;
even while drawing away all one's wealth, women are never really known.
The taking of wealth from an attached man and others is both natural and by stratagem.

children.text: tatra svābhāvikaṃ saṃkalpāt samadhikaṃ vā labhamānā nopāyān prayuñjītetyācāryāḥ
children.translated_text: In that matter, the teachers say that when she is receiving what was agreed upon or more, she should not employ stratagems.

children.text: viditam apyupāyaiḥ pariṣkṛtaṃ dviguṇaṃ dāsyatīti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vātsyāyana</s> says: even what is known, when embellished by stratagems, will give twice as much.
For ornaments, foods to chew, foods to eat, drinks, garlands, clothes, perfumes, valuables, and the like, she may obtain a loan on credit from merchants, with repayment in money.
In his presence she should praise his wealth.
She may use the pretext of giving out of affection for vows, trees, parks, temples, tanks, gardens, and festivals.
On account of going to him, her ornaments may be stolen by guards or thieves.
There may be loss of property in the house because of fire, a break in the wall, or negligence.

children.text: tathā yācitālaṃkārāṇāṃ nāyakālaṃkārāṇāṃ ca tadabhigamanārthasya vyayasya praṇidhibhir nivedanam
children.translated_text: Likewise, through spies, she may report the expense incurred for going to him, both for borrowed ornaments and for the lover's own ornaments.
She may take a loan for his sake.
She may fail to go to the affairs of friends because she has no gift to bring.

children.text: taiśca pūrvam āhṛtā guravo 'bhihārāḥ pūrvam upanītāḥ pūrvaṃ śrāvitāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: And by those friends, the costly gifts previously brought, previously presented, and previously made known should have been brought beforehand.
There may be an interruption of customary rites.
For the lover's sake, work should be commissioned from craftsmen.
There may be an act of assistance for a physician or high official for the sake of some business.
And there may be support for helpful friends in their misfortunes.
There may be household work.

children.text: sakhyāḥ putrasyotsañjanam dohado vyādhir mitrasya duḥkhāpanayanam iti
children.translated_text: The excitement of a friend's son, a pregnancy craving, illness, or the removal of a friend's distress: such are pretexts.
She may sell part of an ornament for the lover's sake.

children.text: tayā śīlitasya cālaṃkārasya bhāṇḍopaskarasya vā vaṇijo vikrayārthaṃ darśanam
children.translated_text: Or she may show to a merchant, for sale, an ornament or household equipment that has been used by her.

children.text: pratigaṇikānāṃ ca sadṛśasya bhāṇḍasya vyatikare prativiśiṣṭasya grahaṇam
children.translated_text: And when courtesan rivals have similar goods, she should take something especially superior in exchange.
She should not forget former favors and should recount them.
Through spies she should have the courtesan rivals hear of her excessive gain.

children.text: tāsu nāyakasamakṣam ātmano 'bhyadhikaṃ lābhaṃ bhūtam abhūtaṃ vā vrīḍitā nāma varṇayet
children.translated_text: In the lover's presence, as if embarrassed, she should describe a gain of her own greater than theirs, whether real or unreal.

children.text: pūrvayogināṃ ca lābhātiśayena punaḥ saṃdhāne yatamānānām āviṣkṛtaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ
children.translated_text: There should be an open refusal of former partners who, because of excessive profit, are trying to make an alliance again.
She should point out those rivaling him who are fit to be abandoned.
"He will not come again": this is a childish request. These are the means of acquiring wealth.

children.text: viraktaṃ ca nityam eva prakṛtivikriyāto vidyāt mukhavarṇācca ||
children.translated_text: And a man who is estranged should always be recognized from a change in his nature and from the color of his face.
He gives too little or too much.
He becomes connected with hostile people.
Having given one pretext, he does something else.
He cuts off what was customary.
He forgets what was promised.
He speaks by signs with his own party.
Under the pretext of a friend's business, he sleeps elsewhere.
And he talks privately with the attendants of a woman with whom he was formerly connected.

children.text: tasya sāradravyāṇi prāg avabodhād anyāpadeśena haste kurvīta
children.translated_text: Before he becomes aware of it, she should get his valuable property into her own hands under some other pretext.

children.text: tāni cāsyā hastād uttamarṇaḥ prasahya gṛhṇīyāt
children.translated_text: And a creditor should forcibly take those things from her hand.

children.text: vivadamānena saha dharmastheṣu vyavahared iti viraktapratipattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: While he disputes, she should go to law with him before the judges. Such is the procedure toward one who has become estranged.
But a man who is attached, even if he has been helpful before, should be kept on with false affection if he yields only little profit.
But one who has no substance and from whom nothing can be obtained should be driven away by stratagems,
after she has secured another man.
Serving what is disagreeable to him,
practicing what he condemns,
withholding the enjoyment of her lips,
striking the ground with her foot,
conversation on a subject he does not understand,
and, when he does understand it, lack of wonder and disparagement,
breaking his pride,
association with men superior to him,
not looking at him,
criticizing people who have the same faults as he does,
and staying apart in private.
Anxiety during the services of lovemaking,
turning her face away,
guarding her hips,
disgust at scratches from nails and bites from teeth,
interposing the needle of her arm between them in an embrace,
stiffness of the limbs,
crossing the thighs,
and devotion to sleep.
When she sees that he is tired, urging him on,
laughing when he is unable,
and showing no delight when he is able,
even by day,
when she sees his feeling, going among many people.
Taking hold of quibbles in his statements,
laughing when there is no joke,

children.text: narmaṇi cānyam apadiśya hasati vadati tasmin kaṭākṣeṇa parijanasya prekṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: and, when there is a joke, laughing and speaking while referring to someone else, and looking sidelong at the attendants and striking them while he is present,
cutting off his story and starting other stories,
recounting his wrongs and his unavoidable vices,
and having a maidservant bring up his vulnerable points,
not being visible when he has arrived,
asking for what should not be asked,
and, in the end, release of herself by her own act: this is <s>Dattaka</s>'s teaching concerning the woman who has a keeper.
And here there are two verses:
Union with men fit to be approached after examining them, winning over the man once united,

children.text: raktād arthasya cādānam ante mokṣaśca vaiśikam ||
children.translated_text: taking wealth from him when he is attached, and release at the end: this is the courtesan's profession.

children.text: evam etena kalpena sthitā veśyā parigrahe
children.translated_text: A courtesan who remains in keeping according to this rule
is not deceived by clients and makes abundant gains.

children.text: vartamānaṃ niṣpīḍitārtham utsṛjantī pūrvasaṃsṛṣṭena saha saṃdadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning a present lover whose wealth has been squeezed out, she should make terms with one with whom she was formerly connected.

children.text: sa ced avasitārtho vittavān sānurāgaśca tataḥ saṃdheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he has lost his wealth but is again wealthy and still affectionate, then he should be reconciled with.
If he has gone elsewhere, he must be considered carefully.
According to the logic of the case, he is of six kinds.

children.text: itaḥ svayam apasṛtas tato 'pi svayam evāpasṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: One who left here of his own accord and left there too of his own accord;
one who left after being expelled both from here and from there;
one who left here of his own accord and left there after being expelled;
one who left here of his own accord and remained there;
one who left here after being expelled and left there of his own accord;
and one who left here after being expelled and remained there.

children.text: itastataśca svayam evāpasṛtyopajapati ced ubhayor guṇān apekṣī calabuddhir asaṃdheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, after leaving both here and there of his own accord, he courts her, he is looking for the advantages of both women, fickle-minded, and not to be reconciled with.
One who has left after being expelled both from here and from there has a steady mind.

children.text: sa ced anyato bahulabhamānayā niṣkāsitaḥ syāt sasāro 'pi tayā roṣito mamāmarṣād bahu dāsyatīti saṃdheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he was expelled by another woman who was receiving much from someone else, then, even if he has substance, he is angry with her; thinking, 'Out of resentment he will give me much,' she may reconcile with him.

children.text: niḥsāratayā kadaryatayā vā tyakto na śreyān ||
children.translated_text: But one rejected because he is without substance or because he is miserly is of no advantage.

children.text: itaḥ svayam apasṛtastato niṣkāsitāpasṛto yadyatiriktam ādau ca dadyāt tataḥ pratigrāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If one who left here of his own accord and left there after being expelled should first give something extra, then he may be accepted.

children.text: itaḥ svayam apasṛtya tatra sthita upajapaṃstarkayitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who left here of his own accord, remained there, and now courts her must be considered carefully.

children.text: viśeṣārthī cāgatastato viśeṣam apaśyann āgantukāmo māṃ jijñāsitukāmaḥ sa āgatya sānurāgatvād dāsyati
children.translated_text: He may have come seeking some special advantage; then, seeing no special advantage there and wishing to come back, he may wish to test me. When he comes, because he is affectionate, he will give.

children.text: tasyāṃ vā doṣān dṛṣṭvā mayi bhūyiṣṭhān guṇān adhunā paśyati sa guṇadarśī bhūyiṣṭhaṃ dāsyati ||
children.translated_text: Or, having seen faults in her, he now sees more numerous virtues in me. As one who sees virtues, he will give the most.

children.text: bālo vā naikatradṛṣṭir atisaṃdhānapradhāno vā haridrārāgo vā yat kiṃcanakārī vā ityavetya saṃdadhyān na vā ||
children.translated_text: Or he may be childish, not fixed on one place, chiefly intent on deception, attached like the color of turmeric, or ready to do anything whatsoever; having ascertained this, she may or may not reconcile with him.
One who left here after being expelled and left there of his own accord, when he courts her, must be considered carefully:
he may wish to come out of affection, and he will give much;

children.text: mama guṇair bhāvito yo 'nyasyāṃ na ramate ||
children.translated_text: he may be so impressed by my virtues that he takes no pleasure in another woman.

children.text: pūrvam ayogena vā mayā niṣkāsitaḥ sa māṃ śīlayitvā vairaṃ niryātayitukāmo dhanam abhiyogād vā mayāsyāpahṛtaṃ tadviśvāsya pratīpam ādātukāmo nirveṣṭukāmo vā māṃ vartamānodbhedayitvā tyaktukāma ityakalyāṇabuddhir asaṃdheyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or he may have been expelled by me before for improper conduct; after becoming familiar with me he may wish to repay hostility. Or wealth may have been taken from him by me through a claim, and after winning my trust he may wish to take it back in return, or to recover it, or to break up my present lover and then abandon me. Such a man of evil intent is not to be reconciled with.
One whose intention is otherwise should be made to wait over time.

children.text: ito niṣkāsitastatra sthita upajapann etena vyākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who was expelled from here and remains there while courting her is explained by this same rule.
When these men are courting her while staying elsewhere, she herself should court one of them.

children.text: vyalīkārthaṃ niṣkāsito mayāsāvanyatra gato yatnād ānetavyaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This man, expelled by me because of a wrong, has gone elsewhere and should be brought back with effort.

children.text: itaḥ pravṛttasaṃbhāṣo vā tato bhedam avāpsyati
children.translated_text: Or, if conversation is begun from here, he will obtain a breach there.
Or he will cause a loss of wealth to my present lover.
Or it is his time for acquiring wealth.
His position has increased.
He has obtained authority.
He is separated from his wife.
He has turned away from dependence on another.
He has been separated from his father or brother.

children.text: anena vā pratibaddham anena saṃdhiṃ kṛtvā nāyakaṃ dhaninam avāpsyāmi
children.translated_text: Or someone is bound to him; by making an alliance with him I shall obtain a wealthy lover.

children.text: vimānito vā bhāryayā tam eva tasyāṃ vikramayiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Or he has been slighted by his wife, and I shall make him act boldly against her.

children.text: asya vā mitraṃ maddveṣiṇīṃ sapatnīṃ kāmayate tad amunā bhedayiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: Or his friend desires a co-wife who hates me; I shall split her from him by means of this man.
Or, because he is fickle-minded, I shall bring him into contempt.'

children.text: tasya pīṭhamardādayo mātur dauḥśīlyena nāyikāyāḥ satyapyanurāge vivaśāyāḥ pūrvaṃ niṣkāsanaṃ varṇayeyuḥ
children.translated_text: His <s>pīṭhamarda</s>s and the others should describe how, because of the mother's bad character, the <s>nāyikā</s>, though she had affection, was formerly driven away while helpless.
They should also describe her present unwilling association and her hatred of it.
And by tokens of recognition, connected with her former affection, they should make him trust her again.

children.text: abhijñānaṃ ca tatkṛtopakārasambaddhaṃ syād iti viśīrṇapratisaṃdhānam ||
children.translated_text: The token of recognition should be connected with some service done by him. Thus there is the renewal of a broken bond.
Between one not previously enjoyed and one formerly enjoyed, the one formerly enjoyed is better.

children.text: sa hi viditaśīlo dṛṣṭarāgaśca sūpacāro bhavatītyācāryāḥ
children.translated_text: For his character is known, his passion has been seen, and he is easy to serve, say the teachers.

children.text: pūrvasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ sarvato niṣpīḍitārthatvān nātyartham arthado duḥkhaṃ ca punarviśvāsayitum
children.translated_text: One formerly enjoyed, however, because his resources have been pressed from every side, is not an especially great giver of money, and it is difficult to make him trust again.
But one not previously enjoyed becomes attached easily, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Even so, the distinction depends on the nature of the man.
And here there are verses:

children.text: anyāṃ bhedayituṃ gamyād anyato gamyam eva vā
children.translated_text: Renewal of a connection is desired in order to split him from another woman, or to make accessible a man who has come from elsewhere,
and also in order to injure one who is already established.
Where a deeply attached man fears union with another and does not notice offenses,

children.text: atisaktaḥ pumān yatra bhayād bahu dadāti ca ||
children.translated_text: and from fear gives much,
there she should welcome the unattached man and likewise slight the attached one,
and the man who is very skilled when other messengers descend upon him.
There, in time, a woman should connect herself first with the one who approaches,
and she should have an unbroken bond, yet should not abandon the attached man.

children.text: saktaṃ tu vaśinaṃ nārī sambhāṣyāpyanyato vrajet
children.translated_text: But after speaking with an attached man who is under her control, the woman may go elsewhere;
then, having taken money from there, she should charm the attached man again.

children.text: āyatiṃ prasamīkṣyādau lābhaṃ prītiṃ ca puṣkalām
children.translated_text: Considering future advantage at the outset, and abundant profit and affection,
a clever woman should renew a friendship that has fallen apart.

children.text: gamyabāhulye bahu pratidinaṃ ca labhamānā naikaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: When approachable men are numerous and she is receiving much every day, she should not accept only one.

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ sthitim ātmano guṇān saubhāgyaṃ cānyābhyo nyūnātiriktatāṃ cāvekṣya rajanyām arthaṃ sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: After considering the place, the time, her own situation, her qualities, her good fortune, and whether she is inferior or superior to other women, she should set the price for the night.
She should employ female messengers toward an approachable man.
And she herself should send those who are connected with him.
For the sake of taking an exceptional gain, she may go even to one man who says, 'Two, three, four.'
And she should manage the taking of gifts.

children.text: gamyayaugapadye tu lābhasāmye yad dravyārthinī syāt taddāyini viśeṣaḥ pratyakṣa ityācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when approachable men come at the same time, if the gain is equal and she desires some particular object, the preference is clearly for the giver of that object, say the teachers.
Because it cannot be refused, and because all undertakings have that as their basis, the preference is for the giver of gold, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.

Among gold, silver, copper, bell-metal, iron vessels, furnishings, bedding, coverlets, special garments, perfumes, pungent goods, ghee, oil, grain, and kinds of livestock, each earlier item is superior to the following one.

children.text: yat tatra sāmyād vā dravyasāmye mitravākyād atipātitvād āyatito gamyaguṇataḥ prītitaśca viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If there is equality there, or equality in the goods, then preference depends on a friend's word, urgency, future advantage, the qualities of the approachable man, and affection.
Between a passionate man and a generous man, the preference is clearly for the generous man, say the teachers.
For giving can be made to arise in a passionate man.

children.text: lubdho 'pi hi raktastyajati na tu tyāgī nirbandhād rajyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even a greedy man gives when he is enamored, but a generous man does not become enamored through pressure, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Among such men, between a wealthy man and a poor man, the wealthy man is preferable.
Between a generous man and one who accomplishes a purpose, the preference is clearly for the one who accomplishes the purpose, say the teachers.

children.text: prayojanakartā sakṛt kṛtvā kṛtinam ātmānaṃ manyate tyāgī punar atītaṃ nāpekṣata iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who accomplishes a purpose, having done it once, thinks himself successful; but a generous man does not take account of what is past, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Even there, preference depends on urgency.
Between a grateful man and a generous man, the preference is clearly for the generous man, say the teachers.

children.text: ciram ārādhito 'pi tyāgī vyalīkam ekam upalabhya pratigaṇikayā vā mithyādūṣitaḥ śramam atītaṃ nāpekṣate
children.translated_text: A generous man, even after being served for a long time, if he notices a single offense or is falsely accused by a rival courtesan, does not take account of the labor already spent.

children.text: prāyeṇa hi tejasvina ṛjavo 'nādṛtāśca tyāgino bhavanti
children.translated_text: For generous men are usually spirited, straightforward, and not submissive.
But a grateful man, taking account of earlier effort, does not suddenly lose affection.

children.text: parīkṣitaśīlatvācca na mithyā dūṣyata iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because his character has been tested, he is not falsely accused, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Even there, preference depends on future advantage.
Between a friend's word and the arrival of money, the preference is clearly for the arrival of money, say the teachers.
For that arrival of money too will take place.

children.text: mitraṃ tu sakṛd vākye pratihate kaluṣitaṃ syād iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But a friend whose word has once been rejected becomes embittered, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Even there, preference depends on urgency.

children.text: tatra kāryasaṃdarśanena mitram anunīya śvobhūte vacanam astv iti tato 'tipātinam arthaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: In that case, after conciliating the friend by showing the task to be done and saying, 'Let your word be fulfilled tomorrow,' she should then accept the urgent money.
Between the arrival of money and the prevention of misfortune, the preference is clearly for the arrival of money, say the teachers.

children.text: arthaḥ parimitāvacchedaḥ anarthaḥ punaḥ sakṛtprasṛto na jñāyate kvāvatiṣṭhata iti vātsyāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wealth has a limited boundary; but misfortune, once it has spread, is not known where it will stop, says <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Even there, preference depends on relative heaviness and lightness.
By this, the preference for counteracting misfortune over doubtful wealth has been explained.

children.text: devakulataḍāgārāmāṇām karaṇam sthalīnām agnicaityānāṃ nibandhanam gosahasrāṇāṃ pātrāntaritaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dānam devatānāṃ pūjopahārapravartanam tadvyayasahiṣṇor vā dhanasya parigrahaṇam ityuttamagaṇikānāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction of temples, tanks, and gardens; the establishing of fire-shrines on open grounds; the giving of a thousand cows to brahmans through a suitable recipient; the institution of worship and offerings for deities; or the acceptance of wealth from one able to bear such expense: this is the exceptional gain of the highest courtesans.
A complete set of ornaments for the whole body, the making of a spacious house,

children.text: mahārhair bhāṇḍaiḥ paricārakaiśca gṛhaparicchadasyojjvalateti rūpājīvānāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the brightening of the household furnishings with costly vessels and attendants: this is the exceptional gain of women who live by beauty.

children.text: nityaṃ śuklam ācchādanam apakṣudham annapānaṃ nityaṃ saugandhikena tāmbūlena ca yogaḥ sahiraṇyabhāgam alaṃkaraṇam iti kumbhadāsīnāṃ lābhātiśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Daily white clothing, food and drink without stint, constant connection with perfumes and betel, and adornment with a share of gold: this is the special gain of the slave-courtesans.

children.text: etena pradeśena madhyamādhamānām api lābhātiśayān sarvāsām eva yojayed ityācāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this indication, the teachers say, one should apply special gains to all women of the middle and lower classes as well.
But according to <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, this mode of livelihood, with its gains and the like, is not fixed, since it depends on place, time, resources, capacity, affection, and local practice.

children.text: gamyam anyato nivārayitukāmā saktam anyasyām apahartukāmā vā anyāṃ vā lābhato viyuyukṣamāṇāgamyasaṃsargād ātmanaḥ sthānaṃ vṛddhim āyatim abhigamyatāṃ ca manyamānā anarthapratīkāre vā sāhāyam enaṃ kārayitukāmā saktasya vā anyasya vyalīkārthinī pūrvopakāram akṛtam iva paśyantī kevala prītyarthinī vā kalyāṇabuddher alpam api lābhaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: If she wishes to keep a man fit to be approached from going to another woman, or to draw away a man attached to another, or to deprive another woman of profit, or if she thinks that from association with a man not ordinarily accessible she will gain standing, increase, future prospects, and desirability, or if she wishes to make him help in remedying a misfortune, or wishes to wrong another man who is attached, or regards an earlier service as if it had not been repaid, or merely seeks affection from one of good disposition, she may accept even a small gain.

children.text: āyatyarthinī tu tam āśritya cānarthaṃ praticikīrṣantī naiva pratigṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: But if she seeks future advantage and intends, by relying on him, to remedy a misfortune, she should not accept anything at all.

children.text: tyakṣyāmyenam anyataḥ pratisaṃdhāsyāmi gamiṣyati dārair yokṣyate nāśayiṣyatyanarthān aṅkuśabhūta uttarādhyakṣo 'syāgamiṣyati svāmī pitā vā sthānabhraṃśo vāsya bhaviṣyati calacittaśceti manyamānā tadātve tasmāl lābham icchet ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'I shall abandon him; I shall make an alliance elsewhere; he will go away; he will be joined with his wife; he will remove my troubles; his superior officer, acting as a goad, will come, or his master or father; he will lose his position; or he is fickle-minded,' she should seek gain from him at the present time.

children.text: pratijñātam īśvareṇa pratigrahaṃ lapsyate adhikaraṇaṃ sthānaṃ vā prāpsyati vṛttikālo 'sya vā āsannaḥ vāhanam asyā gamiṣyati sthalapattraṃ vā sasyam asya pakṣyate kṛtam asmin na naśyati nityam avisaṃvādako vetyāyatyām icchet
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'He will obtain the gift promised by a powerful man; he will obtain an office or position; the time of his livelihood is near; his vehicle will arrive; or his land document or crop will mature; what has been done for him will not be wasted; or he is always one who does not deceive,' she should seek gain in the future.
Or she should act according to the rule for being kept as a mistress.
And on this point there are verses:
Those whose wealth has been obtained with difficulty, and harsh men who are favorites of kings,

children.text: āyātyāṃ ca tadātve ca dūrād eva vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should avoid from afar, both with regard to future gain and present gain.
Those whose avoidance brings misfortune and whose approach likewise brings prosperity,
one should secure even with effort, and begin with a plausible pretext.

children.text: prasannā ye prayacchanti svalpe apyagaṇitaṃ vasu
children.translated_text: Those who, when pleased, give wealth without counting it, even on a small occasion,

children.text: sthūlalakṣān mahotsāhāṃstān gacchet svair api vyayaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: men of large aims and great energy: one should approach them even at one's own expense.
When gains are being pursued, losses, further consequences, and doubts also arise.

children.text: te buddhidaurbalyād atirāgād atyabhimānād atidambhād atyārjavād ativiśvāsād atikrodhāt pramādāt sāhasād daivayogācca syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: These may arise from weakness of judgment, excessive passion, excessive self-regard, excessive deceit, excessive straightforwardness, excessive trust, excessive anger, negligence, rashness, and the operation of fate.

children.text: teṣāṃ phalaṃ kṛtasya vyayasya niṣphalatvam anāyatirāgam iṣyato 'rthasya nivartanam āptasya niṣkramaṇaṃ pāruṣyasya prāptir gamyatā śarīrasya praghātaḥ keśānāṃ chedanaṃ pātanam aṅgavaikalyāpattiḥ
children.translated_text: Their results are the fruitlessness of the expense incurred, absence of future affection, reversal of the desired gain, loss of what has been obtained, the experience of harsh treatment, becoming accessible to others, injury to the body, cutting of the hair, being cast down, and the occurrence of bodily deformity.

children.text: tasmāt tān ādita eva parijihīrṣed arthabhūyiṣṭhāṃścopekṣeta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should seek to avoid them from the very beginning, and one should pass over even those cases in which wealth is predominant.
<s>Artha</s> (material gain), <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) are the triad of aims.
<s>Anartha</s> (loss), <s>adharma</s> (wrong conduct), and hatred are the triad opposed to the aims.
When these are being pursued, the accomplishment of another among them is a further consequence.

children.text: saṃdigdhāyāṃ tu phalaprāptau syād vā na veti śuddhasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the attainment of the result is doubtful, 'Will it occur or not?' is a pure doubt.

children.text: idaṃ vā syād idaṃ veti saṃkīrṇaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Will it be this or that?' is a mixed doubt.

children.text: ekasmin kriyamāṇe kārye kāryadvayasyotpattir ubhayato yogaḥ
children.translated_text: When one task is being undertaken and two results arise, that is connection on both sides.

children.text: samantād utpattiḥ samantatoyoga iti tān udāhariṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Arising on all sides is connection on all sides; we shall illustrate these cases.
The triad of aims has the form already considered.
The triad of losses is precisely the opposite of it.

children.text: yasyottamasyābhigamane pratyakṣato 'rthalābho grahaṇīyatvam āyatir āgamaḥ prārthanīyatvaṃ cānyeṣāṃ syāt so 'rtho 'rthānubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, in approaching an excellent man, there is direct acquisition of wealth, acceptability, future income, and desirability to others, that is <s>artha</s> with a further consequence of <s>artha</s>.

children.text: lābhamātre kasyacid anyasya gamanaṃ so 'rtho niranubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going to some other man for mere gain is <s>artha</s> without further consequence.

children.text: anyārthaparigrahe saktād āyaticchedanam arthasya niṣkramaṇaṃ lokavidviṣṭasya vā nīcasya gamanam āyatighnam artho 'narthānubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, in taking up with someone for the sake of another gain, future prospects are cut off by the man who is attached, wealth is lost, or going to a man hated by people or low-born damages future prospects, that is <s>artha</s> with a further consequence of <s>anartha</s>.

children.text: svena vyayena śūrasya mahāmātrasya prabhavato vā lubdhasya gamanaṃ niṣphalam api vyasanapratīkārārthaṃ mahataścārthaghnasya nimittasya praśamanam āyatijananaṃ vā so 'nartho 'rthānubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going at one's own expense to a brave man, a high official, or a powerful greedy man may be fruitless in itself, yet may serve to remedy a danger, pacify a great cause of loss of wealth, or create future advantage; that is <s>anartha</s> with a further consequence of <s>artha</s>.

children.text: kadaryasya subhagamāninaḥ kṛtaghnasya vātisaṃdhānaśīlasya svair api vyayaistathārādhanam ante niṣphalaṃ so 'nartho niranubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Appeasing, even at one's own expense, a miser who thinks himself handsome, an ungrateful man, or one habitually deceitful, is fruitless in the end; that is <s>anartha</s> without further consequence.

children.text: tasyaiva rājavallabhasya krauryaprabhāvādhikasya tathaivārādhanam ante niṣphalaṃ niṣkāsanaṃ ca doṣakaraṃ so 'nartho 'narthānubandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Appeasing that same man when he is a favorite of the king and superior in cruelty and power is likewise fruitless in the end, and expelling him brings danger; that is <s>anartha</s> with a further consequence of <s>anartha</s>.
In the same way one should apply further consequences also to <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>.
And by mutual reasoning one should combine them; these are the further consequences.
Even if he has been pleased, will he give or not? This is doubt about <s>artha</s>.

children.text: niṣpīḍitārtham aphalam utsṛjantyā artham alabhamānāyā dharmaḥ syān na veti dharmasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: For a woman who abandons a source of wealth that has been squeezed dry and is fruitless, and who receives no money, will there be <s>dharma</s> or not? This is doubt about <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: abhipretam upalabhya paricārakam anyaṃ vā kṣudraṃ gatvā kāmaḥ syān na veti kāmasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: After obtaining the desired man, if she goes to an attendant or some other low man, will there be <s>kāma</s> or not? This is doubt about <s>kāma</s>.
The doubt concerning harm is: will an insignificant but influential man, though not desired, cause harm or not?

children.text: atyantaniṣphalaḥ saktaḥ parityaktaḥ pitṛlokaṃ yāyāt tatrādharmaḥ syān na vetyadharmasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The doubt concerning <s>adharma</s> is: if a passionately attached man who is utterly without benefit is abandoned, he might go to the world of the fathers; would there be <s>adharma</s> in that or not?
Even when passion is to be declared, if the intended object is not obtained, there is loss of passion.
Thus are the pure doubts.
Now the mixed ones.

children.text: āgantor aviditaśīlasya vallabhasaṃśrayasya prabhaviṣṇor vā samupasthitasyārādhanam artho 'nartha iti saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When a visitor whose character is unknown, or one who is protected by a favorite, or one who is powerful, presents himself, the doubt is whether gratifying him is profit or harm.

children.text: śrotriyasya brahmacāriṇo dīkṣitasya vratino liṅgino vā māṃ dṛṣṭvā jātarāgasya mumūrṣor mitravākyād ānṛśaṃsyācca gamanaṃ dharmo 'dharma iti saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When a <s>śrotriya</s>, a celibate student, an initiated man, a vow-keeper, or an ascetic marked by a sectarian sign, having seen me, has fallen in love and is about to die, going to him at a friend's word and out of compassion is a doubt between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.

children.text: lokād evākṛtapratyayād aguṇo guṇavān vetyanavekṣya gamanaṃ kāmo dveṣa iti saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Going to a man without examination, from public report alone and without established confidence, while asking whether he is without qualities or possessed of qualities, is a doubt between desire and aversion.
And they may be mixed with one another; thus are the mixed doubts.

children.text: yatra parasyābhigamane arthaḥ saktācca saṃgharṣataḥ sa ubhayayo 'rthaḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is profit in approaching another man, and also profit from an attached man through rivalry, that is profit on both sides.

children.text: yatra svena vyayena niṣphalam abhigamanaṃ saktāccāmarṣitād vittapratyādānaṃ sa ubhayato 'narthaḥ
children.translated_text: Where an approach made at one's own expense is fruitless, and from an attached but resentful man there is the demanding back of wealth, that is harm on both sides.

children.text: yatrābhigamane artho bhaviṣyati na vetyāśaṅkā sakto 'pi saṃgharṣād dāsyati na veti sa ubhayato 'rthasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, in approaching him, there is uncertainty whether profit will arise or not, and whether an attached man will give because of rivalry or not, that is doubt of profit on both sides.

children.text: yatrābhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ krodhād apakāraṃ kariṣyati na veti sakto vāmarṣito dattaṃ pratyādāsyati na veti sa ubhayato 'narthasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where, in an approach involving expense, there is uncertainty whether a former hostile man of influence will do injury from anger or not, or whether an attached but resentful man will take back what was given or not, that is doubt of harm on both sides.
Thus are <s>Auddālaki</s>'s two-sided conjunctures.
But the followers of <s>Bābhravya</s> say:

children.text: yatrābhigamane artho 'nabhigamane ca saktād arthaḥ sa ubhayato 'rthaḥ
children.translated_text: Where there is profit in approaching, and also profit from an attached man in not approaching, that is profit on both sides.

children.text: yatrābhigamane niṣphalo vyayo 'nabhigamane ca niṣpratīkāro 'narthaḥ sa ubhayato 'narthaḥ
children.translated_text: Where in approaching there is fruitless expense, and in not approaching there is irremediable harm, that is harm on both sides.

children.text: yatrābhigamane nirvyayo dāsyati na veti saṃśayo 'nabhigamane sakto dāsyati na veti sa ubhayato 'rthasaṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where in approaching without expense there is doubt whether he will give or not, and in not approaching there is doubt whether an attached man will give or not, that is doubt of profit on both sides.

children.text: yatrābhigamane vyayavati pūrvo viruddhaḥ prabhāvavān prāpsyate na veti saṃśayo 'nabhigamane ca krodhād anarthaṃ kariṣyati na veti sa ubhayato 'narthasaṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where in an approach involving expense there is doubt whether a former hostile man of influence will be obtained or not, and in not approaching there is doubt whether he will cause harm from anger or not, that is doubt of harm on both sides.

children.text: eteṣām eva vyatikare anyato 'rtho 'nyato 'nartho 'nyato 'rtho 'nyato 'rthasaṃśayo 'nyato 'rtho 'nyato 'narthasaṃśaya iti ṣaṭsaṃkīrṇayogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In permutations of these same cases, with profit from one side and harm from another, profit from one side and doubt of profit from another, or profit from one side and doubt of harm from another, there are six mixed conjunctures, including the reversals.

children.text: teṣu sahāyaiḥ saha vimṛśya yato 'rthabhūyiṣṭho 'rthasaṃśayo gurur anarthapraśamo vā tataḥ pravarteta ||
