children.translated_text: Among these, after deliberating with assistants, she should proceed from the side where profit is greatest, where the chance of profit is weightiest, or where harm is most calmed.
In this same way one should illustrate <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> also by this reasoning.
And they may be mixed with one another and combined with one another; thus are the two-sided conjunctures.

children.text: sambhūya ca viṭāḥ parigṛhṇantyekām asau goṣṭhīparigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: When libertines jointly maintain one woman, that is possession by a circle.

children.text: sā teṣām itastataḥ saṃsṛjyamānā pratyekaṃ saṃgharṣād arthaṃ nirvartayet
children.translated_text: As she associates with them here and there, she should obtain profit from each individually through rivalry.

children.text: suvasantakādiṣu ca yoge yo me imam amuṃ ca saṃpādayiṣyati tasyādya gamiṣyati me duhiteti mātrā vācayet
children.translated_text: On occasions such as <s>Suvasantaka</s>, the mother should have it announced: 'My daughter will go today to the one who procures this man and that man for me.'

children.text: teṣāṃ ca saṃgharṣaje abhigamane kāryāṇi lakṣayet
children.translated_text: And in approaches born from their rivalry, she should observe the things to be done.

children.text: ekato 'rthaḥ sarvato 'rthaḥ ekato 'narthaḥ sarvato 'nartho 'rdhato 'rthaḥ sarvato 'rthaḥ ardhato 'narthaḥ sarvato 'narthaḥ
children.translated_text: Profit from one side, profit from all sides; harm from one side, harm from all sides; profit from half, profit from all sides; harm from half, harm from all sides.
Thus are the conjunctures on all sides.
She should apply doubt of profit and doubt of harm as before.
And she should mix them in the same way, and <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> as well.
Thus end the considerations of consequent profit, harm, and doubt.

children.text: kumbhadāsī paricārikā kulaṭā svairiṇī naṭī śilpakārikā prakāśavinaṣṭā rūpājīvā gaṇikā ceti veśyāviśeṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A water-pot slave-girl, an attendant, an unchaste married woman, an independent woman, an actress, a craftswoman, a publicly ruined woman, a woman who lives by her beauty, and a courtesan: these are the special types of prostitute.

children.text: sarvāsāṃ cānurūpeṇa gamyāḥ sahāyāstad uparañjanam arthāgamopāyā niṣkāsanaṃ punaḥ sadhānaṃ lābhaviśeṣānubandhā arthānarthānubandhasaṃśayavicārāśceti vaiśikam ||
children.translated_text: For all of them, according to suitability, the men to be approached, the assistants, the winning over of those men, the means of acquiring wealth, dismissal, renewed association with one who again has wealth, the consequences of special gains, and the considerations of consequent profit, harm, and doubt: this is the courtesan's section.
And here there are two verses.
Since men have pleasure as their aim, and women too have pleasure as their aim,
because the purpose of the treatise is chiefly profit, the application here is to women.

children.text: santi rāgaparā nāryaḥ santi cārthaparā api
children.translated_text: There are women intent on passion, and there are also women intent on wealth.

children.text: prāk tatra varṇito rāgo veśyāyogāśca vaiśike ||
children.translated_text: Passion was described earlier; the conjunctures concerning prostitutes are in the courtesan section.
And the <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been explained.

children.text: tatroktaistu vidhibhir abhipretam artham anadhigacchan aupaniṣadikam ācaret
children.translated_text: If, by the methods stated there, he does not obtain the desired object, he should practice the esoteric procedure.
Beauty, good qualities, youth, and generosity are means of making oneself beloved.

The same substances beginning with <s>madayantikā</s> restore it.

children.text: bahupādikākuṣṭhatagaratālīśadevadāruvajrakandakair upaliptaṃ vaṃśaṃ vādayato yā śabdaṃ śṛṇoti sā vaśyā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: A woman who hears the sound of a bamboo flute smeared with <s>bahupādikā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>tālīśa</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>vajrakanda</s> becomes subject to control.
Food mixed with <s>dhattūra</s> fruit causes madness.
Jaggery, and the digested remedy, bring restoration.

children.text: haritālamanaḥśilābhakṣiṇo mayūrasya purīṣeṇa liptahasto yad dravyaṃ spṛśati tan na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: When a hand is smeared with the dung of a peacock that has eaten orpiment and realgar, whatever object it touches is not seen.

children.text: aṅgāratṛṇabhasmanā tailena vimiśram udakaṃ kṣīravarṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Water mixed with oil and the ash of charcoal and grass becomes milk-colored.

children.text: harītakyāmrātakayoḥ śravaṇapriyaṃgukābhiśca piṣṭābhir liptāni lohabhāṇḍāni tāmrībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Iron vessels smeared with ground <s>harītakī</s>, <s>āmrātaka</s>, <s>śravaṇa</s>, and <s>priyaṅgukā</s> become copper-colored.

children.text: śravaṇapriyaṃgukātailena dukūlasarpanirmokeṇa vartyā dīpaṃ prajvālya pārśve dīrghīkṛtāni kāṣṭhāni sarpavad dṛśyante ||
children.translated_text: If a lamp is lit with <s>śravaṇa-priyaṅgukā</s> oil and a wick made with silk cloth and a snake's cast-off skin, pieces of wood stretched out nearby appear like snakes.

children.text: śvetāyāḥ śvetavatsāyā goḥ kṣīrasya pānaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam ||
children.translated_text: Drinking the milk of a white cow with a white calf brings fame and long life.
So too do the blessings of esteemed brahmans.
Having examined the earlier śāstras and also approached practical applications,
this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> has been carefully set forth in brief.

children.text: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca pratyayaṃ lokam eva ca
children.translated_text: One who knows the truth of this text sees <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, confidence, and the world itself,

children.text: paśyatyetasya tattvajño na ca rāgāt pravartate ||
children.translated_text: and he does not act from passion.
Those various passion-increasing practices that were stated because of the subject matter
have, immediately after that, been carefully restrained here itself.

children.text: na śāstram astītyetena prayogo hi samīkṣyate
children.translated_text: For a practice is not to be judged merely by saying, 'There is a śāstra for it.'
One should know the meanings of śāstra to be wide-ranging, but practices to be particular.
After thoroughly considering the sūtra topics of <s>Bābhravya</s> and the received tradition,
<s>Vātsyāyana</s> composed this <s>Kāmasūtra</s> according to rule.

children.text: tad etad brahmacaryeṇa pareṇa ca samādhinā
children.translated_text: This was composed with celibacy and the highest concentration,
for the conduct of life in the world; its rule is not intended for passion.
Guarding the proper worldly stability of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>,
one who knows the truth of this śāstra indeed becomes master of his senses.
Therefore the skillful and learned man, observing <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>,
succeeds when he uses this as a lover who is not excessively governed by passion.
